issues.title: Add `localeDetector` option to customize locale detection during Vue component rendering
issues.body: ### Describe the feature #### Background The `nuxt-i18n` module provides a `strategy` option with the following values: * `no_prefix` * `prefix_except_default` * `prefix` * `prefix_and_default` ref: https://i18n.nuxtjs.org/docs/guide The `no_prefix` strategy disables the use of locale prefixes (e.g., `/en`, `/ja`) in the URL. Additionally, `nuxt-i18n` has a feature that automatically detects the locale based on the URL. For example, accessing a URL like `/en/*` will switch the locale to `en`. However, when the `no_prefix` strategy is used, this automatic locale detection based on the pathname is disabled, as the pathname does not contain locale information. ref: https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/blob/25b900a9f5d509ac1081716a3a7d5c1d22edbd71/src/runtime/utils.ts#L247-L249 This behavior seems logical given the absence of locale information in the URL. However, it causes issues when building multilingual documentation sites using `nuxt/content`. ##### Example Use Case: Suppose we have the following markdown files for multilingual content: * `docs/en/about.md` * `docs/ja/about.md` In this case, we want to access `/en/about` and `/ja/about` to display the corresponding localized content. However, since the locale detection from pathname is disabled with `no_prefix`, the locale is not correctly detected based on the URL. As a result, during SSG (Static Site Generation), both `/en/about` and `/ja/about` will be generated using the language setting of the build machine, causing incorrect locale assignments. e.g. https://github.com/odan-sandbox/nuxt-content-and-i18n-no_prefix-example | http://localhost:3000/en/about | http://localhost:3000/ja/about | |-|-| ||| #### Proposed Feature: `localeDetector` Option ##### Current Behavior Example To illustrate the current behavior, consider the following scenario: * Accessing `/en/about` and `/ja/about` under the `no_prefix` strategy will not trigger locale detection based on the pathname. * As a result, both paths will use the language setting of the build machine during SSG, resulting in both paths potentially being generated in the same language. Screenshots and repository links demonstrating the current behavior will be provided to further clarify the issue. To address this issue, I propose adding a new `localeDetector` option to the module configuration. This option allows specifying the methods for locale detection as follows: ```typescript type LocaleDetector = ("pathname" | "domain" | "cookie" | "browser")[]; const localeDetector: LocaleDetector = ["pathname", "domain", "cookie", "browser"]; ``` If `pathname` is specified, the locale will be automatically detected based on the URL pathname. The default value of `localeDetector` will vary depending on the `strategy` value to maintain backward compatibility. For instance, when `no_prefix` is selected, the default value would be: ```javascript localeDetector: ["domain", "cookie", "browser"] ``` ##### Example Configuration for My Use Case: ```javascript strategy: "no_prefix", localeDetector: ["pathname", "cookie", "browser"] ``` This configuration would resolve the issue by enabling locale detection based on pathname while maintaining backward compatibility with existing behavior. Thank you for considering this feature request. I would be happy to provide further clarifications or contribute to the implementation if needed. ### Additional information - [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature? - [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module? ### Final checks - [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution) (The contribution guideline of nuxt-modules/i18n is compliant with Nuxt too). - [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

The detection function specified by `experimental.localeDetector` is only executed for API calls and is not invoked during the rendering of Vue components. Therefore, it does not conflict with the proposed `localeDetector` option.
ref: https://i18n.nuxtjs.org/docs/guide/server-side-translations

Additionally, since `experimental.localeDetector` is intended for server-side translations, it might be more appropriate to rename it to `experimental.serverLocaleDetector` if the proposed `localeDetector` option is adopted.

issues.title: Support complex multi-domain i18n configurations in a single build
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

### Description

Hi there,
I'm working on a Nuxt project that needs to serve multiple countries, each on a separate domain. Each domain has its own i18n requirements:

* Some domains have **only one official language** (e.g., `site.fr` → French only, no prefix needed).
* Others have **multiple languages**, and the strategy varies:

  * Some use `prefix_except_default` (e.g., `site.ca` with `fr` and `en`)
  * Others use `prefix` (e.g., `site.be` with `fr` and `nl`)

### Constraints:

* I want to **use a single Nuxt build** to serve all domains.
* I need to **dynamically adapt the i18n config** (strategy, locales, defaultLocale) based on the current domain (host).
* I also need to **detect the current domain** at runtime (server & client) to configure things like API base URLs.
* Compatible with SSR & SEO

### Problem

Currently, I need to generate and deploy **one build per domain** to accommodate the differences in `strategy`, `defaultLocale`, and available `locales`. That means I must build the app **8 times**, which is time-consuming and hard to maintain.

### Question

Is there currently any **official or recommended way** to support multiple domains with different i18n strategies **using a single build**?

If not, would this be considered a valid feature request, or are there technical constraints that prevent this kind of setup?

Thanks a lot for your help!


### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution) (The contribution guideline of nuxt-modules/i18n is compliant with Nuxt too).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

### Describe the feature

I’d like to configure my application so that a locale like pt-BR uses a human‑friendly prefix instead of the code in URLs.

E.g. `/brazil/about` instead of `/pt-BR/about`.

Ideally, something like this:

```js
locales: [
  {
    code: 'pt-BR',
    file: 'pt-BR.yml',
    language: 'pt-BR',
    prefix: 'brazil'
  }
]
```

That way:

- I don’t need to map every route manually via pages config or macros.
- I can keep my existing locale code value (`pt-BR`) unchanged.
- I can support a custom prefix string (`brazil`) that’s meaningful and SEO‑friendly.

comments.author: BobbieGoede
comments.body:
>I can support a custom prefix string (brazil) that’s meaningful and SEO‑friendly.

I have to note that language tags are more meaningful than a country name on its own, and language tags are the appropriate way to localize URLs if SEO is a priority.

`/pt-br/` => Language tag meaning Portuguese as spoken/written in Brazil
`/brazil/` => Could be a page and is not a valid language tag

comments.body:
Thanks for the reply, @BobbieGoede.

One thing that’s important here is not to mix language with country (and market). In many real-world projects, the URL segment is chosen based on the business market (BR, UK, MX, etc.), not on the actual locale code like `pt-BR` or `en-GB`.

A good example is apple.com: they use country paths (`/br/`, `/pt/`, `/fr/`…), because that’s what makes sense for their global structure, not because the language is different.

That’s why the feature request was about allowing a custom prefix per locale: the app can still use the correct locale internally (`pt-BR`), but expose a business-oriented prefix in the URL (like `/brazil/`).

---

Examples:

- https://www.apple.com/br/
- https://www.nike.com/fr/
- https://www.zara.com/it/

issues.title: Support stricter $t key typing from generated locale schema (no fallback to string)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

When using typedOptionsAndMessages, autocomplete for $t works, but TypeScript still accepts non-existent paths.

Example:

```ts
$t('home.title') // ✅ autocomplete works
$t('foo.bar')    // ❌ should be an error, but TS accepts it
```

Currently, I'm using a workaround with a typed helper:

```ts
// USAGE: $t(r('path'))

import type { DefineLocaleMessage } from 'vue-i18n'

type RemoveIndexSignature<T> = {
  [K in keyof T as string extends K ? never : K]: T[K]
}

type Join<K, P> = K extends string | number
  ? P extends string | number
    ? `${K}.${P}`
    : never
  : never

type DotPaths<T> = T extends object
  ? {
      [K in keyof T & (string | number)]: T[K] extends object
        ? `${K}` | Join<K, DotPaths<T[K]>>
        : `${K}`
    }[keyof T & (string | number)]
  : never

type CleanLocale = RemoveIndexSignature<DefineLocaleMessage>
type LocalePaths = DotPaths<CleanLocale>

export function r<K extends LocalePaths>(key: K): K {
  return key
}
```

…but it would be nice if this strict typing was built-in, for example via a $tr method.

comments.author: CallumPeers
comments.body:
We're hitting this in production (Nuxt 4.5.2, @nuxtjs/i18n 10.4.0, Nitro 2.13.4, Firebase App Hosting / Cloud Run, SWR route rules), roughly 1.7k Sentry events a week at 0.1 sampling. After digging through the request logs I don't think this is about cold cache at all. It's a cold start race, which would also explain why it never reproduces in dev or on a warm server.

Here's one failing request from our Cloud Run logs:

```
15:58:56.250  GET /politicians/<slug>/_payload.json arrives, no instance available, request queued
15:58:56.257  Cloud Run: "Starting new instance. Reason: AUTOSCALING"
15:59:02.5xx  app module init logs (about 6s of bundle evaluation on throttled cold start CPU)
15:59:02.978  "Listening on http://[::]:8080"
15:59:03      the queued request is served milliseconds after listen() and 500s with
              "Nuxt I18n server context has not been set up yet."
              (logged latency 6.51s = queue + boot + handling)
```

We have a second incident on another instance: "Starting new instance" at 14:54:50, then a queued burst of ~15 requests released together. 8 of them 500 with this error, interleaved with 200s in the same seconds, and the same URLs succeed on warm instances moments later. Every occurrence we can find falls within the first seconds of a fresh instance. Warm instances never produce it.

What I think is happening:

1. Nitro doesn't await plugin bodies (`runNitroPlugins`, and the plugins docs mention an async plugin isn't awaited before the server accepts traffic).
2. The i18n server plugin (`runtime/server/plugin.js`) is async and awaits the `nitro:handlers:i18n` cache cleanup before it registers the `request` hook that creates `event.context.nuxtI18n`.
3. On serverless, queued requests are released the moment the port opens, which lands them exactly in that window. Requests that pass `onRequest` before the hook is registered never get a context.
4. When one of those requests reaches the renderer, `render:before` calls `useI18nContext(event)` and throws. `import.meta.prerender` is false in production so the lazy init fallback that exists for prerender doesn't kick in. The error page render reuses the same event, so it throws a second time, which is why the exception shows up doubled.

`_payload.json` dominates the reports simply because client side navigations are usually what wake a scaled-to-zero instance. We see the same error on normal page SSR and even on 404 renders in the same cold start windows.

A fix could be to let `render:before` self-heal the way it already does for prerender:

```js
const ctx = tryUseI18nContext(event) ?? await initializeI18nContext(event)
```

or to register the hooks before any awaited work in the plugin body (though the lazy init also covers requests that entered the pipeline before registration happened).

For anyone else hitting this in the meantime: `experimental: { nitroContextDetection: false }` made the 500s go away for us, since the `render:before` block is the only place that hard-requires the server context. The docs mark that flag as temporary though, so a proper fix would be great.

issues.body:
### Describe the feature

I can see that despite having a few configuration options, the module is opinionated in terms of path preference. In case of the `prefix_and_default` strategy, it consistently prefers a path with no prefix. I don't think this should be the case: the module users should have an option to change this, depending on what drew them to thinking about using this strategy.

I would like to have an option to set the opposite preference, so that specifically:

- When `setLocale` is called, the user is redirected to `/en/foo` rather than `/foo`.

issues.title: Ability to dynamically set proper headers for redirects with the `prefix` strategy
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

I am looking into using the `prefix` strategy with `redirectOn: 'no prefix'` enabled. This, however, causes some headaches on deployment to an environment with proper caching enabled (e.g., Netlify), as proper headers are not set.

Nuxt 4 is smart enough, e.g., to set `netlify-vary` header to `query` automatically for app routes that require it when deploying to Netlify as one of the platforms that are supported out of the box. One would expect that adding this module would not break it, but it does. In this example Netlify with ISR enabled (the recommended way) will cache the first redirect to one of the supported languages. To fix this scenario, the module should set the header to, e.g., `query,cookie=language,language=en|fr` (depending on how the cookie is named and which languages are actually supported).

The fix suggested above is the optimized approach. A much worse option would be to use the regular `vary` header that offers less option and could result in cache pollution, however could still work correctly from the end user's perspective.

Ideally the module should handle each official deployment target of Nuxt on its own. As an alternative, the module could at least provide an option to inject the logic related to setting custom headers to its redirection logic. Actually, it would be nice to have such a possibility anyway in order to handle some specific custom scenarios. Or is there such an option and I somehow missed it when looking for it?

As a side note, simply setting the above header for `/**` in Nuxt's `routeRules` is not a good option either, as in such case it is applied even to resources under `/_nuxt/` and there is no way to disable it for them. So while a similar approach could easily work for `/` with `redirectOn: 'root'`, the `redirectOn: 'no prefix'` option is more challenging.

### Additional information

- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

comments.body:
> If you can back this up with docs/resources then we have to change this.

Well, thank you for inspiring me to do a small research. So here goes a side note regarding this topic, which is based on [Google's guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions) and what Google actually does:

- There is no clear mention of duplicates, and yet the documentation mentions listing actual alternatives rather than providing some hints, hence it implies a notion of uniqueness in an indirect way, and absolutely none of the examples show more than one `link` with the same `href` with `rel="alternate"`, and this matches what Google does itself.
- Contrary to what I previously suggested, Google strongly prefers, e.g., `en` over `en-US` (or `en-us`, how they would usually write it in the examples, although not always). Looking at [an example](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions#example_1) I understand that in case of having, e.g., versions for `en-US` and `en-GB`, where the former one is intended for the global audience (i.e., the default for English-language speakers), I would list them as `en` and `en-gb` correspondingly (and that's it, no duplicates to somehow "target" `en-US`).
- As for `rel="x-default"`, as [explained](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions#xdefault), it was designed for language selector pages and so it will work best with those. Looking again at the above mentioned example, you will not find it, as it is entirely optional. In case of this module, it is well suited for mentioning the path with no prefix that has a redirect when the `prefix` strategy is used. Although the Google's site itself uses `x-default` to point again to the `href` assigned to `en`. This is the only exception where you can find multiple `link` elements that share the same `href`, however notice that there are still no duplicates among `link` elements marked as `rel="alternate"`.

> It's good to get feedback, but I'm not sure what to do with this issue 🤷

My key takeaway is that given the purpose of having the `head` elements and how Nuxt works underneath, it makes the most sense to have the `import.meta.server` guard [as suggested in the Nuxt documentation](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-seo-meta#performance). If not the only option, this should be the default one, regardless of whether `useLocaleHead` or a configuration option is used. Once that's implemented, the main issue that I reported here is gone.

Additionally, as with the duplicate `link` elements, I would like to strongly discourage you from polluting the output by using `id` (worse choice) /`key` (better choice) attributes, which should not be needed at all when modifying `head` only once, on the server side, as IMHO should be in case of `strictSeo`.

It's nice when things happen automatically by themselves, as with the redirect in the `prefix` strategy, or with `strictSeo`, however when you need to make certain tweaks (e.g., add headers for `netlify-vary` in the former case, as I mentioned in [another issue](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/issues/3915), or restrict runtime to server in the latter), and you see that you have no control over how the feature works, there comes a real headache.

In any case, as the module evolves, I hope there will always be an option to handle SEO elements manually like there is now.

issues.title: Launch a performance mode configuration option.
issues.body:
**Subject: Performance Bottlenecks in Large-Scale Nuxt-i18n Projects & Proposal for SSR Optimization**

Our project currently supports 14 languages with over 300 routes. In SSR scenarios, `nuxt-i18n` generates a routes array containing thousands of entries. This leads to extremely slow static analysis and bundling, especially during the Nitro server build phase. Furthermore, with translation files reaching several MBs, CPU usage during page rendering is exceptionally high, resulting in single-digit RPS (Requests Per Second).

We have performed an internal refactor that reduced CPU load by 50% and improved build speeds by 1/3. We implemented on-demand loading, ensuring each page only loads a few KBs of translations. However, our current implementation is an internal hotfix tailored specifically for our `no_prefix` / `no_expect_prefix` strategy, making it difficult to submit as a universal PR. 

We strongly urge the official team to support this mode; otherwise, we will have to reconsider using `nuxt-i18n` for future large-scale projects. (Note: This requirement specifically targets SSR performance).

### Proposed Strategy:

1. **Route Generation Optimization**: 
   Limit route generation to just two paths: the default locale and a regex-based match for other locales, rather than flattening thousands of permutations.

2. **Static Dependency Scanning & Virtual Modules**:
   - During the client build phase, scan all pages and dependencies to extract `_ctx.$t` usages. 
   - Generate a mapping of Page Names to required Translation Keys.
   - Inject this as a virtual module into Nitro.

3. **On-Demand Hydration & Caching**:
   - **Server-side**: Expose an API endpoint to fetch specific translations via `route + locale` during SSR, then inject them into the i18n instance. 
   - **Hydration**: Use `useState` to sync translations to the client.
   - **Client-side Navigation**: When switching routes, use the API endpoint (carrying a build ID or file hash) to fetch the required translations for the new route and cache them permanently in the browser.

issues.title: Auto-discovery of nested locale files with filename-based namespacing
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

**Summary**
Add support for automatic discovery of translation files within locale subdirectories, where directory and file names are automatically mapped to message namespace keys — similar to how Laravel handles translation namespacing.

**Motivation**
As projects grow, storing all translations in a single file per locale (e.g. `en.json`) becomes hard to maintain. The current `files` array partially addresses this, but it requires manually listing every file in `nuxt.config.ts` *and* manually wrapping keys inside each file to avoid collisions. This creates two friction points:

1. Every new translation file must be registered in config
2. Developers must self-enforce a namespacing convention with no guardrails

**Proposed behavior**
When a locale's directory is used as the source (e.g. `langDir: 'locales/'` and a subfolder `locales/en/` exists), the module should automatically:

- Discover all `.json` / `.yaml` / `.ts` files within that subdirectory recursively
- Use the file path relative to the locale folder as the namespace key

For example, given this structure:
```
locales/
└── en/
    ├── errors.json
    ├── alerts.json
    └── checkout/
        └── validation.json
```

The resulting message keys would be:
```
errors.not_found
alerts.success
checkout.validation.required_field
```

No manual registration in `nuxt.config.ts` would be needed beyond pointing to the locale directory.

**Suggested config API**
```ts
i18n: {
  langDir: 'locales/',
  locales: [
    { code: 'en', dir: 'en/' }, // use `dir` instead of `file`/`files` to opt into auto-discovery
    { code: 'fr', dir: 'fr/' },
  ]
}
```

Alternatively, this could be an opt-in flag:
```ts
{ code: 'en', files: 'en/', autoNamespace: true }
```

**Why this improves DX**
- Mirrors a well-established convention from Laravel that many developers are already familiar with
- Eliminates boilerplate config updates whenever a new translation file is added
- Enforces consistent namespacing automatically, reducing key collision bugs
- Scales naturally — teams can split translations by feature, domain, or page without any extra wiring

**Backward compatibility**
This feature would be purely opt-in via the new `dir` key or flag, leaving existing `file`/`files` behavior completely unchanged.

Happy to discuss implementation details or contribute if there's interest. Thanks for the great module!

There is an existing discussion that addresses a similar feature-request. But I wanted to give a more detailed description of the feature.

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

issues.title: Runtime-configurable default locale: single build serving regions with different defaults (prefix_except_default)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

**Summary**

Allow the **default locale to be chosen at runtime** under `strategy: 'prefix_except_default'`, so a single build artifact can serve multiple deployments that each have a different default locale.

Today `defaultLocale` is a build-time decision. The default-locale route tree is generated unprefixed and named per-locale (`<base>___en`), and the runtime name getter (`createLocaleRouteNameGetter`) binds the default locale to that build value. To serve a different default locale you must rebuild. For "one image" deployments — one Docker image, N regional pods, each pod's default locale set from an env var at boot — this forces either N builds or a fork patch.

**Use case**

- A single CI build artifact deployed to multiple regions.
- Each region's default (unprefixed `/`) locale differs and is chosen at runtime (e.g. `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE`).
- Non-default locales stay prefixed (`/de/…`), exactly as `prefix_except_default` works today.
- Pairs naturally with `experimental.compactRoutes` (non-default locales are already one regex route).

**Why it can't fully be a module today (the crux)**

The *build* side can be done from a module: a `pages:resolved` hook can rename the default-locale tree to a **locale-agnostic** name (`<base>___default` instead of `<base>___en`) and widen the compact `:locale(...)` param to include the build default. That part works in userland.

The *runtime* side cannot. `createLocaleRouteNameGetter` (`runtime/routing/utils.ts`) hardcodes, for `prefix_except_default`, `getLocalizedRouteName(name, locale, /* isDefault */ false)` → `<base>___<locale>`. For name-based resolution (`localePath`/`localeRoute`, and the hreflang/canonical link generation built on them) to target the locale-agnostic tree, the default locale must resolve to `<base>___default`. There is no hook or option to influence this runtime getter, so the only way to make it agree with the renamed tree is to **patch `dist/`** — which is fragile across releases.

**Proposed direction**

An opt-in experimental flag (working name `experimental.localeAgnosticDefaultRoutes`) that, under `prefix_except_default`, resolves the default locale to the locale-agnostic `___default` route name in `createLocaleRouteNameGetter` — turning the `dist/` patch into a supported option. A complete feature would additionally:

1. generate the default-locale tree with the `___default` name natively (so no companion module rename is needed), and
2. read the effective default locale from runtime config and let locale detection fall back to it — `getLocaleFromRouteName('<base>___default')` already yields a non-locale `"default"` that fails `isSupportedLocale`, so detection self-heals.

I've opened a small proof-of-concept PR implementing the runtime-getter seam behind the flag, with unit tests — see the linked PR below. It deliberately scopes to the runtime getter (the part that can't be a userland module); happy to extend toward (1)/(2) or reshape the API however you prefer.

**Alternatives considered**

- Build per region — defeats the single-artifact goal (N images, N pipelines).
- `differentDomains` — solves per-domain defaults, not per-deployment runtime defaults of the same build; and requires domain config.
- Patching `dist/` (current workaround) — works, but breaks on every version bump and isn't shareable.

**Prior art / related**

Same "make i18n config runtime-resolvable" theme as #2888 (locales in `runtimeConfig`), #2602 (different domains at runtime), #3748 (multi-domain in a single config), and #3499 (dynamic default language). Runtime default locale for a single-build / multi-region deployment is the unaddressed case.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module? — only partly: the build-time route rename can live in a module, but the runtime name-getter behavior cannot without patching `dist/`. That gap is what this requests.

### Final checks

- [x] Read the contribution guide.
- [x] Checked existing discussions and issues.

comments.author: Togetic
comments.body:
**Update for 10.6.0** — two things in the original write-up are now out of date, and both make the ask *smaller*.

1. **The effective default locale already comes from runtime config.** `src/runtime/plugins/i18n.ts` resolves it per request as `resolveDefaultLocale(useRequestURL({ xForwardedHost: true }).host, runtimeI18n.defaultLocale)`, `runtimeConfig.public.i18n.defaultLocale` is seeded in `module.ts` and therefore overridable at boot (`NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE`), and it flows through `createNuxtI18nContext` → `ctx.getDefaultLocale()` → `createRoutingContext({ defaultLocale })`. `prefixable` then correctly leaves that locale unprefixed. So follow-up item (2) in the original post is essentially already there — nothing to add.

2. **The runtime getter is no longer where I said it hardcodes.** `createLocaleRouteNameGetter` lost its `defaultLocale` parameter and its per-strategy branching; it now takes a `hasRoute` probe and resolves against the generated route table ("the route table is the authority"). It is locale-blind by design, which is a better design — it just means the flag belongs at the call site rather than inside it.

**What's actually left is one mismatch.** With `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE=ja` on a build whose default was `en`, `prefixable` says `ja` is the unprefixed locale, while name-based resolution returns `index___ja` → `/ja`. The route *name* is the only remaining build-bound piece, and a locale-agnostic `<base>___default` is what reconciles the two.

So the request narrows to: **let the unprefixed tree be addressable by a name that carries no locale.** Two halves:

- **runtime** — resolve the host's default locale to `<base>___default`. This is the half that cannot live in a userland module without patching `dist/`; #4017 is rebased and reshaped for the refactor above, with `hasRoute` probing so that enabling it without the build-side rename is a no-op rather than a break.
- **build** — emit that name from `localizeRoutes` instead of `___<defaultLocale>`, so no companion `pages:resolved` rename is needed on the consumer side. On current `main` that's roughly two lines in the `prefix_except_default` branch of `src/routing.ts`, plus widening the compact `:locale(...)` pattern to include the build default (every locale can be the prefixed one on some deployment).

Happy to do both halves in #4017 if a self-contained flag is preferable to a minimal seam — or to drop the flag entirely and shape it some other way if you have a different direction in mind.

comments.author: Togetic
comments.body:
Follow-up 1 is done — the `___default` tree is now generated natively in nuxt-modules/i18n#4017 (`f30d586`), so the flag no longer needs a companion `pages:resolved` rename in userland. Combined with the earlier correction that follow-up 2 was already satisfied on `main`, both halves of the original request are implemented behind one off-by-default option.

It turned out to fall out of the existing machinery rather than needing new concepts: under the flag, `prefix_except_default` produces the same two-variant shape `prefix_and_default` already does — prefixed plus unprefixed — differing only in that the unprefixed variant is named `<base>___default` instead of `<base>___<locale>___default`. Three small changes get there (`resolveDefaultTreeLocales` returns the default locale, `createShouldPrefix` stops exempting it, `localizeRouteName` omits the locale from the default-tree name), plus widening the compact `:locale(…)` pattern to every locale when `compactRoutes` is on.

The one design consequence worth naming here: the build's own default locale has to become **prefixable**. The unprefixed tree now belongs to whichever locale the deployment defaults to, so leaving `en` unprefixed-only would leave it with no reachable route on a deployment defaulting to something else. That is a real behaviour change for the default locale under this strategy — which is why it sits behind an opt-in flag rather than becoming the default, and it's the part I'd most like maintainer input on.

issues.title: feat: support Nuxt 5 and Nitro 3 while retaining Nuxt 4 compatibility
issues.body:
Nuxt 5 moves the server runtime to Nitro 3 and H3 v2. The i18n server runtime still imports Nitro 2 APIs and writes locale redirects through the old Node response, so it cannot run unchanged on Nuxt 5.

I have a small pnpm patch running in a private application, including a deployed preview. It updates those server seams and the application has behaved correctly there.

Could we keep Nuxt 4 and Nuxt 5 support in the same release line? The change I have in mind is deliberately narrow:

- Keep locale handling, detection, and redirect logic shared.
- Generate the tiny Nitro/H3 compatibility layer when the module is set up, so each installed Nuxt version gets imports it can resolve.
- Cover one locale redirect on both version lines, including the status, Location header, and cookie.

Nuxt Image is already moving to the Nitro 3 API style in https://github.com/nuxt/image/pull/2281. That work is a useful reference, although this proposal would retain Nuxt 4 support too.

If this direction makes sense, I can open one focused PR. If you would rather take it on internally, I hope the boundary above makes the change easy to pick up.

issues.title: `useSetI18nParams`: a page's dynamic params are stamped onto the next route, leaking into pages that never call it
issues.body: ### Environment - `@nuxtjs/i18n`: **10.6.0** (current `latest`) — also reproduces on 10.5.0, and the code below is unchanged on `main` - `nuxt`: 4.5.2 - `vue`: 3.5.41, `vue-router`: 5.2.0 - Node: 24.16.0 - Config: `strategy: 'prefix'`, 7 locales, SSR enabled ### Reproduction I have not attached a StackBlitz — apologies. The mechanism is a specific unguarded write in `_useSetI18nParams` (quoted below with the exact lines), and reproducing it needs only two pages and one client-side navigation. Happy to publish a starter fork if you'd still like one; I did not want to open the issue without the analysis attached. Against the [v10 reproduction starter](https://stackblitz.com/fork/github/BobbieGoede/nuxt-i18n-starter/tree/v10), add two pages: ```vue ``` ```vue ``` 1. Load `/en/article/hello`. 2. Click through to the homepage — **client-side**; a full page load does not reproduce. **Expected** on `/en`: the homepage declared no dynamic params, so `route.meta.nuxtI18nInternal` should be empty — the state a direct load of `/en` produces. **Actual** on `/en`: ``` meta: {"en":{"slug":"hello"},"de":{"slug":"hallo"}} ``` The homepage carries the article's params. `switchLocalePath('de')` still returns `/de` here, because the homepage route has no `:slug` segment for the leftovers to fill — with truthy params the corruption is real but latent. See "Additional context" for where it surfaces. ### Describe the bug `_useSetI18nParams` registers one watcher **per composable instance**, which re-applies *that instance's* params to whatever route is current whenever `fullPath` changes — [`src/runtime/routing/head.ts`](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/blob/main/src/runtime/routing/head.ts): ```ts const unsub = watch( () => router.currentRoute.value.fullPath, () => { router.currentRoute.value.meta[__DYNAMIC_PARAMS_KEY__] = _i18nParams.value ctx.strictSeo && updateState() }, ) if (getCurrentScope()) { onScopeDispose(unsub) } ``` Nothing checks that the params being written describe the route being written to. During a client-side navigation ``'s Suspense keeps the **outgoing** page mounted while the incoming one resolves, so the outgoing page's watcher is still live when the route commits — and it stamps its params onto the incoming route. A page that declares params of its own overwrites them (its instance registers later, so its watcher runs last), which hides this for most routes. **A page that never calls `useSetI18nParams` has nothing to overwrite them with, and inherits the previous page's params.** Nothing removes them afterwards. This is not a race. Keeping the outgoing subtree mounted through the transition is what Suspense is specified to do, so the overlap is guaranteed on every client-side navigation away from a page that sets params. `onScopeDispose` unsubscribes one tick too late by construction. I'm happy to submit a PR if you'd like — see the suggested direction below, but I'd rather agree the shape with you first. ### Additional context **Why it matters.** `switchLocalePath()` and the `rel="alternate"` links both read this meta, so the leak sits on the SEO path. It becomes user-visible with the pattern used for content that exists in only one language — declaring a **falsy** param for the locales a page does not have, which is also what `experimental.strictSeo` keys on (`strictSeo && !params[locale]`) to suppress alternates for unsupported locales: ```js useSetI18nParams({ en: { slug: 'hello' }, de: null, fr: null /* … */ }) ``` Navigate off that page and the destination inherits the `null`s. On a fully-translated page such as the homepage, `switchLocalePath()` then returns `''` for **every** other locale: the language switcher disappears and the alternates are suppressed, on a page unrelated to the article. It recovers on reload, so it only affects real client-side sessions. That combination — a page with no setter, plus params whose falsiness is meaningful — is presumably why this has gone unreported: either half alone masks it. **Suggested direction.** The watcher's *purpose* is sound and should be preserved: params are usually set after an `await` (fetch the localized slugs, then declare them), by which point the route may already have changed, so re-applying makes them stick (rationale in [nuxt/nuxt#28826](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions/28826)). What's missing is any binding between the params and the route they describe: ```ts let paramsRoute = null const i18nParams = computed({ get() { /* unchanged */ }, set(val) { _i18nParams.value = val paramsRoute = router.currentRoute.value.name router.currentRoute.value.meta[__DYNAMIC_PARAMS_KEY__] = val // … }, }) const unsub = watch( () => router.currentRoute.value.fullPath, () => { // Re-apply only to the route these params were set for. Under Suspense the // setter often runs against the outgoing route, so compare on the matched // record rather than the exact path. if (router.currentRoute.value.name !== paramsRoute) { return } router.currentRoute.value.meta[__DYNAMIC_PARAMS_KEY__] = _i18nParams.value ctx.strictSeo && updateState() }, ) ``` Storing params per route record (e.g. a `WeakMap` keyed by the matched record) rather than on the shared merged `meta` would address the same thing more thoroughly, and would stop the value outliving the page that wrote it. If the intended contract is that every page manages its own params, that's a fair answer too — it would just be worth stating in the docs, since pages that never opt into the feature are currently affected by it. **Workaround**, for anyone else hitting this: wrap the composable so each page registers as the owner of its params while mounted, and clear leftovers on `page:finish` when nothing claims them. `page:finish` is the useful hook — it lands after every page-scoped watcher for the navigation *and* after the incoming page has settled. Clearing from the landing page's own `setup()` does not work (under Suspense that runs against the outgoing route and is then overwritten), and neither does an app-level clearing instance (it registers first, so the outgoing page's watcher wins).

Opened #4132 with a fix.

While preparing it I found that this behaviour is currently **covered by a test** — `restores dynamic params after navigation` in `test/routing-head.test.ts` sets params on `/products/big-chair`, pushes `/`, and asserts the product's params are on the index route. So what I reported is, as the suite stands, asserted behaviour. Worth flagging plainly in case that was intentional and I've misread the design.

I think the test is protecting something real but overreaching. Every navigation builds a fresh merged `meta`, so params genuinely are lost on navigation and something has to re-apply them — that part is necessary. What isn't is re-applying them to a *different* route. The PR splits the test accordingly: same-route restore keeps passing, cross-route inheritance now fails.

Instrumenting the composable across four scenarios on 10.6.0 (Nuxt 4.5.2), with `set()`/watcher logging:

| Scenario | Watcher | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Direct load of the page that sets params | never fires | `set()` alone is sufficient |
| Nav → page **with** its own setter | never fires | incoming page's `set()` applies its params |
| Nav → page **without** a setter | fires, `meta undefined → article params` | **the defect** |
| Same-record param change (`/a` → `/b`) | never fires | `setup()` re-runs, fresh `set()` |

In every case the setter ran with `router.currentRoute` already on its own route, so the direct write covered it. The only cross-route write the watcher made was the bug.

That's also the limit of what I can claim: I couldn't find what the unguarded re-apply was originally for. The one case the PR changes is params set *before* their route commits — `_i18nParamsRoute` would hold the previous route and the re-apply would be skipped. I couldn't produce that on Nuxt 4.5.2, but I can't rule it out for older Nuxt, `keepalive`, or a custom `<NuxtPage>` key where the component is reused. issues.title: NuxtConfig['i18n'] is typed via a type alias, so it cannot be augmented by other modules
issues.body:
`NuxtConfig['i18n']` is declared through a type alias, so other modules cannot augment it.

`dist/module.d.mts`:

```ts
type UserNuxtI18nOptions = Omit<NuxtI18nOptions, 'locales'> & { locales?: ... }

interface ModuleOptions extends UserNuxtI18nOptions {}   // augmentable

declare module '@nuxt/schema' {
  interface NuxtConfig {
    ['i18n']?: Partial<UserNuxtI18nOptions>   // but this uses the alias
  }
}
```

`ModuleOptions` is an interface and can be augmented, but the config key is typed via the alias, so an augmentation never reaches it:

```
error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties,
and 'glossary' does not exist in type 'Partial<UserNuxtI18nOptions>'.
```

(Nuxt 4.4.2, `@nuxtjs/i18n` 10.2.3, checked against Nuxt's generated `.nuxt/tsconfig.node.json`. Unknown keys survive normalisation at runtime — only the types reject them.)

**Suggested fix:** declare the key in terms of the interface.

```ts
['i18n']?: Partial<ModuleOptions>
```

That keeps the public type identical while letting companion modules add their own keys under `i18n` via standard declaration merging.

| **Nuxt version**     | `4.4.8`                                                                                                          |
| **Nitro version**    | `2.13.4`                                                                                                         |
| **Builder**          | `vite@7.3.5`                                                                                                     |
| **Config**           | `app`, `compatibilityDate`, `css`, `devtools`, `fonts`, `i18n`, `icon`, `modules`, `schemaOrg`, `site`, `vite`   |
| **Modules**          | `@nuxt/fonts@0.14.0`, `@nuxt/icon@2.2.3`, `@nuxt/image@2.0.0`, `@nuxtjs/i18n@10.4.0`, `@nuxtjs/seo@5.3.0`        |


### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/bobbiegoede-nuxt-i18n-starter-j7iqccls

### Describe the bug

When using detectBrowserLanguage, for example:
```ts
detectBrowserLanguage: {
    useCookie: false,
  },
}
```

And dynamically rendering components/templates based on `useI18n().locale` (see reproduction example):

In a static pre-rendered site, if your browser language is NL and you load the EN site, you get "redirected" client-side to your language NL. In this case, strings translated using `$t()` get correctly re-rendered from EN to NL, but components/templates conditionally rendered do not get re-rendered, they stay in EN.
A `Hydration completed but contains mismatches.` error is logged. Logging `useI18n().locale.value` shows it correctly switched from EN to NL. But the DOM was not updated.

Manually toggling the language using the language selector gets the dynamic components/templates to re-render.

**Workaround**

For now, I disabled `detectBrowserLanguage: false`, and in app.vue, I added:

```ts
import { findBrowserLocale } from '#i18n-kit/browser'
import { normalizedLocales } from '#build/i18n-options.mjs'
import type { Locale } from 'vue-i18n'

const { locale, setLocale } = useI18n()
onMounted(() => {
  const wantedLocale = findBrowserLocale(normalizedLocales, navigator.languages) as Locale

  if (locale.value !== wantedLocale) {
    setLocale(wantedLocale)
  }
})
```

This workaround likely works because setLocale is executed "later" and Vue properly re-renders the DOM, whereas the built-in language detection must have some kind of race condition where the locale is updated after the DOM had a chance to re-render.

### Additional context

The error happens only on static sites where the "redirect" for language detection is client-side. Therefore, for the reproduction to work, you might need to manually generate it and start it
```
nuxt generate
npx serve .output/public
```


### Logs

```shell
Hydration completed but contains mismatches.
```

issues.title: initializeI18nContext runs on every request and response times at our ingress go from ~50 ms to 250–500 ms
issues.body:
### Environment


│ │  Node.js version       v22.17.0                                │
│ │  nuxt/cli version      3.37.0                                  │
│ │  Package manager       pnpm 9.15.9                             │
│ │  Nuxt version          4.5.2                                   │
│ │  Nitro version         2.13.4                                  │
│ │  Builder               vite 8.2.1                              │
│ │  Config                -                                       │
│ │  Modules               - 

### Reproduction

every repo

### Describe the bug

Context: we upgraded a Nuxt 3.15 monorepo to Nuxt 4.5.2 / @nuxtjs/i18n 10.6.0 and saw response times at our ingress go
from ~50 ms to 250–500 ms, with pods saturating on CPU. We serve static assets from the Node pods themselves
(node-server preset, no CDN in front), so every /_nuxt/*.js chunk request goes through the Nitro request pipeline.

Profiling the production build under load (node --cpu-prof, requests for a single 442-byte JS chunk, 20 concurrent
keep-alive connections) showed this stack:

getEnv
← applyEnv
← useRuntimeConfig
← useRuntimeI18n
← initializeI18nContext
← nitro hook "request"

Sample distribution in that profile:

┌──────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ function │ % of samples │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ getEnv │ 8.9 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ kebabCase │ 2.1 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ snakeCase │ 1.7 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ splitByCase │ 1.1 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ deepCopy │ 1.1 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ applyEnv + klona │ 1.2 % │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ total │ 16.5 % (≈ half of all non-idle CPU) │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘

That's useRuntimeI18n(undefined, event) → useRuntimeConfig(event), which clones the whole runtime config and walks
every key through splitByCase/kebabCase/snakeCase looking for process.env overrides — once per request, including
requests that will never touch i18n.

Measured impact, same build, only difference being a guard on the request hook:

┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────┐
│ │ rps │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
│ 10.6.0 as-is │ ~2065 │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
│ 10.6.0 with the request hook skipping buildAssetsDir │ ~8290 │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
│ (our previous stack, Nuxt 3.15.4 + i18n 9.5.6, for reference) │ ~9060 │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘

The guard we tested:

const { buildAssetsDir } = useRuntimeConfig().app // resolved once at plugin setup

nitro.hooks.hook('request', async (event) => {
if (event.path.startsWith(buildAssetsDir)) return
await initializeI18nContext(event)
})

Static asset 404s still return 404 (Nitro throws those before the renderer, so render:before never runs and
useI18nContext is never reached), and SSR requests are untouched.

Worth noting our results don't contradict yours — they're complementary. We run 2–3 locales, and createLocaleConfigs
didn't appear in our profile at all, which lines up with your benchmark showing the win scaling with locale count.

_No response_

```shell

```

issues.title: SSR: runtime plugins resolve a concurrent request's Nuxt app via useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id) → "Cannot redefine property: $i18n"
issues.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: Cloudflare Workers (`cloudflare_module` Nitro preset), also reproducible with plain `@vue/server-renderer` in Node 24
- Node Version: v24.18.0 (build), workerd (runtime)
- Nuxt Version: 4.5.2
- Nitro Version: 2.13.4
- Package Manager: npm
- Builder: vite
- User Config: `modules: ['@nuxtjs/i18n']`, `i18n: { strategy: 'prefix_except_default', defaultLocale: 'nl', customRoutes: 'config', detectBrowserLanguage: false }`, `experimental.asyncContext` left at its default
- @nuxtjs/i18n: 10.6.0 (the published `dist` for the current `main` has the same code)

### Reproduction

Two concurrent SSR requests in the same isolate, one of which renders a page whose `<script setup>` has a top-level `await` (e.g. `await useAsyncData(...)`). The plugin phase of the second request occasionally throws:

```
TypeError: Cannot redefine property: $i18n
    at setup (node_modules/@nuxtjs/i18n/dist/runtime/plugins/i18n.js:107)
    at callWithNuxt / callAsync / runWithContext / applyPlugin
```

The line that throws is `Object.defineProperty(nuxt, "$i18n", { get: ... })`, where `nuxt` comes from `const nuxt = useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id)` at the top of `setup(_nuxt)` (introduced in #3690).

Minimal standalone reproduction of the underlying leak (no Nuxt needed), run with `node repro.mjs` next to a `node_modules` containing `vue` 3.5.42:

```js
import { createSSRApp, h, withAsyncContext, getCurrentInstance, hasInjectionContext } from 'vue'
import { renderToString } from '@vue/server-renderer'

// Request A: page whose <script setup> has a top-level await (compiled form).
let resolveA; const dataA = new Promise(r => resolveA = r)
const appA = createSSRApp({
  async setup() {
    let __temp, __restore
    ;([__temp, __restore] = withAsyncContext(() => dataA)), await __temp, __restore()
    return () => h('div', 'A')
  }
})
appA.$nuxt = 'NUXT_APP_A'
const renderA = renderToString(appA)

// Request B, mid-plugin-phase: what Nuxt's tryUseNuxtApp does inside vueApp.runWithContext.
const appB = createSSRApp({ render: () => h('div', 'B') }); appB.$nuxt = 'NUXT_APP_B'
const tryUseNuxtApp = () => hasInjectionContext() ? (getCurrentInstance()?.appContext.app.$nuxt ?? '(unctx fallback)') : '(no ctx)'

await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5))
resolveA() // A's data resolves; B's pending plugin continuations sit in the same microtask queue
for (let hops = 0; hops <= 3; hops++) {
  let p = Promise.resolve(); for (let i = 0; i < hops; i++) p = p.then(() => {})
  p.then(() => console.log(`microtask depth ${hops}: B's plugin sees`, appB.runWithContext(tryUseNuxtApp)))
}
await renderA; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5))
```

Output:

```
microtask depth 0: B's plugin sees (unctx fallback)
microtask depth 1: B's plugin sees NUXT_APP_A
microtask depth 2: B's plugin sees (unctx fallback)
microtask depth 3: B's plugin sees (unctx fallback)
```

### Describe the bug

Every runtime plugin in this module resolves the Nuxt app with `useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id)` instead of using the `_nuxt` argument it was handed. Nuxt's `tryUseNuxtApp` (nuxt 4.5.2, `app/nuxt.js`) tries `getCurrentInstance()?.appContext.app.$nuxt` **before** consulting the unctx context, and the `id` argument only affects the latter.

Vue's `withAsyncContext` (what a top-level `await` in `<script setup>` compiles to) restores the component as the global current instance when the awaited promise resolves and only unsets it again via `Promise.resolve().then(cleanup)`, one microtask later. On a server that handles concurrent requests in one isolate (Cloudflare Workers, but any Node SSR server too), a second request whose plugin phase runs inside that microtask gets the *first* request's component from `getCurrentInstance()`, and therefore the first request's Nuxt app from `useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id)`.

In `i18n:plugin` that app already has `$i18n` defined (non-configurable getter), so `Object.defineProperty` throws and the request 500s. In the other plugins (`route-locale-detect`, `switch-locale-path-ssr`, `preload`, `ssg-detect`, `dev`) the same lookup silently attaches state to the wrong request's app.

`experimental.asyncContext` does not help: it only changes the unctx fallback, and the leaking path runs first.

#3690 ("reuse nuxt instance at plugin setup") changed `useNuxtApp()` to `useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id)` to fix the multi-app/Storybook case, which is the unctx branch; it did not touch the `getCurrentInstance()` branch.

### Suggested fix

In every `defineNuxtPlugin({ setup(_nuxt) { ... } })` of the runtime, use the argument directly:

```diff
-    const nuxt = useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id);
+    const nuxt = _nuxt;
```

The plugin is always invoked with the app it should configure, so the lookup is redundant. We are running this as a `patch-package` patch against 10.6.0 in production and it removes the error.

### Additional context

Nuxt could also harden `tryUseNuxtApp` against this (e.g. prefer the unctx context on the server, or verify the instance belongs to the current app), but the module should not depend on that.

### Logs

```
TypeError Cannot redefine property: $i18n
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:430921 setup
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:101220 <anonymous>
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:101917 callWithNuxt
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/nitro/nitro.mjs:1:107074 Object.callAsync
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:101981 <anonymous>
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/nitro/nitro.mjs:1:210566 Object.runWithContext
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:101960 callWithNuxt
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:509137 Object.runWithContext
    .worker-bundle/.../.output/server/chunks/virtual/entry.mjs:1:101201 run
```

comments.author: TheMeinerLP
comments.body:
We hit the same error in production and found a second trigger, one that makes the failure **persistent per isolate** rather than a one-off race. It adds weight to the suggested fix (`const nuxt = _nuxt`), which covers both.

**Setup:**
- Nuxt 4.4.8, Nitro 2.13.4, `cloudflare_module`
- @nuxtjs/i18n 10.6.0, `strategy: 'prefix'`
- Vue 3.5.42 and 3.5.43 (both affected)
- Cloudflare Workers **Free** plan, which allows 10 ms CPU per request

**What happens:**
1. A server render takes more than 10 ms CPU, and Cloudflare terminates the request midway with error 1102.
2. The termination happens during the synchronous render, so Vue's module-global current instance is never unset.
3. From then on, every request that isolate handles gets the dead request's app from `useNuxtApp(_nuxt._id)`, via the `getCurrentInstance()` branch described above, and throws `Cannot redefine property: $i18n`. This includes strictly sequential requests, until Cloudflare recycles the isolate.

**Numbers from the Workers preview of our `main`, 100 requests at concurrency 5:**
- 4 × 503 `error code: 1102`, followed by 30 × 500 `Cannot redefine property: $i18n`.
- Ten sequential requests afterwards all returned 500.
- Production answered 40–60 % of all requests with this error.

**What we checked:**
- `wrangler dev` enforces no CPU limit, and there we saw 0 failures in 1,000 requests at concurrency 100.
- After moving the account to Workers Paid (30 s CPU default), production passes the same load with 0 errors and no cross-request state (`<html lang>`, title, canonical and JSON-LD all match the requested route).

So the lookup can be hit two ways: by the microtask window in `withAsyncContext` shown in the issue, and by any runtime that can abort a request mid-render and then reuse the isolate. Using the plugin's own `_nuxt` argument removes the dependency on either.

issues.body:
Upgrading from v9.5.6 to v10.6.0, we encounter some undocumented breaking changes (not seen on [Migrating](https://i18n.nuxtjs.org/docs/guide/migrating)).

Here is a small one: `meta.content` type has changed from `string | undefined` to `string | number`.

That causes us a TypeScript error when assigning `meta.content` like so:

```
<template v-for="meta in head.meta" :key="meta.id">
  <Meta :id="meta.id" :property="meta.property" :content="meta.content" />
</template>
```
with:
```
const head = useLocaleHead()
```
The meta `content` attribute only accepts `string | undefined`, not `number`.

Workaround: call `.toString()` on `content`.

It seems previously `I18nHeadMetaInfo` `meta`  was `Record<string, string>[]`, while it is now `PropertyMeta[]` with:
```
interface PropertyMeta extends MetaBase {
    /**
     * The property attribute is used to define a property associated with the content attribute.
     * Mainly used for og and twitter meta tags.
     */
    'property': MetaProperties | (string & Record<never, never>);
    /**
     * This attribute contains the value for the property attribute.
     *
     * @see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-content
     */
    'content': string | number;
    'name'?: never;
    'http-equiv'?: never;
    'charset'?: never;
}
```

But maybe this kind of breaking change is "too small" for being documented.

issues.body:
### Environment

### Environment

Operating System: Darwin 25.6.0
Node Version:     v24.18.0
Package Manager:  pnpm@11.17.0
Nuxt Version:     4.5.2
Nitro Version:    2.13.4
Vite Version:     8.2.2
@nuxtjs/i18n:     10.6.0
Builder:          vite

### Reproduction

https://github.com/raminjafary/nuxt-i18n-preload-frozen-repro

pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm preview, then request /, /en and /en/about.

### Describe the bug

With i18n.experimental.preload enabled, an SSR request that loads a locale a second time logs a TypeError from deepCopy. Two locales and a locale-prefixed route are enough; nothing else in the config matters, and experimental.preload: false gives zero warnings.

https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/pull/4071 hands the cached message tree out by reference and freezes it so a stray mutation surfaces rather than leaking across requests. ctx.messages, which only feeds the preload payload, still merges into whatever is already in the slot with deepCopy. On the server the preload plugin fills ctx.messages from vueI18n.global.messages, so those entries are the frozen cached trees — and the next ctx.loadMessages() in the same request (loadAndSetLocale on a prefixed route, or a setLocale) writes into one.

Pages still render translated, because the preload pass has already installed every locale, so the throw only aborts a redundant re-merge.

### Additional context

Introduced in 10.6.0 by https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/pull/4071. Still present on main — nothing since the tag touches plugins/preload.ts, server/context.ts or server/utils/cache.ts.

issues.title: `useHead` does not resolve reactive input on the client
issues.body:
### 🐛 The bug

The module's `useHead` replacement (`src/runtime/composables/head.ts`) never resolves reactive input. All of its `activeHead.push()` / `patch()` sites hand the raw object to unhead, while `@unhead/vue`'s own `clientUseHead` runs `walkResolver(input, VueResolver)` inside a `watchEffect`.

This only bites on the client: `@unhead/vue/server` creates the head with `propResolvers: [VueResolver]`, so refs resolve inside unhead during SSR. The client head has no prop resolver, so resolution exists *only* in the composable this module replaces.

Two consequences:

1. **Crash** — a ref on `innerHTML`/`textContent` of a `style`/`script` reaches unhead's `normalizeProps`, which JSON-stringifies object values:

   ```
   TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
       --> starting at object with constructor 'ComputedRefImpl'
       |     property 'dep' -> object with constructor 'Dep'
       --- property 'computed' closes the circle
       at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
       at normalizeProps (unhead.js:148:28)
       at normalizeTag (unhead.js:175:15)
       at normalizeEntryToTags (unhead.js:209:56)
       at resolveTags (unhead.js:362:16)
       at _renderDOMHead (unhead.js:183:21)
   ```

   It is thrown inside the debounced `_renderDOMHead`, so the whole head render is abandoned: the tag never lands in the DOM, and it can abort router start.

2. **Silent, for every other prop**: the ref object is used instead of its `.value`, and since there is no `watchEffect`, the tag never updates when the ref changes. Client-side reactive head does not work, though unhead v3 documents it as supported.

`@nuxt/ui` triggers case 1 out of the box: its colors plugin calls `useHead({ style: [{ innerHTML: root, id: 'nuxt-ui-colors' }] })` where `root` is a `computed`. Any `@nuxtjs/ionic` + `@nuxt/ui` app loses its theme colors style. `@nuxtjs/i18n`'s `useLocaleHead()` and `@nuxtjs/seo` hit case 2.

### 🛠️ To reproduce

https://github.com/Carpediem94/nuxt-ionic-head-repro

### 🌈 Expected behaviour

Reactive input resolved before being pushed to unhead, and kept in sync as it changes, matching the behaviour of `@unhead/vue`'s `useHead`.

### ℹ️ Additional context

### 📚 Is your documentation request related to a problem?

I personally would like to know what are the motivations behind this package, and what are the known limitations or limitations you have been thinking about. It seems quite obvious to me that the goal behind nuxt with ionic allows cross platform development with one codebase and still get the advantages of nuxt. To my understanding, just like with next.js in react world, people are mainly using nuxt for the developer experience and SSR/SSG for SEO performance. Correct me if I'm wrong, but SSR shines for unpredictable data (e.g. user generated data) and SSG shines for stable data. One of my main concern is: do SSR and SSG work in this package? There is this [package](https://github.com/mlynch/nextjs-tailwind-ionic-capacitor-starter) in next world, but they say SSR doesn't work out of the box.

Lastly, are there any other undocumented known limitations? 

Knowing and documenting those two points could help other developers have a sense of a kind of roadmap and contribute more easily perhaps.

issues.title: feat: Allow using the layouts folder to customize the app root instead of app.vue
issues.body:
### 🆒 Your use case

When creating a multi platform project (e.g. with web, electron, and ionic), I need to use completely different layouts depending on the project. I do this by changing the [layouts dir](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/configuration/nuxt-config#layouts) in my nuxt config depending on the platform I'm building for.

It seems as though you can only customize the root ionic app with the `app.vue` file. Since the path can't be configured, it breaks the ability to change the app root on a per platform basis. This is because nuxt seems to ignore the layouts folder entirely if there's an `app.vue` file in the root folder.

### 🆕 The solution you'd like

If a default layout is found, use that instead of the default `app.vue` file. Or alternatively, use a layout file called `ionic.vue`. 

Another simple solution would be to allow configuring where nuxt ionic looks for the app.vue file. In this case I could point directly to my app index file:

```js
// Ionic nuxt config...
ionic: {
    appIndex: 'layouts/mobile/default.vue'
}
```


### 🔍 Alternatives you've considered

I couldn't find any info on the docs on how to accomplish this: [https://ionic.nuxtjs.org/cookbook/customising-app-vue](https://ionic.nuxtjs.org/cookbook/customising-app-vue)

### ℹ️ Additional info

comments.author: nWacky
comments.body:
I was having the same issue

Ionic's documentation suggests redirecting from `/` to `/home` when home tab location is `/home`.

Example from [Usage with Router - ionicframework.com](https://ionicframework.com/docs/api/tabs#usage-with-router):

```ts
// src/router.ts

const routes: Array<RouteRecordRaw> = [
    { path: '/', redirect: '/home', },
    {
      path: '/',
      component: Tabs,
      children: [
        { path: '', redirect: '/home', },
        { path: 'home', component: () => import('./views/HomePage.vue'), },
    }
]
```

What helped me is creating `pages/index.vue` and using `redirect` in `definePageMeta` to redirect to the home tab: 

```vue
<!-- pages/index.vue -->
<script lang="ts" setup>
definePageMeta({
  redirect: "/tabs/home",
});
</script>
```

```vue
<!-- pages/tabs/home/index.vue -->
<script lang="ts" setup>
definePageMeta({
  alias: ["/tabs"],
});
</script>
```

This way navigating to `/` redirects to `/tabs/home`, and Home tab is correctly shown as active on initial route

issues.title: [feature] add support for MCP spec version `2026-07-28`
issues.body:
### Description

The `nuxt-mcp-toolkit` package currently targets earlier iterations of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification. Projects relying on this toolkit are unable to upgrade their MCP servers to the  [`2026-07-28`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/learn/versioning) spec version until native support is provided.

### Proposed Solution

Add official support for the `2026-07-28` Model Context Protocol spec version. 

This should include:
- Updating internal `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` dependencies to versions compatible with the `2026-07-28` release.
- Supporting key features and standards introduced in the `2026-07-28` specification:

issues.title: Discussion Starter: Enhancing DX
issues.body:
Hello!

Since I work a lot with Medusa projects and I love working with Nuxt, I've been spending some time thinking about how we could further enhance the developer experience with the module, and I wanted to share some personal observations and ideas to kickstart a discussion within the community.

In my experience, I've found that I often write repetitive boilerplate for common operations. For instance, tasks like fetching product lists with specific criteria, managing the full shopping cart lifecycle, or handling user authentication states seem to be areas where we could potentially simplify things further.

My idea is that perhaps we can build higher-level abstractions to make these common tasks even more intuitive.

Based on these thoughts, I'd like to propose for discussion the idea of enhancing `@nuxtjs/medusa` with a suite of more granular, task-specific composables and utilities. These are just initial suggestions to get the conversation going, and I'm eager to hear other perspectives. Some examples are:

- `useMedusaProducts(options?: ProductListOptions`): Could this simplify reactive fetching of product lists, handling pagination, sorting, filtering, and state (data, loading, error)?

- `useMedusaProduct(id: string)`: For fetching and managing a single product's state.

- `useMedusaCollections(options?: CollectionListOptions)`: Similar to products, but for collections.

- `useMedusaRegions()`: To easily fetch and manage available regions.

Maybe we could do the same with the cart lifecycle, authentication, etc.

Of course, developers can build these abstractions themselves on top of `useMedusaClient`. The discussion point here is whether incorporating standardized versions into the module itself would offer greater community benefits or we should leave it as it is.

My main goal here is to foster a collaborative discussion. I believe that by sharing our experiences and ideas, we can collectively shape the future direction of @nuxtjs/medusa to make it more powerful and enjoyable to use.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts and opinions!

issues.title: Fonts 404 during prerender with @nuxt/fonts v1
issues.body:
Hey 👋 I was testing the next major of `@nuxt/fonts` (currently on `main`, installed from `https://pkg.pr.new/@nuxt/fonts@20223b7`) on the Nuxt UI docs, and OG images lose their fonts at prerender.

In Vite builds, fonts v1 now emits fonts as build assets under `buildAssetsDir` (nuxt/fonts#918). Global font faces now point at `/_nuxt/fonts/<hash>.woff2` instead of `/_fonts/<hash>.woff2`. Every render during `nuxt build` then logs:

```
[@nuxtjs/og-image] WARN Failed to load font Public Sans: [GET] "/_nuxt/fonts/kLYc5-...woff2": 404 Server Error
```

The files do end up in `.output/public/_nuxt/fonts/`. From what I can tell, `FONTS_URL_PREFIX` is hardcoded to `/_fonts`, and the `dev-prerender` font binding only resolves `/_fonts/*` (from `.output/public/_fonts` or the persisted `font-urls.json` mapping). Anything else falls through to `fetchWithEvent`, which 404s during prerender.

Repro: `nuxt-og-image@6.8.0` with the takumi renderer, families declared in `fonts.families` with `global: true`, then `nuxt build`. `main` (6.9.0) still only resolves `/_fonts/*` in the prerender binding, so it should hit the same thing. Dev is fine since fonts v1 still serves from `/_fonts` there.

Maybe reading `assetsBaseURL` from the `fonts:public-asset-context` context instead of the constant would be enough? `renderedFontURLs` should still be keyed by the same filename.

issues.title: optimizeDeps.include entry '@plausible-analytics/tracker' cannot be resolved under pnpm's default layout
issues.body:
### Environment

`@nuxtjs/plausible` 4.0.0, Nuxt 4.6.0, Vite 8.3.2, pnpm 11.14.0 with its default isolated `node_modules` (no hoisting).

### Reproduction

Any pnpm project with `@nuxtjs/plausible` in `modules`. Every `nuxt dev` start prints:

```
WARN  [NUXT_B7002] Some vite.optimizeDeps.include entries could not be resolved: @plausible-analytics/tracker.
╰▶ fix: Remove or correct these entries in the vite.optimizeDeps.include array of your nuxt.config.ts. Report entries added by a Nuxt module to the module author.
```

### What happens

The module pushes the bare id `@plausible-analytics/tracker` into `vite.optimizeDeps.include` (`src/module.ts`, added in #47). Vite resolves `include` entries from the project root. Under pnpm the tracker is only a dependency of `@nuxtjs/plausible` and does not appear in the root `node_modules`, so the entry cannot be resolved there:

```
$ node -e "require.resolve('@plausible-analytics/tracker')"   # from the project root
Error: Cannot find module '@plausible-analytics/tracker'
```

The entry therefore pre-bundles nothing in this setup. The dev server still optimizes the tracker, but only because Vite discovers the import in `runtime/plugin.client.js` at runtime.

### What we tried

Rewriting the entry to Vite's nested form, `'@nuxtjs/plausible > @plausible-analytics/tracker'`, resolves. The warning disappears and the tracker is pre-bundled at startup. Vite still discovers the bare import from the runtime plugin as well, though, and bundles the same `plausible.js` a second time under `@plausible-analytics/tracker`, so the optimized deps end up with two copies of the tracker. The nested form silences the warning but is not a clean fix.

Nuxt 4.6 also scans plugin files that live in `node_modules` before optimizing (`installedScanEntries` in `@nuxt/vite-builder`), which may cover the dev-server side of what #47 addressed. We did not test the Vitest case from #47, so we leave the choice between dropping the entry, nesting it, or something else to you.

issues.title: Difference in resources loaded on client when having visual editing configured
issues.body:
As per request from @rdunk in https://github.com/nuxt-modules/sanity/pull/1023, here's more info on what I've found in relation to resources loaded when having visual editing configured.

Wasn't sure what to label this as, not really a bug and not really a feature request 😅 

I might be totally off here and just looking at this from the wrong angle, but to me, it looks like that when having `visualEditing` section configured in the `nuxt.config.ts`, the page will load with quite a lot more resources.

What I did is create a blank Nuxt project with this module and set up a page that loads a document from Sanity. That page is using the `useSanityQuery`. In my Nuxt config, I'm just toggling the visualEditing section on/off, running a build and then opening the page with `nuxi preview`. I have not gone into Sanity Studio (not even running it) and the Presentation tool. I am just loading this page as any regular non-editor user would.

#### With visual editing configured
```javascript
sanity: {
    projectId: process.env.SANITY_PROJECT_ID,
    dataset: process.env.SANITY_DATASET,
    minimal: false,
    useCdn: true,
    apiVersion: '2024-05-30',
    visualEditing: {
      token: '<token here>',
      studioUrl: 'http://localhost:3333',
    },
  },
```
Results in
![loaded with visual editing](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/sanity/assets/5323483/90970e52-2b07-4239-9ece-9a3835f1d7c8)


#### Without visual editing configured
```javascript
sanity: {
    projectId: process.env.SANITY_PROJECT_ID,
    dataset: process.env.SANITY_DATASET,
    minimal: false,
    useCdn: true,
    apiVersion: '2024-05-30',
  },
```
Results in
![loaded without visual editing](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/sanity/assets/5323483/28188c6c-07ee-4e5b-b735-bf15de571782)

What I think this stems from is the way the module is set up. We are checking the visual editing config in build time and swapping out the client composables with those meant for visual editing. These composables import additional dependencies and therefore will cause more resources to be loaded on the client no matter if you're actually using visual editing at the moment or not.

The best scenario would be if we'd only load the additional resources when visual editing has been enabled. Only way to achieve this currently, is to deploy two versions of the same site. One "public production build" for all normal traffic where visual editing config is removed, and one "editing production build" that Sanity Studio would connect to and has the visual editing config set up.

In addition, if we can figure out a way to load the visual editing stuff conditionally, it would open up for further optimisation by allowing us to use the "minimal client" (`minimal: true`) when a user is not currently using visual editing.

As a comparison, using the minimal client results in these resources being loaded
![loaded with minimal client](https://github.com/nuxt-modules/sanity/assets/5323483/95989abc-003c-4ed0-bf24-2a58afd92888)

comments.body:
My comment above detailing my workaround still had one small corner case where async data was not being updated, and doing some more debugging I discovered that in my case, the key to reproducing the issue was to enable ISR on the route where useSanityQuery was failing to refresh data. When ISR was enabled, it failed to fetch updated data when parameters changed, when ISR was disabled it worked as expected.

This led me to finding [this comment](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/34192#issuecomment-3806388014) on an issue in the Nuxt repo, which explained there were potentially problems with useAsyncData stemming from `'#app'` imports. Sure enough, on the two pages where I was experiencing issues with `useSanityQuery`, I had:

```js
import { useRoute, useRouter } from '#app';
```

Converting these to use `'#imports'` immediately resolved my issue:
```js
import { useRoute, useRouter } from '#imports';
```

I've been able to remove my query key workaround above, it turns out this was simply triggering reactivity that wasn't working due to route watchers. I'd be curious to know if this simple fix might address your issue @jeffreyroulston.

issues.title: The use of the refetch with GROQ param refs since GROQ does not support conditional params
issues.body:
I have a blog listing page which has the following params:

- `$industrySlug` which is used as an optional filter, whereby if applied it filters blog articles by a reference field. so `&& industry->slug.current == $industry`
- `$offset` - which is used to calculate pagination

I might be missing something, but currently, [ according to this line of the docs](https://sanity.nuxtjs.org/getting-started/usage/#usesanityquery), the sanity fetch module listens to changes to the computed properties past into the params argument to trigger a refetch. However, after speaking with [the Sanity team in Slack to confirm](https://sanity-io-land.slack.com/archives/C9Z7RC3V1/p1669829385635669), GROQ does not support conditional params. Meaning if a param is empty, I'll end up with `[_type in ["article"] && industry->slug.current == null`, which will return no articles instead of all articles. What I of course need is `[_type in ["article]]` if no industry is passed. As GROQ does not support conditionals params, any conditional logic has to be handled before the GROQ string is concatenated and passed into the query, however, the module won't be listening to those changes.  
```
const blogQuery = `*[_type == "article"${industry ? ' && industry->slug.current == ${industrySlug}' : ''}]`; // contains conditional logic if industry exists
```

If there was a way to manually refetch, this might suffice, but if there is a way to listen for changes to the query string that would probably be best otherwise we're doubling up on watchers.

issues.title: Set privateRuntimeConfig for cdn use
issues.body:
When using Nuxt in SPR mode, like …

```
export default {
	ssr: true,
	target: 'static',
	…
}
```
(in nuxt.config.js)

… and using Sanity with `useCdn: true`, content is not immediately updated, when running/triggering `nuxt generate`/`npm run generate`.

Fyi: At the Sanity dashboard you can configure web hooks, that are triggered when content changes. So usually you would trigger `nuxt generate` at this place.

The problem is: When using `useCdn: true`, we’ll get a cached response, that is not up to date. This is why we need to achieve `useCdn` being set to `false` while generating.

Overriding `useCdn` inside `privateRuntimeConfig` will solve the problem.

```
sanity: {
	projectId: process.env.SANITY_PROJECT_ID,
	dataset: 'production',
	useCdn: true,
},

privateRuntimeConfig: {
	sanity: {
		useCdn: false,
	},
},
```
(in nuxt.config.js)


So I was wondering why this isn’t the default behaviour?
Or at least add this to the docs?
issues.author: ghost

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body: @JonathanDoelan Could you clarify what you think should be the default behaviour?

comments.author: ghost
comments.body:
@danielroe the privateRuntimeConfig-part. But this maybe conflicts with the mode, where ssr=true and target=server. Because then it would always use the uncached cdn. 

So I think it should be mentioned at least in the docs. For the reasons I‘ve described above.

Then I think you would achieve your desired behaviour of getting freshest content when statically generated, yet using the CDN on client-side.
