issues.title: Trace source of installed modules and injected templates
issues.body:
When modules use `installModule` kit util to install another, it is often hard to trace it without explicitly checking all bundled codes. Adding to top, when users also try to manually install some. 

I think something we could at least do is to support new `from` param for `installModule(name, { from: }`. so that we can trace what module installed another and find a way to encourage module authors do it.

I guess we might at least leverage it for devtools to somehow visualize.

(as another enhancement, we could make nuxt kit made modules to be auto trackable using `unctx` and AsyncLocalStorage it might be useful for further DX enhancements)

---

Reference: How i debugged it currently by patching kit today:

```js
async function installModule(moduleToInstall, inlineOptions, nuxt = useNuxt()) {
  if (typeof moduleToInstall === 'string') {
    const { parseNodeModulePath } = await importModule('mlly')
    const modulePkgName = parseNodeModulePath(moduleToInstall).name
    if (modulePkgName) {
      const trace = new Error('').stack.split('\n')[2]
      const traceFile = /\((.+)\)/.exec(trace)?.[1]?.split(':')[0]
      const traceName = parseNodeModulePath(traceFile).name
      consola.log(`Installing module ${modulePkgName} from ${traceName}`)
    }
  }
```

issues.title: nuxt/kit: ability to configure web components for auto-import
issues.author: WickyNilliams

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body: Would welcome thoughts from @prashantpalikhe and @steveworkman.

comments.author: steveworkman
comments.body:
I agree that adding imports manually is a chore, and in a CSR Vue app it's the only way to split the WC imports effectively due to their inherent side effects. That given, it does work very well.

Assuming that a WC library had a manifest (not all of them do) and the template parser could pick up WCs by their tags as defined in the next config, then it is plausible that they could be auto-imported.

If there is no manifest then I don't see how this can work. One could be supplied in the next config but at that point you may as well have put the imports in the right components.

Thinking of this in relation to the SSR-lit plugin, we had issues with the import order of some of the lit dependencies. The WCs that are detected to be imported would need to be included along with other route/component specific imports so that they are loaded late enough for the SSR plugins to be ready for them.

Happy to test this out if it gets a PR.

comments.author: WickyNilliams
comments.body:
Thanks Steve. Appreicate your perspective especially with regards to SSR. I would personally, as a first step, want to keep the scope very narrow so that it only covers client side rendering, and _only_ extends nuxt kit to allow auto imports of web components. Consuming a manifest, adding options to nuxt config, or SSR concerns can be added later/independently. 

> If there is no manifest then I don't see how this can work. One could be supplied in the next config but at that point you may as well have put the imports in the right components

I'm not sure I agree. The nature of WCs mean that there is no identifier to import. So you get no type errors at build time if you fail to import a WC. And vscode offers no suggestion to add an import. So an import is very easily forgotten. And when you do forget, you get (often silent) failures at runtime. 

Worse yet, because web components are in a global registry, you may not get any failures _even_ if you forget an import. Consider `ComponentA` and `ComponentB` both depend on a web component `my-button`. `ComponentA` correctly imports `my-button`, whilst `ComponentB` did not. 

In isolation, `ComponentB` will not render correctly. But in cases where `ComponentA` was also loaded on the current (or a previous) page, meaning `my-button` is already in the global registry, `ComponentB` will render perfectly fine despite its missing imports. This can get confusing and hard to track down, especially as the module graph gets more complex. 

So there is still value even if manually defining each web component for auto-import, because it guarantees imports are always correlated with usage. Which is why I think extending nuxt kit _just enough_ is useful in itself, and it can act as an enabler for better/smarter functionality to be built on top later.

comments.author: daleweaver777
comments.body:
What would be awesome is when Nitro matches the route, have some way to abort handling the request and allow Nuxt to handle the request.

`Example Route Structure`
server/routes/[slug].get.ts
pages/index.vue

If the the param in `[slug].get.ts` in Nitro doesn't match a certain criteria, you should be able to defer handling the request to Nuxt and render `index.vue` instead.

A great use case would be a url shortner app. If the `slug` param isn't in the redirect database, render the `index.vue` page instead of a `404`.

comments.author: Gonzo17
comments.body:
> * Does my plan sound like I am on the right track?

I don't know about that since I'm not familiar with the nuxt core, but I'd like to find that out as well and help if needed! I've come across this in one of my projects and think a warning would really help.

> * When you say a wildcard route can trigger the warning do you mean that `server/api/[...].ts` would cause an overlap with `pages/foobar.vue` and if that is the case would having this wildcard not overlap with every pages route in the root dir?

Testing around, I realised that `server/routes/[...].ts` doesn't work, while `server/routes/test/[...].ts` does. So one example is if you have `server/routes/test/[...].ts` and something like `pages/test/foobar.vue`.

I think that `server/routes/[...].ts` doesn't work is to prevent that someone blocks page rendering by accident, but wouldn't that also be worth a warning?

Thinking about it, there come more questions to my mind:

- Would having something like `server/routes/foobar.post.ts` still be worth a warning? It would overlap with the path of `pages/foobar.vue`, but since the method is different, both will be accessible.
- When someone uses a catch-all route for pages like `pages/[...].vue`, do we still want to have a warning? Effectively it will clash with every middleware route defined. A use case for that is if you have a CMS. The nuxt application doesn't know about the paths, it just sends them to the CMS. In that case you usually just have a couple of Nuxt pages or just this catch-all route. The warning would not be helpful here, so do we want to ignore this case?



> What would be awesome is when Nitro matches the route, have some way to abort handling the request and allow Nuxt to handle the request.
> [...]
> A great use case would be a url shortner app. If the `slug` param isn't in the redirect database, render the `index.vue` page instead of a `404`.

I feel like this would make things more complex than necessary. In your use case I would suggest to let the pages handle what is shown and create an endpoint in `api` rather then `routes`. If you want to handle redirects before the user enters the page, you can even add a router middleware that calls `/api/some-slug` and decides if the user should be redirected to home based on the result. I've done that in a chat application where I generated invitation links for chat rooms that are only available as long as someone is still in there.

But I also might be wrong here and my approach was not a best practice. So further thoughts to this topic are appreciated. :)

issues.title: Add load and error events for server compoments
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

At the moment there is no real way to display a loading state while a server component is getting fetched.
We basically have 2 options.
1. Intercept fetch request with a worker and check if it is the relevant url
2. Add some global state and modify it inside the server component when it reaches the browser

Both of these solutions have issues.

I suggest we add an event on `document` and let the user do something like 

```js
if (!process.server) {
  document.addEventListener('island:loaded', (e) => {
    console.log(e)
    loading.value = false
  })
}
```

I made a small patch as PoC https://github.com/marccremer/nuxt_islands_issue/blob/loading_island_events/.yarn/patches/nuxt-npm-3.10.0-f38f448dd9.patch

I am looking for feedback on the shape of the event and location in the life cycle.
Additionally I think we should add an error event later on

### Additional information

- [X] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

comments.body:
I didn't know ``expose`` was a thing and adding an additional slot seemed to complex for me, 
as it  would be inside the server component, but behave completely different and only be relevant in the browser.
The ``#fallback`` slot already does loading for lazy server components. What is needed is a loading state for when props change.

Is there a good reason not to use ``document`` ?  The event would only ever fire when there is a document.

marccremer
comments.body:
I am using something like this at work https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/marccremer/nuxt_islands_issue/tree/loading_island_events
and have not had any issues with it yet.

I want to keep the event driven messaging.
It works well for loading and error states. I just choose the document as it was the simplest, but I would love it if there was something like `nuxtApp.shared` , where I could register the listeners

comments.author: huang-julien
comments.body:
What I mean is that this loading state is only related to a single component instance -> the island. And each island have their own loading state. `expose()` and component events are made for that.

We do have hooks on nuxt, yet I don't think this is a good idea to allow islands to use hooks, especially for loading state. This isn't like the nuxt loading indicator which is something more global in the nuxt application context.

I think we should start with by exposing a loading state `ref()` from nuxt island and then it will be up to users to create their own wrapper around nuxt-island if they want to use an event bus. 🙂

issues.title: Scan index files within subdirectories for composables, utils and middlewares
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

A common practice is to separate the logic between files and keep the test files together with the code.
I suggest to scan index files within the subdirectories for composables, utils and middlewares by default, how it is currently done for modules and plugins (but is deprecated https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/25331 😞 ), where the auto-registered files patterns are:

```sh
modules/*/index.ts
modules/*.ts
```

### Motivation:
I recently created another Nuxt project and without suspecting it, created a folder with an index file inside composables, but of course it did not work. So I had to do what I do for all new Nuxt projects::
```ts
  dirs: [
    'composables/*/*.ts',
    'utils/*/*.ts'
  ],
```

Which seems unnatural and, to me, doesn't really fit with Nuxt's title — "The **Intuitive** Vue framework."
The typical folders structure I usually work with:
```sh
composables/
  useHost/
    tests
    index.ts
  useMask/
    tests
    index.ts
...
```

### Additional information

- [X] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [X] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).
issues.author: enkot

comments.author: TheAlexLichter
comments.body:
This behavior [is documented](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/composables#how-files-are-scanned). IMO the current scanning behavior allows your folders, e.g. `composables`, to (re-)export all composables which should be auto-importable on the top level while keeping utility composables on a lower level. This could be used to group code better and avoid end-user mistakes by e.g. accidentally auto-importing composables you do not want to use without more context ☺️ 

Same applies to all other folders.

comments.author: enkot
comments.body:
> IMO the current scanning behavior allows your folders, e.g. `composables`, to (re-)export all composables which should be auto-importable on the top level while keeping utility composables on a lower level. 
> 
It is for this reason that I suggest changing the behavior so that the user doesn't have to worry about re-exports or workarounds (like `dirs: ['composables/*/*.ts']`) 🙂 
> This could be used to group code better and avoid end-user mistakes by e.g. accidentally auto-importing composables you do not want to use without more context 

To avoid such situations we can import from the index file only and not scan any other files inside the directory.

issues.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: `Darwin`
- Node Version:     `v20.7.0`

- Builder:          `-`
- User Config:      `extends`, `alias`, `dir`, `typescript`, `app`, `components`, `imports`
- Runtime Modules:  `-`
- Build Modules:    `-`


### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-zx3fux

### Describe the bug

Using global middlewares with Nuxt Layers will not retain the alphabetical order based on the file names.

In my repodruction my `nuxt-app` project extends `base-layer`.

Global middlwares in `nuxt-app`:
* `00.main.global.ts`

Global middlwares in `base-layer`:
* `01.base.global.ts`

Expected order:
* `00.main.global.ts`
* `01.base.global.ts`

Actual order:
* `01.base.global.ts`
* `00.main.global.ts`

Check logs in the reproduction.

Currently I fixed the issue by using plugins to register the middlewares in the right order:
Base Plugin:
```ts
// base-layer/plugins/00.global-middleware-fix.ts
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  globalBaseMiddlewares.forEach((middleware, index) => addRouteMiddleware(`00-${index}`, middleware, { global: true }))
})
```
Main Plugin:
```ts
// /plugins/00.global-middleware-fix.ts
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  globalMainMiddlewares.forEach((middleware, index) => addRouteMiddleware(`00-${index}`, middleware, { global: true }))
})
```

### Additional context

Related stackoverflow post: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77826748/order-of-middlewares-in-nuxt3-layers

### Logs

_No response_

issues.title: Allow running configured middlewares before scanned middlewares
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

The module I'm working on includes a server middleware component which adds properties to the `event.context`. Consumers of the module may also want to develop server middleware which depends on these properties. For this to work, we need to ensure that the application's server middleware runs after the module's. 

It's possible to register the middleware as the first handler by directly setting the `serverHandlers` option instead of using `addServerHandler`. For example: 

```
nuxt.options.serverHandlers.unshift({
  middleware: true,
  handler: resolve('./runtime/server/middleware/bootstrap'),
})
```

But it appears that any middlewares automatically scanned from the middlewares directory, will still be executed first. https://github.com/unjs/nitro/blob/3cdf3d96e02c2765e7269f6054418982dd876a09/src/rollup/plugins/handlers.ts#L6 The current workaround is to require applications to not use the auto-scanning and instead add `serverHandlers` in their nuxt.config, but this is non-obvious and goes against the default approach. 

Is there a better way that the priorities of server middlewares could be explicitly defined? 

Alternatively, maybe it makes sense to default to executing `scannedMiddlewares` last? I think that would make the workflow a bit easier. If you care about the execution order, you manually set the nitro config and if the ordering is not important you can then rely on the scanning.

(Also, I'm not sure if this would be better as a Nitro issue. Please let me know if I should refile elsewhere. :)The code I linked is from Nitro, but perhaps this use case could be solved at the Nuxt level)

comments.author: xak2000
comments.body:
@warflash

> So `error.data` is what you're looking for.

But why? I found several issues explaining that you should use `error.data.statusMessage` instead of `error.statusMessage`. But none of them explain why.

As I understand, the `error.statusMessage` is the **HTTP Protocol** _status text_ also known as _reason phrase_., returned together with the HTTP _status code_ in the HTTP response [_status line_](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2616#section-6.1). While `error.data.statusMessage` is just a JSON field of the HTTP **response payload**. Please correct me if I'm wrong.

In DEV mode the DEV server response looks like this:

```
HTTP/1.1 <statusCode from createError(...)> <statusMessage from createError(...)>
```

E.g. for an error like this:

```ts
throw createError({
    statusCode: 403,
    statusMessage: 'USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER',
})
```

The response will be like this:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER
...headers...

{"url":"...","statusCode":403,"statusMessage":"USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER"}
```

But in PROD mode the response of the server is like this:

```
HTTP/3 403
...headers...

{"url":"...","statusCode":403,"statusMessage":"USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER"}
```

As you can see the HTTP response _status line_ doesn't contain _status text_. Probably in my case this is not a Nuxt fault, but a Google Load Balancer proxy fault (I suspect the LB removes the response status text, but I'm not sure - can't find it in the docs).

But, even if it is Load Balancer's fault, we should accept that this is pretty common for a load balancers/proxies to mess with the HTTP protocol level _status line_. So, it would be wise to not rely on this when the response is converted back to `FetchError` object. When I'm calling `throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER' })` I expect that on the client I will receive `error.statusMessage` that is equal to `USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER`.

But, if a proxy or a Load Balancer changed the status line before the client received the response, then with the current implementation **this is not the case**. The object `error.statusMessage` will inlcude the augmented value from the status line (or will just be empty). So, the client will lost the information about the error. This behavior is **very confusing and error-prone**.

As `createError` puts the provided `statusMessage` into both status line and JSON body of the response, can we just deserialize `statusMessage` on the client from the response body instead of relying on the HTTP Protocol _status line_? This will be much more reliable as it doesn't involve relying on the HTTP Protocol level status text (reason phrase), that is optional by the HTTP Protocol RFC and is often removed/normalized by production proxies.

From the [RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2616#section-6.1.1):

> The Reason-Phrase is intended to give a short textual description of the Status-Code. The Status-Code is intended for use by automata and **the Reason-Phrase is intended for the human user. The client is not required to examine or display the Reason-Phrase.**

(emphasize is mine)

The RFC doesn't say that the Reason-Phrase shouldn't be examined by the client, but it still states the main reason for the Reason-Phrase to exist: for the human user. And the established practices from the last 20 years are like this. That is why, I think, popular proxy implementations and cloud providers are feeling free to mess with the Reason-Phrase. They do not expect it to be used for the app logic.

If it is not possible to deserialize `error.statusMessage` from the response body, then I think at the very minimum the Nuxt documentation should explain what `statusMessage` of `createError` parameter object is (how it is transferred and how to access it on the client) and warn that we should not rely on the value of this field on the client. I think, the docs should discourage to use this field of the `error` object and encourage to use the `error.data` instead, if it is not possible to deserialize the `error.statusMessage` from the response body.

### TLDR

My main point is: when we do `throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Custom message' })` on the server and then do `catch (error) { console.log(error.statusMessage) }` on the client, we expect `error.statusMessage` to be equal to `Custom message` and not to `Forbidden`. It is just a reasonable expectation, isn't it? _A principle of least surprise_ I would say. And, as `statusMessage` is already serializing into the response body, what is the reason to deserialize it from the response phrase (making deserialization dependent on the proxy's mercy)?

issues.title: useFetch fetchPolicy
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Give more control over caching with fetching strategies/policies:

```js
useFetch('/api/foo', {
  fetchPolicy: 'cache-first',
})
```

- `cache-first`: if present in cache, return without requesting, otherwise request then update the cache.
- `cache-and-network` : if present in cache, return. In any case, request in the background then update the cache.
- `network-only`: request and wait response to return, then update the cache.
- `cache-only`: only return from cache, don't request.
- `no-cache`: request and wait response to return, don't update the cache.
- `standby`: same as `cache-first` but don't refresh if path/parameter changes.

We are encountering an issue with Hot Module Replacement (HMR) within a Docker environment on both MacOS and Windows (using WSL 2.0). Specifically, the problem involves adding new files to the pages and server directories of our Nuxt 3 application. Changes to existing files, including components, styles, and text contents, are correctly recognized and processed. issues.title: Change behavior of `default` in `useCookie` to be consistent with other composables
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

The current behavior of `default` is inconsistent with other composables such as `useFetch`, `useAsyncData` and `useState`:
1. `default` value is used only on init.
2. `default` value is set to cookies in SSR, but not in CSR (https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/26701).

Proposals (breaking):
1. The default value must be used even if the value is later set to `null` or `undefined`:
```ts
const foo = useCookie('foo', { default: () => 'Stark' })
foo.value // -> 'Stark'
foo.value = 'Hulk'
foo.value // -> 'Hulk'
foo.value = undefined
foo.value // -> 'Stark' because it is default
```
Just as it is done for `useFetch` - if the `data` is undefined or it is an error, default value is used.
Also, good examples are [Vue prop default value](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/props.html#prop-validation) and  https://vueuse.org/shared/refDefault.

2. or rename `default` to `init` to match `useState` where default data is only used once during initialization.

In all cases default value should not be set to cookies on init.

### Additional information

- [X] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).

comments.author: dsvgl
comments.body:
Ah, I see. We use https://github.com/freddy38510/vue3-lazy-hydration for such things. So you can wrap your time output in template with:

```vue
<template>
  <LazyHydrationWrapper>
    {{ new Date() }}
  </LazyHydrationWrapper>
</template>
```

Having no lazy-hydration specific prop on `< LazyHydrationWrapper>` means it will never hydrate on client side.

There is also really nice nuxt-module to wrap vue3-lazy-hydration: https://github.com/Baroshem/nuxt-lazy-hydrate.
With this, you'd use `<NuxtLazyHydrate>`  instead of `<LazyHydrationWrapper>`.

There is an open issue to bake this into nuxt. Hopefully it will land some day: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/24242

issues.title: feat: add plugin resolved hook
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

I've recently worked on support for static analysis of nuxt plugin hooks when using the object syntax. This massively improved hooking for us and allowed us to discover one short-coming of plugin hooks / plugin execution order.

Imagine the following situation: Your Nuxt App uses two modules, one is the official `@pinia/nuxt` module which is used for creating a store that hold the locale of the application. The other module is one you write yourself and handles authentication. The authentication module allows you to hook into an event whenever the signed in user identity changes. You now want to update your stored locale whenever the locale of the identity changes to reflect the preferences of your user.
To make that happen you create a plugin in your app that listens to the event, gets the store and updates the locale if necessary.

You now realize that this won't work, as you depend on the `pinia` plugin to have been executed before your hook callback is executed, otherwise there is no active pinia instance. Since the authentication module is generic and doesn't need `pinia`, it doesn't depend on `pinia` and might run in parallel with it.

To solve this I'm proposing the following solution
1. Emit an event whenever a plugin has been resolved, `app:plugin:resolved`, with a callback parameter of the plugin name.
2. Keep track of the resolved plugins
3. Add a nuxtApp method `runAfterPlugin` that allows a user to register a callback that is executed either immediately (if the plugin has been resolved already) or whenever the `app:plugin:resolved` event for the relevant plugin is called.

This allows a user to side-step any race-conditions like described above. It is basically the runtime inverse of the statically defined `dependsOn`. Instead of defining which other plugin you might rely on before executing them, it allows for depending on plugins at runtime.

### Additional information

- [X] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [X] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

issues.title: Ability to add pages dynamically based on an API call
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

**What is this for?**
- Many projects utilize a CMS, allowing users to fully customize the slug of pages. This results in a situation where the specific page file to use for a given route is unknown in advance.
- For example, visiting `/foo` would result in an API call to retrieve the name of the `.vue` file to use and perhaps some additional data. The correct page would then be mounted just like in regular Nuxt routing. These slugs, managed by the website's admin, do not have any prefix and can be customized dynamically.

Many developers are unsure about the best approach to implement something like this in Nuxt.
Here are the main concerns:
- No Nuxt routing features should be sacrificed (e.g., runtime page hooks, page transitions, layout switching, page meta, etc.).
- Normal Nuxt routing should still work, and the developer should have control over whether or not to make the API call for Nuxt-generated routes as well.
- Nuxt should not generate routes for these “dynamic” page files automatically (so that I cannot access the dynamic page `foo.vue`, for example, when no API call to get the page type was made prior)
- NuxtLinks to the dynamic pages should be allowed to appear in the template without causing a Vue Router warning about a non-existing route.
- The async request should ideally be able to run in parallel with everything else before rendering (plugins, etc.)


——

I'm linking the original issue here: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/7437

@Rigo-m 

This functionality cannot be build-time, in the use case of Nuxt over CMS it is assumed that the user can create new entities in the admin panel, and their creation should not require rebuilding the project. Or the user can change routing settings, rename entities and so on.

@CernyMatej  @danielroe 

I solved the problem at the application level rather than at the plugin level (and I think that's the right thing to do).
I've created a single catch-all page (and this is the only page in `/pages` directory) that makes a request to the API to define the page, then passes further control to it. 

Simplified:
```vue
// pages/[..path].vue

<template>
  <component :is="pageComponent" />
</template>

<script setup>
  const entries = {
    'page-index': defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~pages/page-index/page-index.vue')),
    'page-catalog': defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~pages/page-catalog/page-catalog.vue')),
  };

  const { data } = await useAsyncData('entry', () => fetchPageComponent(useRoute().path));

  const pageComponent = computed(() => entries[data.value.entry]);
</script>
```

Next, each page component requests data for itself. 
This was not so easy with Nuxt 2 and the "async data only at page level" restriction (although I figured out a way to solve it anyway), but with Nuxt 3 and `Suspense` this restriction is gone and it works fine.

I don't think this can be universally solved at the platform level by the way, the solution is going to be roughly the same as above on the user side anyway.

**I'd rather have a built-in ability to disable file routing, as the solution suggested above works but feels a little hacky** with that single catch-all route (most of time).

Actually, from the [documentation](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/app), it looks like Nuxt already allows you to do something like the solution above via single `app.vue`, but the comment "If not present, Nuxt won't include [vue-router](https://router.vuejs.org/) dependency" stops me from doing it. 
I still need `vue-router`, although I don't need file routing using the pages directory.

If we can make two new explicit settings in the core like `{ useFileRouting: boolean; includeVueRouter: boolean }` and remove the implicit dependency of `/pages` directory from `vue-router`, then the approach above is perfectly fine with me (although I'm not the author of the issue, but I think we're solving the same problem). 

`app.vue` will be a single entrypoint of the application (which doesn't feel like a hack), and it's up to the developer to decide where to pass control from there.

issues.title: Keep context when opening error page
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Hey there. This might be a duplicate, but this time I got proposal!

So the issue is that when we open error page all context is lost due to new request and Vue limitations. This might be solved in 2 different ways in my opinion.

### Motivation

We, for example, have debug menu, that shows failed requests. That stopped working in Nuxt 3 on SSR.

Also, it would be awesome to access some data you got on some step for error page to show better error - and more!

## Solution 1

Don't fire request on error.

1. Use global Suspense
3. Create inner error component with onServerPrefetch
4. That onServerPrefetch will wait for parent suspense to resolve or fail

That will require https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/8555 to be merged first. This theoretically should work just like it did in Nuxt 2.

## Solution 2

This is my proposal. 

1. Create unique Request UID for each request
2. Make a composable for it to access anywhere
3. Store data for that UID in global context somewhere
4. Transfer UID to error page request
5. On error page check for UID existence and add this context as default
6. To prevent memory leak, clear old UIDs (more than 15 seconds for example) by global interval - in case something will fail when requesting error page

1-2 can actually be done as separate PR, since I think it would be a good Nuxt feature for headers like X-REQUEST-ID for better logging.

That 'fallback error page', which is not to be confused with the [Error Page (i.e.: `error.vue`)](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/error-handling#error-page), is handled by the configured Nitro error handler.

issues.title: Real SSR-friendly Ref
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

### The problem

Sometimes we need a `ref` that works exactly as `ref`, have full semantics and behavior of `ref`, but still works fine with SSR.

In the [docs](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/state-management) `useState` is advertised as "an SSR-friendly `ref` replacement", which is actually not true as `useState` has different semantics and behavior than `ref` in addition to its SSR-friendliness.

To quote the docs:
> [useState](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/composables/use-state) is an SSR-friendly [ref](https://vuejs.org/api/reactivity-core.html#ref) replacement. Its value will be preserved after server-side rendering (during client-side hydration) and shared across all components using a unique key.

What I need is an analogue to `ref` where only the first part of `useState` description ("Its value will be preserved after server-side rendering") is true, but not the second ("shared across all components using a unique key").

I.e. that `ref` should be:
1. Initialized **every time** when `script setup` is executed (`init` function of `useState` is not executed on any client-side navigation except the 1st).
2. Preserved between SSR and client-side setup (i.e. hydrated, just like `useState` does).
3. Not shared between component instances or other components (unlike `useState`).

### The workaround

Currently I use workaround like this:

```ts
const nuxtApp = useNuxtApp()
const componentId = useId()
const myRef = useState(componentId, () => null)
if (!nuxtApp.isHydrating) {
  // Called by SSR (initial page load), but also on each client-side navigation too, just as normal ref(generateInitialValue()) would.
  myRef.value = generateInitialValue()
}
onUnmounted(() => clearNuxtState(componentId))
```

I think with the workaround above `myRef` behaves identical to a usual `Ref`, but preserves the value generated by `generateInitialValue()` called from SSR if the component was first rendered by SSR, instead of generating a new initial value (that could be different from SSR-generated value) when the component is rendered on the client.

Also, `myRef` is not shared with anyone (even different instances of the same component), just like normal `ref`.

And it's initialization will be performed on each call to `script setup` function, just like normal `ref`. Unlike `useState()`, that calls `init` only 1 time, then `init` is never called again until full server-side reload of the page, that is not what you expect from "ref replacement".

The downside of this workaround is that on every client-side navigation a new key is created in `useState` data keys storage. So it is a memory leak in this case, as the semantic of `ref` allows to not preserve the value between navigations. It's just a side-effect of using `useState` and `useId` under the hood. I added `onUnmounted(() => clearNuxtState(componentId))`, but this just removes the values, not the keys. Ideally these keys should be removed right after hydration is finished.

### The proposition

What I want instead is a built-in function that will allow me to write just this:

```ts
const myRef = useSsrFriendlyRef(() => generateInitialValue())
```
(the name of the function is discussable, of course 😂)

### The usefulness

Such SSR-friendly `ref` is useful, for example, to generate an initial data to use it as parameters of API called by `useFetch`. These parameters need to be stable between SSR and client-side calling to `useFetch` to make generated fetch key be stable and hydration work.

One case when I needed this SSR-friendly `ref` is a component that displays a graph with some data. To load these data from the API the component need to pass a range of dates (e.g. `GET /api/data?from=2024-08-13&to=2024-09-13`). The default (initial) range is "from 30 days ago to the current date". After the component is rendered, user should be able to change the range. But on the initial render `useFetch` requests the data for the last 30 days. To make it work properly we need this initial date range to be initialized only once per navigation, but still to be initialized every time the component's setup is called (i.e. the changes user made to `from` and `to` dates should be forgotten if user navigates away from the route and then navigates back). All this behavior is perfectly covered by `ref` except the SSR part. With `ref` the current date could be different in SSR rendered component and client-side rendered component, so the initial date range is different, the `useFetch` key is different, the `useFetch` response hydration doesn't work and `useFetch` is executed 2nd time on the client.

Anyway, it is just one use-case (maybe not the perfect). The idea of this feature-request is not covering just one use-case, but having a standard mechanism to create SSR-friendly `ref`s, with full semantic of normal `ref`, unlike `useState`, that certainly helpful when you need a shared state, but gets in the way when you need a private state, just like with `ref`, but stable between SSR and client-side rendering.

I remember `useId()` was introduced not long time ago to cover just a specific case of html element `id` generation (and similar cases). I think it solves similar problem, but in less generic way (you can't use your own initializer, `useId()` always returns a "random" string).

P.S. I tried to search for similar questions/proposition everywhere but didn't find anything. Maybe it's just my skill of creating a correct search requests. :) Anyway, if this idea was already discussed, please point me at it. Honestly, I'm very surprised that it was never discussed, as it is not the first time when I personally needed this feature, just the 1st time when I decided to create a feature request.

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
  _I would like to, but I'm afraid I will not be able. I tried to understand the implementation of `useId` but it looks like pure black magic to me._
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [X] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).
issues.author: xak2000

comments.author: xak2000
comments.body:
Found an alternative workaround.

```ts
const nuxtApp = useNuxtApp()
const componentId = useId()
const { data: myRef } = await useAsyncData(componentId, () => generateInitialValue())
onUnmounted(() => delete nuxtApp.payload.data[componentId])
```

As `useAsyncData` skips calling to the function when app is hydrating, the semantic is the same as with the 1st workaround above.

I'm not sure about `delete nuxtApp.payload.data[componentId]` though. Is it the right way to delete a key from the cache? I don't like that this code touching Nuxt internals. But `clearNuxtData` doesn't remove the key (only the value).

I also not sure about `onUnmounted` event handler. Is it the right handler to remove the data to simulate `ref` semantics?

And aside question: why is payload data not removed by default by Nuxt when component is unmounted? When component, that called `useAsyncData`, is unmounted or client-side navigation is performed, the data is kept forever in the memory until next page reload happens. With many client-side navigation events (i.e. when page is never hard-reloaded) this could be a problem (memory-leak). This data is not useful anyway because on the next mount the `useAsyncData` handler will be called again anyway, so the data will be fetched again, right? So, why keep these data in the cache and in memory when component, that called `useAsyncData` is not alive anymore? Probably, data could be shared by another compoment by `key` (that is why!), but it (the number of components that use the same `key`) could be tracked, if needed.

comments.author: luc122c
comments.body:
Confirmed in `3.13.2` as above, and main also still in main. 

According to MiniMax:
> The root cause: SSR inline styles use ?inline&used queries that bypass Vite's transform pipeline, so custom Vite plugins never get a chance to process them.
A fix would need to apply Vite transforms to SSR style extraction, or handle custom style attributes in the SSR style plugin itself.

comments.author: luc122c
comments.body:
This one might be a bit over my head. Putting this here for someone more cleverer than me to pick up: 
> The issue is in how @vitejs/plugin-vue handles Vue SFC <style> blocks:
> 1. When SSR needs inline styles, it emits a chunk reference with ?inline&used
> 2. @vitejs/plugin-vue's load and transform hooks intercept these requests
> 3. The CSS is extracted directly from @vitejs/plugin-vue's parsed SFC cache without going through Vite's transform pipeline
> 4. User plugins can't transform the CSS because @vitejs/plugin-vue doesn't call next() for style blocks - it returns directly

Pasting an excerpt from my comment about the now duplicated issue https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/29923#issuecomment-2529500400 as it seems relevant : 

_____


It would also want to see a consolidation of all the auto import settings underneath a single key, to make it easier to enable, disable, understand and share import settings between project. Maybe we can provide a few presets out of the box, `nuxt3` or `minimal` for the people who like them.

Something like this : 

```ts
import { autoImports } from "nuxt"
const legacy = defineNuxtConfig({ autoImports: autoImports("nuxt3") }) // Some preset
const noImport = defineNuxtConfig({ autoImports: false }) //Disable everything
```
It should be straightforward to get the same configuration as now and to disable everything, with a sensible default to make sure that nothing breaks.
The new settings key would be used to configure auto-imports for *everything*, unimport presets, components, composables, modules, nitro, custom directories etc

For modules specifically, I would love to be able to enable or disable auto-imports for a given module, without needing to touch the module configuration itself : For example in [this module](https://github.com/Hebilicious/vue-query-nuxt/blob/3def2729d227226e5dad57d52d60ed2e6e59d568/packages/vue-query-nuxt/src/module.ts#L91) there's a setting to disable them, but I should be able to override auto-import for any module like this : 

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ autoImports: { modules: { myModule: false } } })
```
_____

I'm in favour of using a single key so that we can import full presets and re-use them easily accross projects. Presets must be fully serializable, and must contain everything related to auto-imports.

For example we should find the following keys underneath  autoImport : 

- uninmportPresets
- components
- modules 
- composables
- nitro
- customDirs

issues.title: Nuxt restarts when data in sqlite .db file is updated in directory root
issues.body: ### Environment ------------------------------ - Operating System: Windows_NT - Node Version: v20.15.0 - Nuxt Version: 3.14.0 - CLI Version: 3.15.0 - Nitro Version: - - Package Manager: pnpm@9.4.0 - Builder: - - User Config: default - Runtime Modules: - - Build Modules: - ------------------------------ ### Reproduction To recreate this issue I used Drizzle ORM and added a button to app.vue in order to save some data into a .db file. [https://github.com/matt-clegg/nuxt-restart-issue-repro](https://github.com/matt-clegg/nuxt-restart-issue-repro) 1. Create a new empty Nuxt project with `pnpx nuxi init `. 2. Inside the nuxt.config.ts file, set the compatibility version to 4 with `future: { compatibilityVersion: 4 },` and compatibility date to: `compatibilityDate: "2024-07-30",`, move the app.vue file into the /app directory. 3. Install Drizzle ORM dependency and Drizzle Kit as a dev dependency. 4. Configure Drizzle to use sqlite and store the database in the root directory. 5. Create a simple Drizzle table schema and a server API endpoint to create data in the table. 6. Generate a migration and update the database with the migration with: `drizzle-kit generate` then `drizzle-kit migrate`. 8. Create a button in the app.vue file to call the server API endpoint. 9. Run project, click the button to add data to the database, Nuxt will "restart". I used the following guide to setup Drizzle: [https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/get-started/sqlite-new](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/get-started/sqlite-new) This is what some key files contain. .env ``` DB_FILE_NAME=file:local.db ``` drizzle.config.ts ```ts import {defineConfig} from "drizzle-kit"; export default defineConfig({ out: './server/database/migrations', schema: './server/database/schema.ts', dialect: 'sqlite', dbCredentials: { url: process.env.DB_FILE_NAME!, }, }); ``` /server/database/schema.ts ```ts import { integer, text, sqliteTable } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core"; export const user = sqliteTable("users", { id: integer("id").primaryKey({autoIncrement: true}), name: text("name").notNull() }) ``` /server/database/drizzle.ts ```ts import {drizzle} from "drizzle-orm/libsql"; export function useDrizzle() { return drizzle( process.env.DB_FILE_NAME! ); } ``` /server/api/users/index.post.ts ```ts import { useDrizzle } from "../../database/drizzle"; import { user } from "../../database/schema"; export default eventHandler(async (event) => { const body = await readBody(event); await useDrizzle().insert(user).values(body); }) ``` /app/app.vue ```vue ``` ### Describe the bug When data in a sqlite database, located in the root directory, is modified, the Nuxt process will restart. For some reason Nuxt thinks the nuxt.config.ts file has been updated when a change is made to the database. ``` √ Nuxt Nitro server built in 1597 ms nitro 08:24:56 i nuxt.config.ts updated. Restarting Nuxt... 08:25:15 ➜ DevTools: press Shift + Alt + D in the browser (v1.6.0) 08:25:16 i Running with compatibility version 4 08:25:16 √ Vite client built in 28ms 08:25:16 √ Vite server built in 268ms 08:25:17  ELIFECYCLE  Command failed with exit code 3221225477. ``` This doesn't happen if the .db file is moved into it's own directory, eg `/data/local.db`. ### Additional context _No response_ ### Logs _No response_

issues.body: ### Environment ```` ------------------------------ - Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) - Node Version: v22 - Nuxt Version: - - CLI Version: 3.15.0 - Nitro Version: - - Package Manager: npm@9.5.0 - Builder: - - User Config: - - Runtime Modules: - - Build Modules: - ------------------------------ ```` ### Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/martinszeltins/nuxt-prefetch-test ### Describe the bug Nuxt by default has page prefetching on "visibility". It means when a NuxtLink is visible in the viewport, Nuxt will prefetch the page in the background. Nice! But it seems to only prefetch the ".vue" file and not the data. For example, if I have a "users" page that fetches user data from an API, and then in another page I have a NuxtLink to the users page, every time I click on that link, I am seeing a loader until the page loads its data using useFetch(). The "users.vue" file is prefetched, but not the data. I could not find any configuration setting how to tell Nuxt to fully preload the pages with all its data so that navigation to it would be "instant" ✨ Here is my reproduction link, there is the Nuxt `app` and `nitro-server` and you need to start both of them. First start the Nuxt app and then start the nitro-server. https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/martinszeltins/nuxt-prefetch-test When you open `http://localhost:3000/` You will see a Nuxt Link that takes you to the users page. I set a 2 second delay so to simulate a real backend. The users page Vue file is prefetched in the background but when you click on the link that takes you to the users page you still have to wait until the users page fetches the data it needs. This means the navigation is never "instant" to the users page. I wish it preloaded the whole page in the background not just the ".vue" file. It is not enough for me to just load the list of users and put them in a store, I need to pre-render the whole page on demand and throw it away on some events. NuxLink also does not seem to respect the ``. It still tries to load the full page each time I click on it. But if I put a regular link like `Users` then it is instant. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b74620fc-c630-4e05-b171-8777c155c40b) ### Additional context _No response_ ### Logs _No response_

issues.title: split section of your app via independent routers
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

## **Main issue:** 

It's a fact, `Nuxt` / `Vue app` are leaking all application URL(s) on hydration because the full router is shipped to the client (this is by design for the `Vue Router`).

Problem: This allows attackers to get the full scope of your application as soon as they get to the first page, enlarging the potential attack surface by leaking your secret admin dashboard or other hidden URL .

_Note:  With only `Vue app`, your application is fully rendered in the client, making even all API routes string available without even passing the `Sign in` page, but as `Nuxt` brings `SSR` with it, (and if you do not write monkey code) this should no longer be the case._

Nowadays, more and more people use `Nuxt` with an `ORM` like `Prisma`, making it a real pain in the ass to setup a multi repo for each part of your app (who want's to pay **7$/user** a month to share a `Prisma schema` private module on `npm` ?). 

### **The questions are:** 
1. "How to have 1 repo to rule them all and avoid to spread or copy interdependencies and components between repositories" 
> I'm tired of looking at this:
>   ```
>   Github repository list:
>   - myproject-api <--- prisma.schema
>   - myproject-user-dashboard <--- prisma.schema  +  components like buttons
>   - myproject-admin-dashboard <--- prisma.schema +  components like buttons
>   - myproject-landing <--- prisma.schema +  components like buttons
> ```
> I want this:
>   ```
>   Github repository list:
>   - myproject 🎉
>   ```

2. "How to hide the existence of some section of my application"
> Why should the user receive all data about other section of the application that he should not be sniffing around ? 

3. "How to use 1 app for all section but keeping them isolated of each other"
> Would be great to keep 1 server to render my web app even if it spitted in multiple sections right?

## **Actual partial solution:** 
Build distinct apps for each section of your app. One for the client, one for the admin etc... using `.env` variables and the `nuxt.config.ts` file's `ignore` property:

**Building the client app without ignore:** 
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02b4c02c-a28e-4fdd-b080-a2ead8685d5c)

**Building the client app with ignore:**
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9d1e89f-10ae-4b5b-a30a-e3521a2384d4)

### **Partial solution conclusion:** 
This solve question 1 and 2, but what about question 3 ? I'm finding myself having to handle `1 container` / `node process` per section of my app... It's better, but... I don't need that much granularity.

## **Another solution (feature request):**
To avoid to build and host multiple different apps for each section of your project : 
- 1 app for the landing pages + sign in
- 1 app for the client dashboard
- 1 app for the admin dashboard
- etc...

It would be great to specify sections of the app that **Nuxt** would generate and serve independent router for.

**Example:** 
```
/pages 
  - /landing <-- 1 router for this section
  - /user <-- 1 router for this section
  - /admin <-- 1 router for this section
```

**Could be setup this way:** 
```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
   routers: {
       landing: ["/pages/*.vue","/pages/landing/**"],       
       user: ["/pages/user/**"],
       admin: ["/pages/admin1234/**"]
       ...
   }
});
```

**This would generate 3 independent routers.**
1. If the user goes to the landing page on `/`, it would be serve with the `landing` router, hiding the `user` and `admin` routes.
2. If the user goes to the landing page on `/user`, it would be serve with the `user` router, hiding the `landing` and `admin` routes
3. If the user goes to the landing page on `/admin1234`, it would be serve with the `admin` router, hiding the `landing` and `user` routes

### **Feature solution conclusion:** 
This should keep the evil at bay.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [x] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

issues.title: Allow setting crossOrigin="use-credentials" for static files served from another domain / CDN (buildAssetsDir/cdnUrl)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Currently, there is no way to set different crossorigin value than "" (anonymous) for static files. 
This becomes a problem when JS static files are served from CDN and we need to pass cookies in order to work properly in certain conditions - for example when Cloudflare Under Attack Mode is being on.

As a workaround, we created Nitro plugin which uses render:html hook. In that hook we have to parse html head and manually replace crossOrigin value.

I believe there should be an option (nuxt.config?) alongside buildAssetsDir and cdnUrl that could faciliate implementation, especially in large-scale projects.

issues.title: Add option to `navigateTo` to avoid reloading all components (shallow routing)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

### Problem

Currently, when using `navigateTo`, it reloads all components on the page. This behavior resets the component state, which may not always be desirable.

For example, if I have a "Create Shipment" page with a form to fill out. When I press "Save", I want the URL to change from `/shipment` to `/shipment/:uuid`, but I don't want the form to be reset. Both routes point to the same page and component. When url is `/shipment` you get a new form and with `/shipment/:uuid` you get filled out form. If I use `navigateTo('/shipment/:uuid')`, the form will be reset because all components are reloaded. But I just want the URL to change because if the user refreshes the page, it should open the saved shipment not a new shipment. I have needed this feature several times already.

### Proposed Solution
Next.js has shallow routing, but it doesn't allow updating params, only query.

This feature request proposes adding an optional parameter to the navigateTo function to allow developers to choose whether or not to reload the components on the page or to keep the page alive. This will handle the scenarios where only the URL update is required without impacting the component lifecycle.

Introduce an option to the navigateTo function, such as:

```ts
navigateTo('/shipment/123', { keepAlive: true })

// or silent
navigateTo('/shipment/123', { silent: true })
```

I would love to hear the Nuxt team's thoughts on this.


### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

comments.author: martinszeltins
comments.body:
@gabrielstuff I basically agree with @posva that ignoring lifecycle events could potentially lead to problems in the future. But at the same time it is very tempting to want the route to change without performing a navigation. It's a tricky situation for sure.

My use case was that I had a single page with optional `id` parameter. So at first, it is a new form, then user clicks on "Save" and the form gets saved and I needed to append the `id` to my route. The only way to do that is to navigate to that route (even though it is the same page).

I either 1) performed navigation which caused data to be re-loaded or 2) I put the data into Pinia store and after navigation grabbed the data from there.

I feel like if you know what you are doing, you should still have the option to simply update the route without performing a navigation. (maybe with a warning).

issues.title: support `#fallback` slot for lazy Nuxt components
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Nuxt3 supports built in lazy component by adding `Lazy` prefix into auto imported component, which is great!

But it does not support `#fallback` slot with which skeleton screen will be shown while loading lazy component, and this will impact to user experience.
In Vue3 suspense experimental component, it supports as below
```
const Chat = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('/Chat.vue'))

<Suspense>
   <Chat />
   <template #fallback>
       loading....
   </template>
</Suspense>
```

Is it possible Nuxt built in lazy component to support `#fallback` slot similar to vue3 `Suspense`? or else is there any way to show skeleton screen already? or am I wrong to approach problem?

Due to this issue, we went with `Suspense` experimental solution, but will be happy to replace with Nuxt built lazy load once it supports `#fallback` slot.

Thanks

As a user, I would expect a loading indicator to be shown while the search requests are pending. Now let's say that there are some results visible, I keep typing and another request (let's call it B) is made. Then, while the request B is in progress, I finish typing. A third request (C) is made - this is the final search query. 200ms after I finished typing, request B finishes and the search results are replaced with the "almost" complete results and the loading indicator is still shown. Only after another while does the request C with the final search results finish, the search results are replaced once again and the loading indicator is hidden.
Personally, I'm not a fan of the content flashing. Maybe there is another way we could solve this?

Yesterday I ran into the same problem (using `cloudflare-module` preset). `useFetch` works fine during SSR but `useAsyncData` with `$fetch` doesn't. I did notice though that the bindings were available directly using `process.env` in both the cases. 

I am using `HYPERDRIVE` and it was available as `process.env.HYPERDRIVE` as an object, so I could directly access the connection string using `process.env.HYPERDRIVE?.connectionString` (typescript did complain about this). Not sure if this is an intended behaviour.

comments.author: oritwoen
comments.body:
@danielroe I looked at it.

This is working as designed, not a bug. `event.context.cloudflare` bindings are nitro/server-only and they were never meant to survive `$fetch` roundtrip into the SSR app layer. 

In `packages/nuxt/src/core/templates.ts` the server fetch module sets `globalThis.fetch = serverFetch` (nitro internal fetch) but `$fetch` itself is just `ofetch.create({ baseURL })` - plain HTTP client with no parent request context. And `useRequestFetch` in `packages/nuxt/src/app/composables/ssr.ts` is literally an alias: `return $fetch as $Fetch`. So none of them forward bindings, by design.                                                                                                                                                                             

Why `useFetch` and direct calls look like they work on Cloudflare: the platform re-injects `event.context.cloudflare` on every incoming request, including the internal HTTP call `$fetch` makes to `/api/*`. So the API handler reads its own fresh binding and returns the keys in the response body. It is not context forwarded from the SSR layer, it is Cloudflare re-attaching the binding per request. Matches the nitro docs note that bindings/env must be read "within the event lifecycle" of a server handler: https://v2.nitro.build/deploy/providers/cloudflare#direct-access-to-cloudflare-bindings                                                                                        

In theory `process.env` works, but nitro has its own dedicated bindings integration and it is hard to actually move that to a layer outside nitro. That is a different matter than nuxt and we shouldn't pretend the app layer can see server bindings. I'd close this as works-as-designed.

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body:
some of the code in `main` as a bit different from `4.x` in terms of the nitro layer/$fetch - does your reasoning still stand when comparing `4.x`?

(thank you for diving in!)

comments.author: oritwoen
comments.body:
I just checked. Sometimes I get lost in all these branches 🫠 

In 4.x `useRequestFetch` returns `useRequestEvent()?.$fetch || $fetch` so it uses nitro's context-aware `event.$fetch` and DOES forward the request context. Plain `$fetch` is still `ofetch.create({ baseURL })` without context.

So `useRequestFetch()` inside `useAsyncData` actually works for Cloudflare bindings. Core still holds either way: raw `$fetch` never forwards bindings and they belong in `/server` handlers. 

*_I mixed up some facts and some branches earlier. My answer may have been unclear, and I've edited this post as well. If anything is still unclear, please let me know._*

issues.title: Add a way to remove Nuxt template added with `addTemplate` function
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

For now there is undocumented feature — returning `undefined` inside template's `getContents` function will remove the template and even remove the file if `write: true`.

I think it is a good idea to implement direct ways to remove templates:

1. `remove()` method on `ResolvedNuxtTemplate` which is a return of `addTemplate` method:

```ts
const myTemplate = addTemplate(...);
myTemplate.remove();
```

2. `removeTemplates()` nuxt kit function with the `filter` property working in the same way as `updateTemplates` **BUT** make it required.

```ts
const myTemplate = addTemplate({ filename: 'sample-template.ts' });

removeTemplates({
    filter: template => template.filename === 'sample-template.ts',
)}
```

The second approach is by all means not safe, allowing to shoot yourself in the knee and delete important core-functionality Nuxt templates.

The first approach is safe because you only have references to templates you created or templates Nuxt or module authors provided to you.

As additional safety measure we can add `persistent: boolean = true` property, which will not allow to remove a template in any way other than undocumented `getContents -> undefined` way (meaning such persistent templates can delete themselfes only from inside).

```ts
const persistentTemplate = addTemplate({
    filename: 'i-am-strong',
    getContents: () => killMyself ? undefined as any : 'i am alive', // the only way to remove persistent template
    persistent: true, // true by default
});

persistentTemplate.remove() // Unkown method `remove` error + runtime throw!
```

Anyways, I think the docs should cover this `getContents -> undefined` trick and also allow it because for now to remove template `undefined` has to be cast to `any`: `getContents: () => undefined as any`.

### Use case

I am writing a module which packs all separate `.svg` icons into a single `icons-[hash].svg` set.
I create and keep this set file inside Nuxt build directory as template, because I dont want to pollute users project workspace with `.temp` folders and other ugly-looking stuff.

When icons are changed I regenerate set file with new hash so I need a way to delete an old file in order not to pollute Nuxt build directory and create memory leaks.

In general Nuxt build directory is supposed to be the place where Nuxt and modules can store and work with templates.
And if we already have options to create and update templates, even write them as files, I think we need an ability to remove them.

For full control.

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

issues.title: ResourceHints `Link` header in `HTTP 200`
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Adds a [`Link`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Link) header from the renderer to give the browser hints in the `HTTP 200` response of additional resources while downloading / parsing the server response payload. The intention is to decrease page load time by allowing the browser to simultaneously request upcoming resources needed by the DOM before they are identified. 

If the browser or any proxies don't support [`HTTP 103`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/103) Early Hints, then including hints in the later `HTTP 200` still provides early notice. Implementing the feature should hopefully be of minimal operating disruption compared to adopting `HTTP 103` while providing some of the benefits.

Anecdotal evidence suggests that unloaded CSS files are blocking the client side loading of pages until fetched as a subsequent resource in Lighthouse testing. Hints may reduce page load time by reducing the gap between the resource identified and render awaiting resource including JS and CSS.

Feedback and suggestions are welcome!

---

### Example of how it could initially work:
https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/compare/main...IO-Fire:nuxt:feature/write-link-header
Although this implementation appears to only show JS and not styles (test sample size of 1). This may also impact the current `103` early hints feature.

#### SSG Support
Update the route rules' headers for each page before the creating completing the route rendering.
OR
May require changes in the Nitro static presets to encompass the headers being identified at render time rather than at route creation. 

##### Header rule limits
Some hosting providers including Cloudflare Pages have limits on headers.

Cloudflare Pages limits the total number of "header rules" similar to route rules. 

100 pages / routes with headers would use 100 headers rules. This may limit the number of pages within a site without workarounds such as https://github.com/nuxt-modules/security/issues/504#issuecomment-2562018536

### Module Implementation
Module implementation may not be possible as access to the render's data may not be exposed to a module.

Added important edit to last comment. 

Having now tested without network throttling and more powerful hardware the results are minimal potentially may interrupt the browser scheduling by using `prefetch` instead of `preload`, as discussed below.

There may be still an argument for poorer network connectivity like the example image show, such as `HTTP 103` early hints, or where the browser has enough time to schedule the CSS before the parser identifies the resources. Perhaps the [`blocking`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Link#browser_compatibility) parameter (not available in Firefox and Safari) may schedule the resource at the correct `highest` priority instead of just `high`.

Note that the browser (Chromium based) would throw console warnings for `preload` for CSS as it does not count as being used by the window.

Note while it appears multiple network requests are made for the same resource, this appears to only be present on the client side and doesn't show in the logs of HTTP server used.

Firefox appears to ignores the `prefetch` even when the connection is slow, perhaps may consider `preload`.

Performance uplift is available in Chromium based browsers consistently in a test project of at least `10ms` to `30ms` [Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)](https://web.dev/articles/lcp) saving. This is possible without network throttling or CPU throttling, the increase applies to slower hardware / connections too. ### Tests Using a local project, test with headers from the module include and excluded. - Using an empty browser session with no cache, load the page 2 times. - Clear the browser session and cache. - Measure results, repeat for each combination. #### LCP without module: ![LCP 0.88s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7856c924-c4ef-4a82-9c51-6e6764637913) ![LCP 0.88s, Render blocking resources CSS](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bafdb7c-b457-4353-b7f5-c8edf7bc4c04) ##### 3G Network throttling #### LCP with module: ![LCP 0.84s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55a20581-2a52-46d7-aed9-2b43a2b3372d) `30ms` time saving OR ![LCP 0.87](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63a7ee71-3c68-49cc-81b0-632e69adcc26) `10ms` time saving No render blocking resources ##### 3G Network throttling `510ms` time saving ### Conclusion While a `10ms` / `30ms` time saving could be within margin of error, the results are consistent and scale as the network filtering is applied. The Network filtering helps to reduce the reliance on the web server speed for returning resources as the requests are slowed to allow the web server more time to deliver requests. It is recommended that you conduct your own tests before using this module in production.

issues.title: custom Nuxt `crawlLinks` strategy
issues.body:
currently Nitro crawls every scrap of text in the HTML that matches this pattern: `/(?<=\s)href=(?!")["']?([^"'>]+)/g`

This can result in crawling links that aren't links - they may be present in a code block, in a comment, or in a JSON payload. There are also 'external' links that can't/shouldn't be prerendered by Nitro.

Instead, we can support Nuxt taking full control of the crawl links functionality. This is already possible using Nitro hooks. In addition, we could add prerender hints to Nitro whenever a `<NuxtLink>` is rendered that isn't external.

If the team agree, this would be initially rolled out as an experimental behaviour to avoid breaking any reliance on the old behaviour.

issues.body:
### Environment

------------------------------

### Reproduction

## The layer

`nuxt.config.ts`
```ts
import { createResolver } from '@nuxt/kit';

const { resolve } = createResolver(import.meta.url);

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  compatibilityDate: '2024-11-01',
  devtools: { enabled: true },
  alias: {
    '@base': resolve('./'),
  },
})
```

`components/Button.vue`
```vue
<script lang="ts">
import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from 'vue';

// NOTE: relative import works...
import type { Theme } from '../ui/createTheme'; // WORKS

// BUT: using alias causes issues with the type inference (somehow).
// import type { Theme } from '@base/ui/createTheme'; // FAILS WHEN USING REMOTE LAYER SOURCE

export interface ButtonProps extends Theme {
  type?: ButtonHTMLAttributes['type'];
  disabled?: boolean;
}
</script>

<script lang="ts" setup>
withDefaults(defineProps<ButtonProps>(), {
  type: 'button',
});
</script>
```

`ui/createTheme.ts`
```ts
export interface Theme {
  theme?: string;
}
```

## The app

`nuxt.config.ts`
```ts
// https://nuxt.com/docs/api/configuration/nuxt-config
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  compatibilityDate: '2024-11-01',
  devtools: { enabled: true },
  extends: [
    // ['../nuxt-layer-test-layer', { install: true }],
    ['github:leeovery/nuxt-layer-test-layer', { install: true }]
  ],
});
```

`pages/test.vue`
```vue
<template>
  <Button type="submit">hello</Button>
</template>
```

I have setup two simple repos.

The app: https://github.com/leeovery/nuxt-layer-test-app
The layer: https://github.com/leeovery/nuxt-layer-test-layer

If you extend from the layer in the app using the local version, everything works fine, whether you use the alias or a relative path to import the type.

However, if you import the layer using github (which you can do in the app's nuxt.config.ts), then you will see that using the aliases causes the Vue error regarding failing to resolve base type. If you change the import of the theme type in the Button comp. to be a relative path, then all works as expected.

### Describe the bug

The issue appears to be when:

* Using a Nuxt path alias to reference the layer's root dirs,
* then importing a type using that alias,
* then extending from that type to create your prop definition,
* and finally "using" the layer via a remote source. 

Then in the app (extending the later) you will get this overlay error:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/599b3435-1977-454d-94d2-b12c306eb494)

All these things need to be true (it seems) for this bug to occur.

At this stage Im not 100% sure this is a bug or a known limitation. But either way hopefully this will help others later who run into the same issue.

Are we meant to be using aliases like this? Is it a bug?

Thanks!!
Lee

issues.title: Improve Code-Based API Routes in Nitro
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

# 🚀 Improve Code-Based API Routes in Nitro  

## 🧐 Context  

File-based routing in Nitro is great for structuring APIs, but in **large projects**, it can become **tedious**. In some cases, **declaring routes in code** (like H3) is more efficient, especially for:  

- **Generating CRUD APIs** for databases (`GET → fetch`, `POST → insert`, etc.), which gets repetitive with many tables.  
- **Migrating a large number of procedures**: The company where I work has **3,000+ procedures** to migrate to a JS backend, and many could be declared with similar code.  

---

## 🔍 Current Issues  

### ❌ **Problem 1: Code-based routes are not well integrated into Nitro**  
- **Using a plugin** → Routes work but **don’t appear in DevTools**.  
- **Using a catch-all** → Routes are visible but **truncated in DevTools**.  
- **Using `handlers` in `nitro.config`** → Routes are visible but require **pointing to a dummy file**, while still needing a plugin or catch-all to work.  

### ❌ **Problem 2: Missing type inference for `$fetch` and `useFetch`**  
- With file-based routing, **Nuxt automatically generates API types**, a key DX feature.  
- With code-based routes, there’s **no native way** to get proper type inference.  

---

## 💡 Possible Solutions  

✅ **Allow `handlers` to work like `devHandlers`, but in production**  
- Support **passing functions directly** instead of only file paths.  
- Ensure routes are **recognized and visible** in DevTools.  

✅ **Improve type inference for code-based routes**  
- If a route is defined in `handlers`, **Nuxt should infer its return type** for `$fetch` and `useFetch`.  
- Nitro should allow **extending generated types**, just like file-based routing.  

---

## 🎯 Why This Matters  

💡 **Avoid choosing between Nitro and Express**  
- I’ve **twice compared Nitro vs. Express** in a professional setting, and Nuxt/Nitro **could be a more obvious choice** whitout these limitations.  
- With **H3 and Nitro**, all the pieces are there to offer **the best of both worlds**.  

🏢 **Make Nitro scalable for large projects**  
- Right now, Nitro feels **best suited for small projects** due to its strict file-based approach.  
- **Unifying DX** between code-based and file-based routing would **boost adoption in larger companies**.  

---

This is just my perspective—perhaps there are solutions I haven’t considered. I already searched through docs and discussions but I might have missed something.

Thanks for the amazing work on Nuxt, Nitro, H3, Db0 and all this amazing ecosystem! 🚀

issues.title: [nuxt] Add `postcss-preset-env` by default to nuxt
issues.body:
# Intro

This is a discussion to add `postcss-preset-env` by default to Nuxt. It's a great plugin that includes autoprefixer, and by default allows the usage of all stage-2 css features. This would allow Nuxt users to leverage modern css features with 0 configuration.

## Current behaviour

According to the source code, the current behaviour includes `autoprefixer` and `nano` for all bundlers, and then add `postcss-import` and `postcss-url` for the bundlers that needs it (ie vite comes with `postcss-import` but not `postcss-url`).

## Suggested new behaviour

Introduce preset-env as a top level option within postcss with full typescript support: 

```ts
	postcss: {
		env: {
          stage: 2 // default
		},
		plugins: {
			"my-plugin": {
				edition: "2024-02"
			}
		}
	}
```
`postcss-preset-env` is fully typed so we could use their types : https://github.com/csstools/postcss-plugins/blob/main/plugin-packs/postcss-preset-env/src/options.ts

`autoprefixer` could be removed as it's included in `postcss-preset-env` and can be configured [within env](https://github.com/csstools/postcss-plugins/tree/main/plugin-packs/postcss-preset-env#autoprefixer).

Merging with user provided config is very straightforward.

## Additional thoughts

Features: We could allow a wider area of [features](https://preset-env.cssdb.org/features/) by default, for example stage 0 if we want everything, or a high `minimumVendorImplementations` if we want to be more conservative.

Bundle size : postcss-preset-env is [117 KB](https://bundlephobia.com/package/postcss-preset-env@10.1.5), autoprefixer is [55.4KB](https://bundlephobia.com/package/autoprefixer@10.4.21). So this makes the install time slightly slower (The runtime stays the same as `enableClientSidePolyfills` is disabled by [default](https://github.com/csstools/postcss-plugins/tree/main/plugin-packs/postcss-preset-env#enableclientsidepolyfills).

issues.title: Add useLinkAllowlist composable
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/20500

https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/31039

Add a composable to check `href` in `nuxtLink.allowlist` and return a custom rel by `getCustomRel`.

And `allowlist` is default by `nuxt.config/defaults.nuxtLink.allowlist`

And `externalRelAttribute` is  default by `nuxt.config/defaults.nuxtLink.externalRelAttribute`

If `href` in `allowlist`, `getCustomRel` will return the custom `externalRelAttribute`, if not will return the default set by `defaults.nuxtLink.externalRelAttribute`.

```vue
<template>
  <NuxtLink :rel="getCustomRel(href)" to="https://nuxt.com">test</NuxtLink>
</template>
<script setup>
  const { allowlist, checkUrlInAllowlist, getCustomRel } = useLinkAllowlist({
     allowlist: ['nuxt.com', '.nuxt.com'],
     externalRelAttribute: 'noopener'
  })
  // checkUrlInAllowlist('https://nuxt.com') -> true
  // checkUrlInAllowlist('/test') -> false
  // getCustomRel('https://nuxt.com') -> noopener
  // getCustomRel('/test') -> undefined
  // getCustomRel('/test', { force: true }) -> noopener

</script>
```

What do you think? Thank you for your feedback.❤

Currently, it is not possible to resolve a Nuxt route (vue-router) in a Nitro server route when users want to perform a redirect using [`sendRedirect`](https://h3.unjs.io/utils/response#sendredirectevent-location-code), for example.
