I opened #35773 for this and have just closed it. Leaving the useful part here so the next person does not spend the time twice.

Preserving the window scroll whenever only the child page changes looks right until it meets `test/e2e/route-scroll.test.ts`. The `expect scroll to top on nested pages` case guards #20523, and it navigates `/nested/foo/test` → `/nested/foo/user-test` — same parent component, same interpolated parent key. Any "only the child changed" predicate returns true there, so scroll restoration is suppressed and `window.scrollY` never reaches 0. The test then hangs on `waitForFunction` rather than failing, which makes `test-e2e` time out at 25 minutes instead of reporting an assertion, on every platform.

So the two issues want opposite things for the same navigation shape, and the fixture already encodes #20523's side. That matches what @danielroe said above: scrolling the nested element rather than the window is the only version that satisfies both. Whoever picks this up should probably start from the fixture rather than from `scrollBehavior`.

issues.title: Allow per-request app.cdnURL
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

I am building a whitelabel project which runs on independent domain names, such as:
- https://foo.com
- https://bar.com

I want to serve app assets (scripts and styles) from CDNs operating under respective subdomains:
- https://static.foo.com
- https://static.bar.com

I can use Nitro middleware or Nitro `request` hook to override `useRuntimeConfig(event).app.cdnURL` based on request event, with something like:

```ts
// server/middleware/whitelabel.ts
export default defineEventHandler((event) => {
  useRuntimeConfig(event).app.cdnURL = getCdnUrlFromEvent(event)
})
```

Unfortunately, that doesn't affect the app fully. The `__NUXT__` variable is constructed with correct `cdnUrl` and the front-end Nuxt app works correctly, but the initial SSR HTML code uses the global CDN URL.

I figured this is due to `#internal/nuxt/paths` not using `event`, as mentioned in multiple respective TODOs:
https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/da97ec76a953ee10bfdf4ad618f298b66225ef42/packages/nuxt/src/core/runtime/nitro/utils/paths.ts#L18-L23

I didn't find an issue to track progress on this, so I am creating one.

### Workaround

I am aware that I can work around with `{ cdnURL: "__CDN_URL_PLACEHOLDER__" }` in `nuxt.config.ts` and post-process the output HTML within Nitro `render:response` hook, but I believe this deserves proper implementation.

comments.author: ilyaa123
comments.body:
In the current version of Nuxt 4.2.1, when using a static key (for example 'items' or 'programs'), the data inside the callback gets “frozen” after the first execution. On any subsequent refresh() or watch trigger, the same callback is re-executed, but it receives old values from the closure — outdated filter, props, or route parameters.
The useAsyncData key should represent the type of data, not a specific set of parameters. Example:
```
/example/list/[type]
/example/list/[type]?name=SomeName
/example/list/[type]/[item_id]
```
All of these pages logically share the same key 'items', since they deal with the same entity — a list of items. When filters or route params change, the data should simply refresh, not recreate the key.
Right now, to work around the bug, we have to generate dynamic keys like 'items-${type}', which completely breaks the caching logic and makes it meaningless. This leads to cache bloat, prevents data reuse between pages, and causes inconsistencies during SSR hydration.
This issue is quite serious because it directly affects production projects.
It makes it impossible to correctly use key-based caching for filtering or pagination, breaks the predictable behavior of useAsyncData, and ultimately makes it impossible to migrate to Nuxt 4 in real-world projects.
Essentially, this is a blocking bug — it prevents developers from adopting the new directory structure and improved architecture of Nuxt 4 until useAsyncData starts working with up-to-date parameters.

issues.title: Scope of `callOnce`
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

At the moment, [`callOnce`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/call-once) can be used to execute a function once, either "in total" of an app lifecycle (so e.g. once during SSR, never on client, OR once on client, never after) or per navigation.

The current signature looks similar to `useAsyncData` but lacks certain commodities the composable offers, such as:

* `status` (was it called already, is it being called, or was it not yet)
* Manual execution
* etc.

The question is if we should add these so `callOnce` looks similar to `useAsyncData` and userland boilerplate can be avoided or whether we should keep it as minimal as possible

### Describe the feature

[Just like NextJS](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/middleware#conditional-statements), we too should have a way to actually rewrite, not just redirect, our URLs.

Forexample, this is especially handy for multi tenancy, internationalization, and such.

subdomain.test.com/news -> test.com/subdomain/news

So, the actual user sees the URL, but doesnt actually leave / change the original URL

const rootDomain = "test.com"

export default defineNuxtPlugin(async () => {
    const { hostname, path } = useRequestURL();
    const subDomain = hostname.substring(
      0,
      hostname.indexOf(rootDomain ?? "") - 1
    );

   return redirect(event, `/${subdomain}/${path}`)
})
```

issues.title: Simplify Set-Cookie header forwarding
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

At the moment, when using `$fetch` on the server side, cookies that come to the server can only be passed using `useRequestEvent`.

I propose adding a `passCookies` flag to `$fetch` to simplify this functionality.

## The "why"

Currently, many projects use a wrapper over $fetch to set basic settings (for example, the same `baseURL`).

If we consider that the project has a custom fetch (let's call it `customFetch`), which implements add-ons over the basic `$fetch` configuration, then to forward cookies we have to create another method for fetching (let's call it `customFetchWithCookies`), which creates complications in a large code base.

If for each API in the code base you create a separate method with interfaces for request and response parameters, then to forward cookies you will have to create an additional method with the postfix `withCookie`, which will greatly clutter the code base.

If the forwarding of cookies was done through a conditional flag, then this problem could be avoided

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).
issues.author: tokiory

comments.author: cernymatej
comments.body:
You can use `event.$fetch` to forward cookies or other headers like shown here: https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/server#forwarding-context-headers

As for building custom `$fetch` wrappers, it should be already possible to easily implement what you propose. [ofetch](https://github.com/unjs/ofetch) is already very configurable. I think it's best to leave these types of syntactic sugar up to "userland".


Does this answer your questions or is there something else?

comments.author: tokiory
comments.body:
> You can use `event.$fetch` to forward cookies

`event.$fetch` is working in h3 layer (server plugins/middlewares), I'm talking about Nuxt layer (fetching 3rd party api from component). Of course we can use `ofetch.raw` and append headers with h3 methods inside `useAsyncData`, but this is not the best way to implement this feature, since writing additional logic falls on the developer. There is a feeling that it should be "out of the box" functionality.

Also, `event.$fetch` is forwarding headers from _the client to the server_, but in the issue I'm talking about forwarding _server cookies to the client_ ([Set-Cookie is not forwarded to the client, by default](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/data-fetching#pass-cookies-from-server-side-api-calls-on-ssr-response)).

So in this issue we're talking about server Set-Cookie header (`server -> client`), not a client cookies forwarding (`client -> server`)

> [!NOTE]  
> For clarity, in this issue we discuss the use of `$fetch` inside `useAsyncData` for fetching during SSR.
>
> At the moment, we have to write a wrapper in order to implement the functionality of throwing `Set-Cookie` heading from the server to the client.

issues.title: Support _FILE environment variables for loading secrets from files
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

The problem

Many environments like Docker and Kubernetes provide secrets as files (e.g., /run/secrets/xxx). A common convention in these platforms is to define environment variables ending with _FILE, which point to files containing the actual secret values.

Nuxt currently does not support this convention natively.

For example:
`TEST_SECRET_FILE=/run/secrets/app-secret`

Should automatically populate:
`process.env.TEST_SECRET`

with the contents of that file.

This pattern helps securely inject secrets without hardcoding them into the container or needing custom workarounds like entrypoint.sh scripts.

Proposed behavior

Nuxt should support resolving environment variables from files using a _FILE suffix convention. The logic could be:

- For each process.env[KEY + "_FILE"], if the referenced file exists and is readable:
- Populate process.env[KEY] with the file’s contents
- Skip if process.env[KEY] is already explicitly set (i.e., the _FILE version acts as a fallback)

This approach mirrors standard behavior used in Docker Swarm, Kubernetes, and many CI/CD tools. 
The variable names are flexible — either TEST_SECRET or TEST_SECRET_FILE may be used. If both are defined, TEST_SECRET takes precedence and the file-based value is ignored.

The idea also mention [here](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/15366#issuecomment-2858874131).

issues.title: Allow defining defaults for definePageMeta()
issues.body:
## Context 
Using [`definePageMeta()`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/define-page-meta)) with custom key/values

## Problem:
[`definePageMeta()`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/define-page-meta) is super helpful to set (custom) route meta values. [The docs also explain how to type this custom meta data](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/pages#typing-custom-metadata).
_The only point I'm really missing in this concept is being able to define a default / fallback value for page metadata key/values._

For example, when a few pages (login/registration/password reset/...) should not need auth, it would be great to be able to just write:

```
<!-- pages/example.vue -->
<script setup>
definePageMeta({
  // Override value for this page:
 auth: false
})
</script>
```

And set `auth: true` as default somewhere centrally.

Current workaround only seems to be to check the value for _undefined_ and treat it like `true`?

## Related documentation:
- https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/define-page-meta
- https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/pages#page-metadata
- https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/directory-structure/pages#typing-custom-metadata


## Proposed solution:

### a) Define the default(s) in app.vue
```
<!-- app.vue -->
<script setup>
definePageMeta({
 // Define default: auth: true
 auth: true
})
</script>
```

### b) Define the default(s) in nuxt.config:
```
<!-- nuxt.config.ts -->
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  [...],
  app: {
    pageMeta: {
       // Define default: auth: true
      auth: true,
    }
  },
```

### Override the default in single pages:
```
<!-- pages/example.vue -->
<script setup>
definePageMeta({
  // Override value for this page:
 auth: false
})
</script>
```


What do you think about this concept? Or is it already possible and not yet documented (or I'm too blind to find it)?

Thank you!

issues.title: Introduce remote functions
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

The developer experience of calling server endpoints from client code is often still quite bad and lacks in several areas. [Typing is lackluster](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/issues/2758) if it even works and does not run into stack limits of the typescript compiler. Integration with websockets or server-sent events is also not available. Being force the structure ones backend in a REST fashion also is not always favorable for some website designs.

In this context other web frameworks have done great progress making things considerably easier and more developer friendly to use. For sveltekit it's the recently announced ["remote functions" feature](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/discussions/13897) but React/Nuxt (with Server Actions/Functions) or Astro.js (with Form Actions). I think the approach done by sveltekit could fit very well into the Nuxt ecosystem and I would be grateful if we would eventually end up with something similar.

Related to #20649

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body:
A few comments:

> Default slot to allow for customizing how the time is displayed, while re-using the logic.

The way NuxtTime works at the moment is that it runs _outside_ the Vue context, which means that the content of the `<time>` element it produces needs to be controllable purely by props rather than slots

> Refresh relative time at an interval. For example, 5 mins ago would update to 6 mins ago

This would be a nice straightforward improvement.

> Compact appearance for relative time formatting. Example: instead of "5 days ago" show "5d"

I'd prefer we stick with standards and limit ourselves to just what `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` [supports](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat/RelativeTimeFormat). It includes `style: 'short'` and `'narrow'` but I don't think there's a way to output just `5d` for example.

>  For some reason, the "style" prop is not working.

@danielroe What do you think we should do here?

I originally wanted to include a fix for this in my last PR (#32893) but wasn’t sure about the API. My thought is that we’d keep the existing `style` prop for component styling, but then we need to decide how to handle the `style` option for relative time formatting.

issues.title: Consider Support Content Negotiation based on Accept header
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Nuxt currently does not support content negotiation for routes where both API (e.g., JSON-LD for ActivityPub) and HTML (Nuxt page rendering) responses are needed based on the client's Accept header. Middleware in `server/middleware` must not return anything, while event handlers return a value. This makes it difficult to serve both formats from the same route and avoid route duplication.

I would like server route handlers to:
- Return JSON-LD or other content types for API clients (e.g., Accept: application/ld+json)
- If the handler does not return anything or returns undefined, automatically fall back to rendering the corresponding Nuxt page
- Avoid duplicating server and page routes for the same path

Alternatives considered:
- Creating separate API and page routes (leads to duplication and path conflicts)
- Using custom middleware, but this breaks the default event handler model and complicates routing

Example use case: ActivityPub implementation, where `/activities/12345` should return JSON-LD for API requests and HTML for browser requests.

Example code:
```js
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const accept = event.node.req.headers['accept'] || '';
  const wantsJson = accept.includes('application/json') ||
    accept.includes('application/ld+json')
  if (wantsJson) {
    // XXX: fetch the data from the server
    return {
      "@context": ["https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams",
        { "@language": "en-US" }],
      "id": "https://myserver.com/activities/12345",
      "type": "Article",
      "name": "Minimal ActivityPub Activity",
      "content": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.",
    }
  }
})
```

Target Nuxt version: Nuxt 3
Scope: Generic for all content-type negotiation, not limited to ActivityPub.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

issues.title: An option for when to start leave transitions
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

## What I want

Add a option for when to play leave page/layout transitions. Currently, leave transitions are played after all components resolved and initialized. I want to start leave animations for two moments: once the navigation starts, or all components are ready (original behavior).

## Why is it important?

If some of the js chunks are very large or takes a lot of time to load, or a component `await`s network requests in its `setup`, or the network condition is bad, waiting for all components to be ready will take a long time. This is awful for user experience: the user clicked the button/link and nothing happens, causing dead and rage clicks. After a few seconds, the components are ready, and all of a sudden it begins to navigate. This is very confusing and makes the user believe the performance of our website is bad.

I think transition is a great way to balance user experience and network delay, especially with client side navigation like nuxt does. However, waiting for all components ready makes it more like a gorgeous show, not an improvement in user experience.

btw, I am looking for a work around for this, thanks a lot if anyone can help!

issues.title: Easier way to set up a `src` dir in Nuxt 4
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

In Nuxt 3, setting up a `src` directory was easy. By that I mean a directory which contains "all source code" but no configuration files, node_modules, or nuxt.config.ts. By setting the `srcDir` in your `nuxt.config.ts` one was good to go.

With Nuxt 4, the role of the `srcDir` changed: It not only became `app/` by default but also contains only a part of your source code (e.g. no server, modules or layers folder). To achieve the same behavior as in Nuxt 3, one would need more configuration:


```ts
// In your nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  srcDir: 'src/app',
  serverDir: 'src/server',
  dir: {
    public: 'src/public',
    modules: 'src/modules',
    shared: 'src/shared',
  },
})
```

In addition to that, some parts (e.g. the `layers` folder) are not configurable at the moment. Same applies to other folders coming from third party plugins (e.g. `content` from `nuxt/content`).

Time for your thoughts and feedback!

Curious to hear how many of you used a `src` (or differently named) folder in Nuxt 3 and would like to see an easier integration, either via module or via core config option.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [x] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).

- Given the above two, `srcDir` (or `rootDir`) could also be repurposed to specify the root for all top-level folders/files except config, with the default `/`. That way you could set `srcDir` to `src` like before and have the same behavior as in v3. Then you can still use `dir` to customize further relative to `srcDir`.

issues.title: Support trusted domains for `useFetch` to forward headers
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

#### Background

Currently, `useFetch` in Nuxt has different behaviors depending on whether the request is local (relative URL) or external:

* For **same-origin/local requests**, `useFetch` uses `useRequestFetch`, which automatically proxies cookies from the SSR context (great for authentication).
* For **cross-origin requests** (e.g., API hosted on a different subdomain), `useFetch` falls back to `$fetch`, so cookies are **not automatically forwarded**.

Although it's documented behavior, this makes it difficult to use `useFetch` with APIs hosted on **trusted subdomains** (e.g., `api.example.com` vs `www.example.com`) where cookies should still be forwarded.

#### Problem

When frontend is deployed at:

```
www.example.com
```

and a custom backend API is deployed at:

```
api.example.com
```

Using `useFetch('https://api.example.com/...')` does **not** forward cookies automatically, even though:

* Both are trusted subdomains.
* CORS and cookie settings (`SameSite=None; Secure`) are correctly configured.

This breaks SSR auth flows, since session cookies are lost when calling the API.

#### Proposed solution

Add an option in Nuxt configuration to declare **trusted domains** for cookie proxying. For example:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  fetch: {
    trustedDomains: ['https://api.example.com']
  }
})
```

Then, when `useFetch` is called with a URL that matches one of the `trustedDomains`, Nuxt should **force using `useRequestFetch`** (instead of `$fetch`) so cookies are proxied from the request context.

Alternatively, provide a `forceRequestFetch: true` option at callsite, so that users can decide when to use `useRequestFetch`:

```ts
const { data } = await useFetch('https://api.rememo-app.com/user', {
  forceRequestFetch: true
})
```

#### Benefits

* Enables SSR cookie authentication across trusted subdomains.
* Avoids boilerplate workarounds (e.g., manually forwarding cookies, writing custom composables).
* Backwards-compatible (default behavior remains unchanged).
* Gives developers fine-grained control (either global config or per-request).

#### Willing to contribute

I’d be happy to submit a PR for this feature if maintainers agree with the approach.

---

issues.title: Add payload extraction for large data fetched during SSR to avoid rendering in HTML
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

When fetching large amounts of data during server-side rendering, Nuxt currently inlines the payload directly into the rendered HTML. This can cause performance issues for pages that rely on large datasets that can't be scaled down with existing solutions (e.g. `pick`).

For example, we have a page that fetches an OpenAPI Specification (OAS) via a custom `$fetch` client. Since the entire OAS is inlined in the SSR output, the HTML response size can become extremely large (often 1MB or more). This negatively impacts performance by blocking TTFB and forcing the browser to download and parse a much larger HTML document than necessary.

A possible improvement would be to provide an opt-in way to externalize large payloads into a separate file, with the server-rendered HTML referencing it rather than embedding it inline. This would keep the HTML response small, improve TTFB, and still allow hydration to work seamlessly since the payload would be fetched alongside the page.

Ideally, this could be supported regardless of whether the data is fetched with `useAsyncData`, `useFetch`, or a custom `$fetch` client, while remaining optional so that existing behavior continues to work by default.

issues.title: Parallel middlewares
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Seems like an obvious performance win - allow running some, if not all middlewares in parallel for sped up navigation. Middlewares commonly have API calls in them to do access checks etc., and it makes no sense that these are always invoked serially.

I already implemented this in a sort of hacky way in the Nuxt app i'm working on, but it would be better to have a less hacky and officially suported way: https://github.com/specklesystems/speckle-server/pull/5314

Main issue that makes this hacky is:
* Promise.all() all of the pending middlewares throws because useNuxtApp() is undefined in async scopes unless if I turn on `asyncContext` and technically i'm not in middleware scope anymore, which also causes abortNavigation() to throw etc.

Another complication is that there's no easy way to add a 'last' middleware dynamically to all pages - the one that would actually Promise.all() all of the pending middlewares. Global middlewares always occur before named middlewares and none of the build hooks helped me updated middlewares for all pages either.
I did resolve this w/ routeRule middlewares, those seem to be added at the end, but its sort of undefined behaviour that could easily change in the future.

issues.title: [Enhancement] Better Syntax/Convention for Nested Layouts in Nuxt
issues.body: ### Describe the feature ### Context Currently, Nuxt supports layouts via the `layouts/` directory and supports nested UI sections using **nested routes** (e.g., `pages/profile.vue` wrapping `pages/profile/favorite.vue`). While this works, once the project grows with many folders and files, the pattern of mixing `parent.vue` (used as a wrapper) alongside actual child routes can get confusing and lose context. For example: ``` pages/ ├─ profile.vue // Parent layout wrapper └─ profile/ ├─ index.vue // Child route └─ favorite.vue // Child route ``` Here, `profile.vue` is conceptually acting as a **nested layout**, but it is treated as a page, which can make code organization less clear. ### Problem * `parent.vue` files inside `pages/` double as both “layout” and “page,” which can blur their purpose. * As the folder structure deepens, it becomes harder to distinguish what is a layout wrapper and what is an actual page. * The developer has to “remember” which `.vue` file is serving as a pseudo-layout. ### Proposal / Suggestion Introduce a **dedicated convention** for nested layouts within route groups. For example: ``` pages/ └─ profile/ ├─ @layout.vue // Explicitly marks this as the wrapper layout ├─ index.vue // Child route └─ favorite.vue // Child route ``` Usage: ```vue ``` This improves clarity by: * Explicitly distinguishing **nested layout files** from **page files**. * Avoiding the overloaded role of `parent.vue`. * Making folder structures self-explanatory. ### Benefits * More intuitive project structure for large apps. * Easier onboarding for new developers (clear separation of layouts vs. pages). * Cleaner, scalable convention that aligns with the mental model of “global layouts” vs. “section layouts.” ### Additional information - [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature? - [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module? ### Final checks - [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution). - [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

issues.title: Group nested pages
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

As a developer working with Nuxt auto-generated router from `pages/` directory, I am tired of creating "intermediary" pages for the nested routes. What I mean is, if I have pages:
- `pages/posts/index.vue`
- `pages/posts/[id].vue`

then these page are not "grouped" into a single router tree node, and `<nuxt-link to="/posts">` is not marked as "active" when user is viewing the page `/posts/123` (which is a subtle bug which may be long staying unnoticed).

To overcome this, one needs not to forget to create `pages/posts.vue` with a single `<nuxt-page/>` in it:

```vue
<!-- for vue-router to group child pages -->

<template lang="pug">
nuxt-page
</template>
```

In a deeply nested pages structure, a solid portion of my files are these groupers.

What I propose is, add a `nuxt.config.ts` setting that will inject these "intermediary" grouping components automatically, something like:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  pages: {
    groupNestedPages: true // should use better name
  }
})
```

Granted, this can be implemented as an external module, but then the router generator itself can be implemented as a module, yet it's built-in.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [x] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).
issues.author: IlyaSemenov

comments.author: IlyaSemenov
comments.body:
I was just thinking, that sometimes this behavior is — on the contrary — not desirable. A single "all or nothing" flag does not always fit. Ideally, the grouping/ungrouping should be additionally configurable on per-route level:

```ts
definePageMeta({
  groupWithParent: false, // should use better naming
})
```

Example use case:

- `pages/orgs.vue`
- `pages/orgs/index.vue`
- `pages/orgs/create.vue`
- `pages/orgs/import.vue`
- `pages/orgs/[id].vue`

I would like to be able to group the first 3 nested pages (`/orgs`, `/orgs/create` and `/orgs/import`) under the common parent. However, the `/orgs/:id` should be able to be excluded from the group and have its own root (or rather, grandparent's) route record, even though sharing the URL prefix.

The reason for that is being able to provide the shared UI (e.g. navigation tabs) in `orgs.vue` for some nested pages, but allow to opt-out for others.

Perhaps this be achieved using a different directory and providing a custom `definePageMeta({ path })` but even if it's possible, it's less convenient.

comments.author: Flo0806
comments.body:
1. When a package is pre-built with Vite, the `?worker` import is compiled to a hardcoded path like `new Worker('/assets/worker-XXX.js')`
2. In Nuxt dev mode, this asset file exists in `node_modules/{package}/dist/assets/` but Vite/Nuxt doesn't know to serve it
3. The request gets intercepted by Vue Router, which returns a 404 or serves it with incorrect MIME type

### My idea to solve this: 

Add middleware in `packages/vite/src/plugins/dev-server.ts` to serve worker assets directly from `node_modules:`
1. Intercepts requests for worker JavaScript files (paths containing `worker` and ending in `.js`)
2. Searches through `node_modules` directories to locate the worker asset file
3. Serves the file directly with the correct `application/javascript` MIME type

This middleware needs to run early in the request chain (before Vue Router and other handlers) to properly intercept and handle worker requests.

I don't know, but that feels wrong (?). Should I try it that way? @danielroe

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body: could that folder be added to nitro's publicAssets array? then nitro would handle serving it.

comments.author: Flo0806
comments.body:
The challenge with `publicAssets` is that it's configured statically at build time, but we don't know which packages will have workers until runtime.
We'd need to:
- Scan all installed packages
- Find which ones contain worker assets
- Add each to `publicAssets` dynamically

The middleware approach is simpler because it:
- Discovers worker files on-demand
- Works with any package structure
- Requires no configuration from users

That said, if there's a good way to populate publicAssets dynamically during dev server init, that could work too!

issues.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: `Darwin`
- Node Version:     `v20.19.1`
- Nuxt Version:     `3.19.1`
- CLI Version:      `3.28.0`
- Nitro Version:    `2.12.5`
- Package Manager:  `npm@11.3.0`
- Builder:          `-`
- User Config:      `-`
- Runtime Modules:  `-`
- Build Modules:    `-`

### Reproduction

1. Enable prerendering for pages either with `npm run generate` or `npm run build` and using `routeRules` in the Nuxt config to enable it for some pages.
2. Deploy the app and open the website on, say, 1 PM and keep the session open.
3. Make huge changes on the code structure of a prerendered page.
4. Deploy the app again on, say, 1:30 PM.
5. After the deployment, return to the session you'd previously opened and "internally navigate" to the mentioned page.
6. Assuming the old `_payload.json` file hasn't been cached, you'd get a "new" `_payload.json` file on an old deployment which is not compatible with the new payload structure and you'd potentially end up on a broken page or otherwise broken content.




### Describe the bug

The `_payload.json` file contains the payload required for rendering in the page. The structure of it depends on the page's architecture and code. This file gets shipped with this URL structure:

`https://something.com/some-path/_payload.json?793f23f3-d5fe-44e3-b045-4b10ab949322 `

The file's "path" remains the same with every build and only the query param changes. This means that old clients who haven't refreshed their sessions after deployments still need to get the old `_payload.json` files but the old file has already been replaced with the new one. This could result in broken pages if the structure of the page changes.

### Additional context

In Nuxt 2, the equivalent `payload.js` files had build-time timestamps in their URLs which kept deployments graceful:

`https://something.com/_nuxt/static/1762158826/some-path/payload.js`

A similar approach could solve the issue in my opinion.

comments.author: sadeghi-aa
comments.body:
So I got an update for this issue. I changed `app.cdnUrl` in the Nuxt config to `/builds/<some-unique-id>`. As a result, all CSS and JS files (including _payload.json files) were prefixed with that subdirectory. This already solves several skew issues but I still faced two other issues:


1. The node server doesn't seem to be able to answer _payload.json requests when prefixed with a non-empty `app.cdnUrl`. For example:

`https://somedomain.com/builds/123456/some-route/_payload.json`

for an SWR-enabled route would reach the node server for response to which it responds with a 404 error.


2. I fixed the above issue with an nginx location block that cuts the prefix before passing it to the node server, but there's some other kind of skew that could happen. When navigating from a page to an SSR/SWR page, Nuxt needs to fetch the _payload.json file directly from the node server since that file doesn't really exist on the disk. If you happen to have only one node server, you'll always serve new payloads to both old and new clients. I'm not sure if a solution could be proposed for this though. Only Vercel-like architectures for deployment - where there are multiple node server from different versions - could actually prevent such skews. Caching could of course reduce the chance of skew by serving the old payloads but that's only in case a request was made for that file before the new deployment.

Any ideas?

issues.title: Public asset paths are inconsistent in server context (`new URL(..., import.meta.url)` and `useStorage('assets:*')` do not resolve real paths after build)
issues.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: Linux
- Node Version:     v20.19.5
- Nuxt Version:     4.2.1
- CLI Version:      3.30.0
- Nitro Version:    2.12.9
- Package Manager:  bun@1.3.2


### Reproduction

Minimal reproduction:

```ts
// server/utils/watermark.ts
// Expected: get real filesystem path to an image from /public folder
// for use with sharp/jimp/etc.

const watermarkPath = new URL('../../../public/assets/images/logo_www_square_shadow_dark-xs.png', import.meta.url).pathname
console.log('watermarkPath:', watermarkPath)
```

**Result:**
✅ Works in dev
❌ Breaks after build — the relative path no longer matches because of output structure differences.

Also tried using Nitro storage API:

```ts
await useStorage('assets:server').getMeta('assets/images/logo_www_square_shadow_dark-xs.png')?.path
await useStorage('assets:public').getMeta('assets/images/logo_www_square_shadow_dark-xs.png')?.path
```

Both return `undefined` or no valid `.path` property, even though `public/` is part of the Nitro storage tree.

### Describe the bug

There’s currently **no reliable way** to get the *real file system path* (not the URL) to a file inside the `public/` folder from server code.

* `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` breaks because relative structure changes between dev and build output.
* `useStorage('assets:server' | 'assets:public')` doesn’t resolve or expose a real path, though it should since `public/` is part of Nitro’s virtual storage.

This makes it difficult to pass asset paths to server libraries like **sharp**, **jimp**, or other tools that need actual file system access.

---

### **Expected behavior**

There should be a documented, framework-supported way to resolve the real (absolute) file path to a file in `public/` from server-side code.

Something like:

```ts
import { resolvePublicPath } from '#internal/nuxt' // hypothetical helper
const absPath = resolvePublicPath('assets/images/logo.png')
```

---

### **Workaround**

Currently, I’m using a temporary helper to handle this:

```ts
import { join } from 'node:path'

export function resolvePublicPath(relativePath: string) {
  const publicDir = import.meta.dev
    ? join(process.cwd(), './public')
    : join(process.cwd(), '../public')

  return join(publicDir, relativePath)
}
```

It works, but it’s fragile and depends on internal directory layout — ideally, Nuxt should expose a runtime-safe, documented utility for this.

### Additional context

* The docs currently explain how to **reference** public files via URLs, but not how to **resolve their real file system paths** for use on the server.
* This is important for SSR-side processing, image manipulation, watermarking, etc.
* Suggestion: add an API or helper (or `useRuntimeConfig().paths.publicDir`) and a docs section covering this use case.

comments.author: moshetanzer
comments.body:
Hey Team,

This is what i have done in the meantime - in case anyone would benefit:

```
export function useExtendedRuntimeConfig<T = string>(camelKey: string): T | undefined {
  const runtime = typeof useRuntimeConfig === 'function'
    ? useRuntimeConfig()
    : undefined

  if (runtime && camelKey in runtime) {
    return runtime[camelKey] as T
  }

  const envKey = `NUXT_${camelKey.replace(/([A-Z])/g, '_$1').toUpperCase()}`
  return process.env[envKey] as T | undefined
}
```
Wasnt sure how to get type safety working properly (not sure if it is even possible in user land becuase runtime.d.ts isnt generated), therefore also just stuck with passing it as an option to function.

Cheers

cc @danielroe @huang-julien

issues.title: Feature Request / Discussion: Route Masking Support (Modal Routes)
issues.body:
### Modal Routes

TanStack Router provides [route masking](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/framework/react/guide/route-masking) as a first-class feature, allowing a URL to represent one route while rendering another (commonly used for modal routes).

However, Vue Router does not currently offer an official or ergonomic equivalent.

While similar behavior can be achieved using state and navigation guards, this approach:

- Is not well-documented
- Requires manual abstractions
- Is effectively incompatible with Nuxt file-based routing

Vue Router has an internal E2E example demonstrating modal routing via history state:

https://github.com/vuejs/router/blob/main/packages/router/e2e/modal/index.ts

I am wondering Nuxt could provide an abstraction that makes this pattern easier and more ergonomic to use.

more context:

https://x.com/danielcroe/status/2003110312879542563

cc @danielroe

comments.body:
Hello :wave: 
I don't think it is a good idea to have vue component as SPA loaders. The idea of it is to have something that is **bare minimal** so it doesn't bloat your browser's SPA load. It shouldn't have any dependency to your application because it is its purpose to load immediatly while your application is loading in your browser, which means importing vue and all different javascript chunks to load your applicaiton. 
If your spa loader includes js dependencies, it means that theses dependencies needs to be loaded before loading your SPA.

issues.title: Feature Request: More nuxt way to extend vue.compilerOptions.isCustomElement
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Currently the only way to change this option is to replace the function.

If a module replaces the function it breaks other modules and even the user's own function if they set it. This can be very hard to debug. I think having them wrap the function might work but I'm not sure what would happen with multiple modules doing it. Currently all modules I've seen use this function just set it directly. I have to patch them all.

Less needed, but if a layer tries to set the option but the user already set it, it **can't** override it or extend it in any way. 

All of this is very error prone, non-obvious, and very hard to debug.

I propose some new option that is just an array of names/functions. So layers can extend it, and for modules it's more obvious they should push to it. Then nuxt can handle actually calling isCustomElement unless the user sets it. If a config contains both options, a warning can be emitted. 

Alternatively a helper for modules `addCustomVueComponent` or something like that.

comments.author: onmax
comments.body:
The build failure is caused by `@nuxt/icon` (a dependency of `@nuxt/ui`) which uses `#imports` in its server code.

**Why it worked in 4.2 but breaks in 4.3:**

The `nitroAutoImports` option was [added in 4.3](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/c4f46c641). In 4.2, server auto-imports were always enabled. In 4.3+, when `compatibilityVersion >= 5`, `nitroAutoImports` defaults to `false`, which means the `#imports` file is not generated for Nitro. Modules using `#imports` in server code will fail.

**Workaround:**

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  future: { compatibilityVersion: 5 },
  experimental: { nitroAutoImports: true }
})
```

**Long-term fix:** Modules like `@nuxt/icon` need to be updated to use explicit imports (e.g., `import { ... } from 'h3'`) instead of `#imports` for v5 compatibility.

comments.author: jd-solanki
comments.body:
Still reproduces on 4.6.0 and on nightly `4.6.0-2610091445-242e197`, and it reaches beyond `defineAppConfig`.

Reproduction: https://github.com/jd-solanki/reproductions/tree/nuxt-compat5-nitro2-drops-shared-auto-imports--2026-10-10 (`pnpm install && pnpm test`)

With `future.compatibilityVersion: 5` on Nitro 2, a server route that imports its helpers from `nuxt/server` still loses:

- a `shared/utils` export: `ReferenceError: greet is not defined`
- `defineAppConfig`, once server code reads the app config through `useAppConfig(event)`: `ReferenceError: defineAppConfig is not defined`

Both pass with `experimental.nitroAutoImports: true`. With it off, `@nuxt/nitro-server` passes Nitro `imports: false`, which drops the `shared/` dirs and `defineAppConfig` along with h3's helpers. The Nuxt 5 upgrade guide says "Your own exports from `server/utils/` and `shared/utils/` are still auto-imported", which doesn't hold on Nuxt 4.

issues.title: Consider adding onBeforeUnmount(done) to NuxtLayout for deferHydration consistency
issues.body:
PR #34152 added `onBeforeUnmount(done)` to `NuxtPage` to ensure `deferHydration` callback fires when the component unmounts before Suspense resolves (e.g., during layout navigation).

## Question

`NuxtLayout` also calls `deferHydration()` at line 79 in `packages/nuxt/src/app/components/nuxt-layout.ts` but doesn't have the same `onBeforeUnmount(done)` pattern.

Should it? The same edge case might occur if a layout unmounts before its Suspense resolves.

## Considerations

- Layout's Suspense is the parent of page's Suspense, so lifecycle timing differs
- The bug in #30291 specifically affected page components during layout changes
- This might be intentional, or it might be a gap

issues.body:
### Environment

| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| **Operating system** | `Windows 10.0.26200`                        |
| **CPU**              | `Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155U (14 cores)` |

| **Modules**          | `-`                                         |


### Reproduction

https://github.com/jaxoncrosmas/nuxi-typecheck-ambient-declaration-bug

### Describe the bug

When using ambient type declarations (`.d.ts` files) in `server/types/`, `nuxi typecheck` throws `TS2304: Cannot find name 'X'` despite the files being correctly included in the TypeScript compilation. Running `vue-tsc` directly produces no errors.

### Additional context

The following commands produce no errors:
```bash
npx vue-tsc --noEmit
npx vue-tsc --project .nuxt/tsconfig.server.json --noEmit
```

However, running `nuxi typecheck` results in an error:
```bash
# TS2304: Cannot find name 'AuthenticatedUser'
npx nuxi typecheck
```

The VS Code language server also resolves the types correctly.

The generated `tsconfig` files are correctly configured. `tsconfig.app.json` explicitly excludes the `server/` directory:
```json
"exclude": ["../server"]
```

And `tsconfig.server.json` explicitly includes it:
```json
"include": ["../server/**/*"]
```

Running `vue-tsc --project .nuxt/tsconfig.server.json --listFiles` confirms that `server/types/AuthenticatedUser.d.ts` is included in the server compilation. Despite this, `nuxi typecheck` fails to resolve the ambient declaration while `vue-tsc --project .nuxt/tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` run directly produces no errors.

comments.author: dusta
comments.body: @cernymatej Maybe I’ll elaborate on my point a bit. We don’t use Nuxt JS features like NuxtLink or useFetch that are built into the framework. We do use JS, but in forms like slider animations or adding a product to the cart. However, we don’t use JS for "core functionality." For search queries, we use classic JS that sends XHR requests and returns HTML. Since the content is prerendered and we only append it afterwards, we can cache these requests on other servers. That’s why noScript is a good solution, but it would be great to have a way for fetch requests to not be included in __NUXT_DATA__ and still work as static content under SSR, and not and it won't completely disable JS ```js const contectWithHydration = await useAsyncData ... const staticHtmlBlockDontIncludedTo__NUXT_DATA__ = await useFetchSSR... // no hydration ``` Imagine that each page has a block showing product details. Why would I need to hydrate this block if it’s purely static content? The same applies to many other parts of a page that don’t require interactivity, such as: -Product descriptions -Images -Specifications The system is so large that the backend isn’t hosted on a single address. Sometimes this data shouldn’t be added to __NUXT_DATA__. For example, we might need the supplier ID for terms and conditions, but we don’t want it to be public. Currently, the code includes it in __NUXT_DATA__, which makes supplier IDs and names visible in "View Source". The first random example from your website. Not everyone wants such data in a ‘friendly grabbing’ format. JSON can be exposed from a response even without making a client-side request on the website. And let’s add information that should only be considered ‘technical data,’ such as the promotion end date (which we don’t want to show to the customer) or the number of remaining products. Of course, it’s possible to work around this by making requests like whether the promotion is still active or whether a product is available. **But as I mentioned, when it comes to TB of data, this is not a good idea**.

comments.body:
@dusta 
To me, it looks like you're trying to fight Nuxt's hybrid rendering strategy. I see the feature request as more of a “disable client-side routing” request. It's still not very clear to me what benefits you see in that, though.

You can currently either make your pages completely javascript free using `noScripts`, or you should make sure that they work during client-side navigation as well -> meaning they need to be properly hydrated. > some data need to be used for conditions but should not be visible to the user

Keep in mind that security by obscurity is absolutely pointless. Whether the data is in the `__NUXT_DATA__` script element or in the JS chunks, it is still accessible to the user.

@codeflorist the rationale is:
- you cannot respect a route query when prerendering a page - it's not possible to store `/thing?sort=asc` and `/thing?sort=desc` separately on the server.
- therefore the HTML of any page is prerendered _with an empty query_ (and always has been)
- therefore if we have a query string visible on the client when hydrating, it will break hydration
- therefore we hydrate on a route without query and then once hydrated, we push to the query rendered on the client

this is only true for prerendered pages.

ideally I would have it already 'present' again in `onMounted`, leaving only the hydration stage without the query.

comments.body:
We are seeing this in a production app as well, on a prerendered technical redirect route.

I understand why the prerendered HTML/payload has to be queryless: a static route cannot store separate HTML for `/thing?sort=asc` and `/thing?sort=desc`, and hydrating immediately against the browser query can cause hydration mismatches.

The issue for us is the timing of when the browser route is restored.

The route is opened as:

`/redirect?waitingForRedirect=true`

The page component reads `useRoute().query` during initial client setup to decide whether it should wait for a cross-window redirect handshake or close itself. With Nuxt 4.4.x, that initial setup sees the prerendered payload route instead of the actual browser URL:

```json
{
  "fullPath": "/redirect",
  "query": {},
  "browserHref": "https://example.test/redirect",
  "browserSearch": ""
}
```

Later, after Nuxt finishes hydration, the route is corrected:

```json
{
  "fullPath": "/redirect?waitingForRedirect=true",
  "query": {
    "waitingForRedirect": "true"
  },
  "browserHref": "https://example.test/redirect?waitingForRedirect=true",
  "browserSearch": "?waitingForRedirect=true"
}
```

So for us this is not about expecting the prerendered HTML to include query-specific state. The problem is that application code running during initial `script setup` can observe the temporary queryless payload route and make an irreversible decision before the browser route is restored.

One additional debugging observation: during that initial phase, `window.location.search` can also reflect the temporary queryless route. The originally requested URL was still visible via `performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].name`, but that feels more like a browser-level escape hatch than a Nuxt API.

A route-specific workaround that works for our case is:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  routeRules: {
    '/redirect': { ssr: false },
  },
})
```

This turns the technical route into a static client entry (`data-ssr="false"`) and avoids the deferred prerender hydration path for this route, without disabling SSR/prerendering globally.

Ideally, Nuxt would either restore the browser route before application setup/mount logic can make one-shot decisions, or provide/document a supported way to access the original requested client URL during prerender hydration.

## Description
When viewTransition is enabled, there is a synchronization gap between route change and DOM hydration for asynchronous data. Even when using top-level await with useAsyncData (or useSanityQuery), the View Transition API is unable to match view-transition-named objects in the DOM between each view.

Enable: { viewTransition: true } in nuxt.config.ts.

Create a List Page where elements have a unique view-transition-name 

Create a Detail Page that uses await useAsyncData (or useSanityQuery) to fetch content based on the route parameter.

Assign the same view-transition-name to an element on the Detail Page.

Navigate from the List Page to the Detail Page.

## Expected Behaviour
The browser should "hold" the transition until the await in the Page Component is resolved and the resulting DOM is painted, allowing for a smooth transition between matching names.

## Actual Behaviour
No visible view transition occurs

issues.title: routeRules cache with single wildcard pattern (`/:a/page`) breaks `_payload.json`
issues.body:
### Environment

  - Nuxt: 4.4.2                                                                                                     
  - Nitro: 2.13.2
  - Vue: 3.5.31                                                                                                     
  - Node: v25.6.1                                                 
  - OS: macOS 25.3.0    
  


### Reproduction

- https://stackblitz.com/github/maxmalysh/nuxt-route-rules-payload-bug
- https://github.com/maxmalysh/nuxt-route-rules-payload-bug


### Describe the bug

When a `routeRules` entry uses a pattern with **one** dynamic segment followed by a static segment (e.g. `/:slug/about`), client-side navigation to that route produces Vue Router warnings — the `_payload.json` request gets no match and the page either 404s or falls back to a full reload.
                                                                                                                    
The **exact same** cache config with **two** dynamic segments before the static segment (e.g. `/:locale/:slug/about`) works correctly.
                                                                                                                    
  ```ts                                                                                                             
  routeRules: {
    // ❌ _payload.json 404 on client-side navigation                                                               
    '/:slug/about': { cache: { swr: true, maxAge: 180, staleMaxAge: 28800 } },                                      
                                                                                                                    
    // ✅ works fine                                                                                                
    '/:locale/:slug/about': { cache: { swr: true, maxAge: 180, staleMaxAge: 28800 } },                              
  }                                                                                                                 
  ```
                                                                                                                    
  **Steps:**                                                      
  1. Run the minimal reproduction
  2. Open `/`, click "Travel — About" (uses `/:slug/about`) → console warnings:                                     
  ```                                                                                                               
  [Vue Router warn]: No match found for location with path "/travel/about/_payload.json"                            
  ```                                                                                                               
  3. Go back, click "EN / Travel — About" (uses `/:locale/:slug/about`) → works, no warnings
                                                                                                                    
  **Expected:** `/:slug/about` should handle `_payload.json` the same way `/:locale/:slug/about` does.              
       

### Additional context

The pattern `/:param/static` seems to be mishandled when Nuxt/Nitro resolves the `_payload.json` path for cached routes.                                                                                            
                                                                  
Literal routes (e.g. `/travel/about` instead of `/:slug/about`) don't have this problem.                          
                                                                    
This makes `routeRules` cache almost unusable with `@nuxtjs/i18n` (`prefix_and_default` strategy). The default locale has no prefix, so routes like `/:slug/about` hit the bug. The prefixed locale variants (`/:locale/:slug/about`) work fine — meaning the same page is broken in one language and works in all others. You end up having to either drop caching for default-locale routes or list every slug literally (and this is not possible for 20 languages X 20 categories X 20 pages).

### Logs

```shell-script
[16:17:37]  WARN  [Vue Router warn]: No match found for location with path "/travel/about/_payload.json"
[16:17:37]  WARN  [Vue Router warn]: No match found for location with path "/cooking/about/_payload.json?1774613857331"
```

issues.title: Array support for layouts in definePageMeta
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Regarding the current implementation of `definePageMeta`, the `layout` property is restricted to a single string. While this works for simple use cases, achieving nested or stacked layouts currently requires developers to manually wrap page content with `<NuxtLayout>` components inside the page template. 

In large-scale projects, this manual nesting leads to repetitive boilerplate and makes layout composition difficult to manage across various routes. The proposal is to enable array support for the `layout` property to allow declarative layout stacking, similar to how `middleware` is handled:

```ts
definePageMeta({
  layout: ['base-theme', 'dashboard-sidebar']
})
```

With this support, Nuxt would wrap the page content sequentially based on the array order. The first layout in the array would become the outermost wrapper, and subsequent layouts would be injected into the default slot of the previous one. 

This change would reduce template clutter and offer a more scalable, native way to manage nested layout structures without needing to manually manage them in every single file.

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

### Final checks

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/community/contribution).
- [x] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

comments.body:
I feel that this is a very specific use case you have here and makes it harder to understand that layouts could be an array.

`middleware` makes sense as you want more or less security layers for a page (`auth` + `admin` for instance)

But I have trouble finding a use case as the `base-theme` could just be in `app.vue` right?

comments.body: the `layout` also supports `{ name?: LayoutKey | false; props?: Record<string, unknown> /* or the selected layout's props */ }` this way you could pass props to your layout

comments.author: hanzydev
comments.body:
> I feel that this is a very specific use case you have here and makes it harder to understand that layouts could be an array.
> 
> `middleware` makes sense as you want more or less security layers for a page (`auth` + `admin` for instance)
> 
> But I have trouble finding a use case as the `base-theme` could just be in `app.vue` right?

Fair point! However, the main reason `app.vue` isn't always the solution is that not every page shares the same 'base' structure. 

In a large-scale SaaS or a multi-portal application, you might have:
- **Marketing pages** that need a `landing-base` (Header/Footer).
- **Admin pages** that need a `dashboard-base` (Sidebar/Topbar).
- **Auth pages** that need a `minimal-base` (Centered box).

If we put the 'base' in `app.vue`, we end up with complex conditional logic (`v-if`) inside `app.vue` to decide which base to show.

The real benefit of array support in `layout` shows up when you have **nested sub-layouts**. For example, in a dashboard:
- Some pages: `layout: ['admin', 'settings-sidebar']`
- Other pages: `layout: ['admin', 'inventory-sidebar']`

Currently, we have to manually wrap every single page template with `<NuxtLayout name="settings-sidebar">`. If I have 20 settings pages, I have to repeat this 20 times. If the layout structure changes later, I have to update all 20 files.

By allowing an array in `definePageMeta`, we keep the page templates clean and manage the UI hierarchy purely through metadata, just like we do with `middleware`. It's not about security layers, it's about **UI composition layers**.

comments.author: hanzydev
comments.body:
> the `layout` also supports `{ name?: LayoutKey | false; props?: Record<string, unknown> /* or the selected layout's props */ }` this way you could pass props to your layout

That’s a great point! The object support is indeed very powerful for parameterizing a single layout. However, the proposal for array support addresses a different architectural need: **UI Composition (Nesting)** rather than just **Parameterization**.

While the current object format allows us to pass props to *one* layout, it doesn't solve the issue of stacking multiple layouts (e.g., a `base-theme` wrapper AND a `dashboard-sidebar` wrapper) without returning to manual nesting inside the page template.

Ideally, array support could even embrace this object format to provide the best of both worlds:

```ts
definePageMeta({
  layout: [
    { name: 'base-theme', props: { theme: 'dark' } },
    'dashboard-sidebar'
  ]
})
```

This would allow developers to manage both the hierarchy and the configuration of the entire layout stack natively within `definePageMeta`. The goal is to make **composition** as seamless as **parameterization** currently is.

issues.title: Add 'relative-parts' prop to <NuxtTime> for compact relative time output
issues.body:
### Description

When using `<NuxtTime>` with `relative` and `relative-style="narrow"`, the output includes the literal suffix (e.g., "5m ago", "2h ago", "14y ago"). There's currently no way to get just the value and unit without the directional literal (e.g., "5m", "2h", "14y").

This compact format is common in social UIs (Reddit, Twitter/X, YouTube, GitHub) where timestamps appear inline next to usernames and space is tight.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `relative-parts` prop (or `relativeParts`) that, when set, uses `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.formatToParts()` instead of `.format()` and filters the output to only include the `integer` and `unit` parts:

```vue
<!-- Current: outputs "14y ago" -->
<NuxtTime :datetime="oldDate" relative relative-style="narrow" />

<!-- Proposed: outputs "14y" -->
<NuxtTime :datetime="oldDate" relative relative-style="narrow" relative-parts="value" />
```

### Implementation

The change is minimal. In the `formattedDate` computed (and the corresponding `onPrehydrate` script), when `relativeParts` is set, replace:

```js
return formatter.value.format(Math.round(value), unit)
```

with:

```js
const parts = formatter.value.formatToParts(Math.round(value), unit)
return parts
  .filter(part => part.type === 'integer' || part.type === 'unit')
  .map(part => part.value)
  .join('')
```

This uses the standard `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.formatToParts()` API, which returns typed parts like:

```js
// formatToParts(-14, 'year') with style: 'narrow'
[
  { type: 'integer', value: '14' },
  { type: 'literal', value: ' ' },   // ← filtered out
  { type: 'unit', value: 'y' },
  { type: 'literal', value: ' ago' } // ← filtered out
]
```

### Alternatives Considered

- **Default slot override**: `NuxtTime` doesn't expose a slot for custom rendering
- **Custom component**: Works but loses the hydration-safe `onPrehydrate` behavior that `NuxtTime` provides
- **CSS `text-overflow`**: Can't selectively hide " ago" without also hiding the unit

### Additional Context

| Style | `format()` | `formatToParts()` filtered |
|-------|-----------|---------------------------|
| `narrow` | "14y ago" | "14y" |
| `short` | "14 yr. ago" | "14yr." |
| `long` | "14 years ago" | "14years" |

The `narrow` + filtered combination produces the most useful compact output.

Related:
https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/32478


### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

comments.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated reply by CodeRabbit -->
`@spencerwalsh651-cmyk`, thanks for sharing your experience! I had already replied with general troubleshooting steps, but here are some more targeted findings for the two specific issues you're seeing:

---

### Types Not Recognised

There is a known Nuxt 4 issue where `defineNuxtConfig` types are missing in layers added in the `extends` array that are **not** inside the expected `layers` directory which Nuxt currently scans.

A couple of things to check:

1. **Explicit imports workaround** — Adding `imports: { imports: [{ from: 'nuxt/config', name: 'defineNuxtConfig' }] }` to your config can solve the missing types issue.

2. **Auto imports config errors** — A misconfigured auto imports entry (e.g. using `typeFrom` incorrectly) can silently prevent types from all layers from being generated. Check your dev server output for any `ERROR Could not compile template types/imports.d.ts` messages, as that's a telltale sign.

3. **Layer placement** — By default, any layers within your project in the `~/layers` directory will be automatically registered as layers in your project, which also ensures TypeScript picks them up properly.

4. **Relative paths in layer config** — When using relative paths in a layer's `nuxt.config` file, they are resolved relative to the user's project instead of the layer. As a workaround, use fully resolved paths using `fileURLToPath` and `dirname`.

---

### Inconsistent HMR

There have been several improvements and fixes related to HMR in Nuxt v4, especially around layers. However, some users have still reported issues with HMR not working as expected within layers after upgrading.

If your layers are dependencies in `node_modules`, be aware that HMR and aliasing may not work perfectly due to current limitations.

---

Could you confirm whether your layers live inside `~/layers/` or are referenced via a relative path in `extends`? That detail, combined with your Nuxt version, would help narrow down whether you're hitting `#32980` or a separate issue.

})

issues.title: Memory usage during `nuxt build`
issues.body:
## Description

I'm running into frequent memory issues (OOM) during `nuxt build` across multiple projects.

Increasing `--max-old-space-size` usually resolves it, but it raises a more fundamental question: **what is the expected memory footprint for a Nuxt build?**

At the moment, it’s unclear what is “normal” vs. a sign of a misconfiguration or underlying issue.

## Observations
* Fresh Nuxt project (minimal setup, only `@nuxt/ui`)
  * Peak memory usage: ~3.5–4 GB
* Larger project:
  * Server + client source maps enabled
  * Prerendering thousands of routes
  * Peak memory usage: 12+ GB
* Runtime memory usage (after build) is relatively low in comparison
* On typical infrastructure (e.g. 8 GB RAM servers), builds can fail due to OOM

## What I’ve found so far
There are multiple issues and discussions related to high memory usage, often tied to:
* Vite / Rollup internals
* Source maps
* Large prerender workloads

However, I haven't found clear guidance on:
* Expected baseline memory usage
* How memory scales with project size/features
* Recommended limits or infrastructure planning

## Questions
1. What is considered a **normal / expected memory range** for `nuxt build`?
2. Are there known **major contributors** to memory usage (e.g. sourcemaps, prerendering, modules)?
3. Are there **recommended strategies** to reduce memory usage besides increasing Node memory?
4. Is there any **official guidance** on sizing infrastructure for builds?
issues.author: remihuigen

comments.author: DamianGlowala

comments.author: remihuigen
comments.body:
I didn’t mention a specific Nuxt version in the original post because this doesn’t seem tied to a single version.

For reference, the fresh project I mentioned (peaking at ~3.5–4 GB during build) is running on Nuxt 4.4.2.

That said, I’ve been running into this in some way or another ever since v3. I’m also not entirely sure this should be treated as a bug. It may just be how Nuxt behaves.

The main goal of this issue is to get clarity on what’s considered “normal” and whether there’s any guidance on managing or planning for build-time memory usage, rather than pointing to a regression in a specific version.

| **Nitro version**    | `2.13.3`                                                |
| **Builder**          | `vite@7.3.2`                                            |
| **Config**           | `compatibilityDate`, `devtools`, `future`               |
| **Modules**          | `-`                                                     |

Reproducible with Nuxt `v3`, `v4.3`, `v4.4` and `compatibilityVersion: 5`.

### Reproduction

- Without `pages`: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-6ajrnclj?file=app%2Fplugins%2Fredirect.ts
- With `pages`: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-6ajrnclj-pzbqriez?file=app%2Fplugins%2Fredirect.ts

1. Navigate to `/self-redirect`
2. Or run `nuxt generate`

### Describe the bug

When a middleware redirects to itself, `vue-router` should send a `500` response.

```ts
export default defineNuxtRouteMiddleware((to) => {
  if (to.path === '/self-redirect') {
    return navigateTo('/self-redirect');
  }
});
```

While this behavior is covered in the Nuxt basic test fixture, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/51d09706a2f358fffd8a4391acacb891de773f2e/test/basic.test.ts#L270-L273 the test succeeds only because it is ran in a dev environment.

vue-router only throws an error in dev mode, https://github.com/vuejs/router/blob/10a8b773eecaa7facfb9291fc01a86d2506479b0/packages/router/src/router.ts#L494-L516

If the route is not caught by a page, or if the page is being fetched by the prerenderer, `vue-router` does not throw an error. This results in an infinite loop until the process crashes to OOM.

|                                         | Handled by vue-router (`nuxt/src/pages/runtime/plugins/router.ts`) | Handled by `nuxt/src/app/plugins/router.ts` |
| --------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| `dev` server                            | ✅ Vue router throws `500: Infinite redirect in navigation guard`   | ❌ Infinite loop until OOM                   |
| `build` server w/ `NODE_ENV=production` | ❌ Infinite loop until OOM                                          | ❌ Infinite loop until OOM                   |
| prerenderer                             | ❌ Infinite loop until OOM                                          | ❌ Infinite loop until OOM                   |

### Expected Behavior

Always throw `500` or warn whenever a self-redirect is detected. It would be nice if we can implement a dedicated self-redirect detection mechanism rather than relying exclusively on vue-router to throw.

### Additional context

Found in https://github.com/ZTL-UwU/shadcn-docs-nuxt/issues/180.

In Nuxt Content v2's documentDriven mode, there is a [plugin](https://github.com/nuxt/content/blob/c2f0881a7af68cab3b952ab31351aa724e520966/src/runtime/plugins/documentDriven.ts#L260-L281) that can create a self-redirecting middleware when `navigate.to` is set to itself in `_dir.yml`.

comments.author: vsergiu93
comments.body:
Hello @capraruioan @danielroe,

This seems to happen only when `experimental.componentIslands.selectiveClient` is `true` or `'deep'`.

When `selectiveClient` resolves to a truthy value, Nuxt adds the Vite `ComponentsChunkPlugin` in [`packages/nuxt/src/components/module.ts`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/e6ccdeb8492f36afe21d5de2b9363f4fb44d4930/packages/nuxt/src/components/module.ts#L276). Then, in [`packages/nuxt/src/components/plugins/islands-transform.ts`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/e6ccdeb8492f36afe21d5de2b9363f4fb44d4930/packages/nuxt/src/components/plugins/islands-transform.ts#L216), it emits a dedicated chunk for every registered component that is not `mode === 'server'`.

My understanding is:

- To hydrate a component inside a server component/server page via `nuxt-client`, Nuxt needs to return a chunk URL for that client component so the browser can download and hydrate it.
- Since a `nuxt-client` component can appear at different depths inside a server component tree, Nuxt currently prepares for that by emitting dedicated chunks for all possible non-server components.
- This guarantees that any `nuxt-client` component can be loaded by name, but it also means Rollup can no longer merge single-use child components into their parent chunk.

For example, if `Test.vue` uses `Child.vue`, and `Child.vue` is only used there, Rollup would normally be able to bundle them together. With `selectiveClient`, both `Test.vue` and `Child.vue` are emitted as explicit component chunks, so they remain split and both are loaded separately.

On a larger app this scales with the number of registered components. 

I guess one possible way to address this would be to somehow emit chunks or for the components that are used with `nuxt-client` in a server component/page.

issues.title: [Feature]: Add hook or option to prevent suspenseKey increment during navigation (stable page content on fast navigation)
issues.body:
## Problem

When navigating quickly between routes (cross-component), `<NuxtPage>` increments `suspenseKey` on every navigation. This recreates `<Suspense>` and tears down the previous component content — even if we want to keep showing it while the new page loads.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Navigate A → B (request pending, data not yet loaded)
2. Before B resolves, navigate B → C
3. `suspenseKey++` recreates `<Suspense>`, tears down B's vnode
4. C mounts with `data: null` — blank content flash until C's request resolves

**Current behavior:** blank/broken layout flash for the duration of the final fetch

**Expected behavior:** last successfully rendered page stays visible until the new page fully resolves, then swaps — no blank flash

---

## Context

We want a **url-first navigation model**:
- URL changes immediately on every click ✅
- Old page content stays visible while new page loads ✅
- When final pending page resolves — it replaces the stable content ✅
- No blank flash, no partial renders with `data: null` ✅

---

## What already exists

The mechanism for holding the old vnode already exists in `page.ts`:

```ts
// works for same-component navigation (e.g. brand → brand)
if (!nuxtApp.isHydrating && previousPageKey === key && !willRenderAnotherChild) {
  return vnode
}
```

This works perfectly when `previousPageKey === key`. The request is to extend this to **cross-component** navigation during a pending transition.

---

## Proposed solutions

**Option 1 — Nuxt hook:**
```ts
nuxtApp.hook('page:suspend', ({ previousVnode, resume }) => {
  // hold previous vnode, call resume() when ready to swap
})
```

**Option 2 — Prop on `<NuxtPage>`:**
```vue
<NuxtPage :stable-content="true" />
```

**Option 3 — Expose `suspenseKey` via `provide`** so userland can freeze it externally

---

## Workarounds tried and why they fail

| Approach | Why it fails |
|---|---|
| `onLeave` transition hook holding `done()` | `<Transition>` holds the wrapper but `suspenseKey++` empties the content inside |
| `pageKey` prop freeze | works only when `previousPageKey === key`, not cross-component |
| `getCachedData` / `default()` | fixes data state but doesn't prevent component teardown |
| Custom `RouterView` | breaks `useRoute()` internal state managed by `<NuxtPage>` |

---

## Additional context

- The single-navigation case works correctly — `<Suspense>` holds the previous `#default` content while new content resolves
- The problem is specific to **rapid/concurrent navigation**: second click causes `suspenseKey++` which destroys the pending first component before it resolved, and the second component starts with `data: null`
- `<Suspense>` itself only holds one pending state — this is a Vue limitation, the fix needs to be at the `<NuxtPage>` level

issues.title: beasties integration for css optimisation
issues.body:
`features.inlineStyles` inlines the whole of every rendered component's css into the html, even if the css isn't relevant.

global css also can't be inlined, and this means we still have external stylesheets blocking render, and in some cases that external css is _duplicate_ of what is inlined

### 💡 concept

I'm working in beasties (https://github.com/danielroe/beasties/pull/403) to add a build-time compiler and a zero-dependency runtime to beasties, so we can inline critical css for a page without needing to parse css or building a dom per request.

### 🗺️ implementation

right now, at request time we know exactly which css is a candidate (as far as every vue file is concerned, plus the global css). so we could:

- at build, where the `styleMap` is generated, compile each entry with `beasties/compiler` into a json plan + emit it lazily exactly as the css strings are today
- at request, scan the rendered html once with `beasties/runtime` to collect the tags/classes/ids/attributes present, then emit only the rules from those plans that match

the idea would be to add a third `critical` value for `features.inlineStyles` so this could be compared before we change any defaults

this would replace https://github.com/nuxt-modules/critters

### 🤷 potential cons/costs

- ~0.1 to 0.3ms to scan a 20kB document
- ~27kB for the runtime + ~1.1x the size of the css (potentially much less if it's tailwind-style css)
- ~9ms to decode a 300kB plan

issues.title: Server-Timing headers for plugins and middlewares
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

Currently, profiling SSR performance bottlenecks in Nuxt applications can be a bit of a black box. While Nitro natively supports `Server-Timing` headers for server-level tasks via the `nitro.timing` flag, the Nuxt/Vue application layer does not natively expose the execution times of **Nuxt plugins** and **route middleware**.

I would love to add native `Server-Timing` header support for Nuxt plugins and middleware during SSR.

Since plugins and middleware run on the critical path of every initial SSR request, they are heavily responsible for latency and TTFB inflation. Being able to get these metrics on a staging or integ system would valuable to pinpoint the reason in a specific plugin or middleware.

### Use case

1. You set a build-time flag to enable the Server-Timing headers
2. Nuxt app is built and deployed
3. Under the **Timing** tab in the browser devtools you can observe that `plugin:my-custom-analytics` took 400ms, while `middleware:auth` took 10ms.
4. You know which plugins/middlewares need optimizations

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

issues.title: Support dev-only `typescript.typeCheck`
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

It is currently possible to set the `typescript.typeCheck` to the following values:
- `true` --> Enable typecheck in build and dev.
- `false` --> Disable typechecks.
- `build` --> Only typecheck on build.

It would be nice to also add `dev` which would enable typechecking only when running the dev server.

A use case for this that we encountered is wanting to split up and/or parallelize typechecking and building. For example, we use nx to manage our monorepo and parallelize typecheck and build in CI. Besides that we do not run typechecking during CD because it already ran during CI. 

We achieved this by setting `typescript.typeCheck` to `false` and adding the vite-plugin-checker only during dev, but it would be nicer if nuxt supported this since it also supports build-only. 

If you feel this is a good idea I am totally down to create a PR :)
