issues.title: RFC: Extract `$cookie` from `useCookie`
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

## Summary

Split cookie access into two layers, mirroring the `$fetch`/`useFetch` relationship:

  - `$cookie`: an imperative, non-reactive accessor: `$cookie.get(name)`, `$cookie.set(name, value)`, `$cookie.remove(name)`.
  - `useCookie`: the existing reactive composable, refactored to build on `$cookie`s raw read/write primitives.

Today `useCookie` is the only way to touch cookies in app code, and it always returns a `CookieRef` wired up with watchers, expiration timers, cross-tab sync (cookieStore/BroadcastChannel), and scope disposal. That machinery is pure overhead when all you want is a one-shot read or write.

## Proposed API

```ts
interface NuxtCookieAccessor {
  /** Read + decode a cookie. Returns undefined if absent. */
  get<T = string | null | undefined>(name: string, opts?: CookieOptions<T>): T | undefined

  /** Encode + write a cookie immediately (Set-Cookie on server, document.cookie on client). */
  set<T>(name: string, value: T, opts?: CookieOptions<T>): void

  /** Delete a cookie. */
  remove(name: string, opts?: Pick<CookieOptions, 'path' | 'domain' | ...>): void

  /** Optional: read all cookies as a record. */
  getAll?(opts?: CookieParseOptions): Record<string, unknown>
}
```

```ts
const token = $cookie.get('token')
$cookie.set('token', value, { maxAge: 3600 })
$cookie.remove('token')
```

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?
- [x] Could this feature be implemented as a module?

issues.title: rspack/webpack builder: dev SSR fails on Windows with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME (externals emitted as raw absolute paths)
issues.body:
# Environment

- Operating System: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26100)
- Node Version: v24.15.0
- Nuxt Version: 4.5.2
- Nitro Version: 2.13.4
- Package Manager: pnpm@11.0.8
- Builder: @nuxt/rspack-builder 4.5.2 (Rspack 2.1.9)
- User Config: `builder: 'rspack'`

# Reproduction

Windows-only bug, so StackBlitz can't reproduce it. Minimal steps on any Windows machine:

```bash
npm create nuxt@latest test-rspack   # accept defaults
cd test-rspack
pnpm add -D @nuxt/rspack-builder
```

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15',
  builder: 'rspack',
})
```

```bash
pnpm dev
# open http://localhost:3000
```

Every SSR request returns a 500 error. The same config works on Linux/macOS, and the same project works on Windows with the default Vite builder.

# Describe the bug

In the server externals callback, runtime dependencies are resolved to absolute paths and returned as the external specifier so that "nitro can handle version resolution":

https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/main/packages/webpack/src/configs/server.ts#L99-L101

```ts
if (resolved && isAbsolute(resolved)) {
  return cb(undefined, resolved)
}
```

With ESM output (`output.module: true`), Rspack emits these externals verbatim as import specifiers in `.nuxt/dist/server/server.dev.mjs`:

```js
import * as ... from "D:/path/to/project/node_modules/.pnpm/defu@6.1.7/node_modules/defu/dist/defu.mjs";
```

In dev, this file is imported directly by the Node ESM loader, which parses `D:/...` as a URL with protocol `d:` and throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME`. On POSIX the raw absolute path happens to work, which is why this is Windows-only.

# Suggested fix

Wrap the resolved path with `pathToFileURL()` **in dev only**:

```ts
if (resolved && isAbsolute(resolved)) {
  return cb(undefined, ctx.nuxt.options.dev ? pathToFileURL(resolved).href : resolved)
}
```

Verified locally via `pnpm patch` on `@nuxt/rspack-builder@4.5.2`: dev SSR renders correctly on Windows, and `nuxt build` output is unchanged.

The dev-only gate matters: returning a `file://` URL unconditionally breaks the production path — Nitro's Rollup can't resolve `file://` specifiers when bundling `.nuxt/dist/server/server.mjs`, logs `"file:///D:/..." is imported by ".nuxt/dist/server/server.mjs", but could not be resolved – treating it as an external dependency` for every runtime dep, and leaks machine-absolute `file://` imports into `.output` (verified: this exact failure mode occurs with an unconditional patch). Raw absolute paths must be kept for the production build.

Same class of bug as the recent Vite-side fix #35492 (`fix(vite): use file URLs for dev virtual imports on Windows`).

# Logs

```
ERROR  [request error] [unhandled] [GET] http://localhost:3000/

Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader. On Windows, absolute paths must be valid file:// URLs. Received protocol 'd:'
    at throwIfUnsupportedURLScheme (node:internal/modules/esm/load:195:11)
    at defaultLoadSync (node:internal/modules/esm/load:142:3)
    at #loadAndMaybeBlockOnLoaderThread (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:776:12)
    at #loadSync (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:796:49)
    at ModuleLoader.load (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:762:26)
    at ModuleLoader.loadAndTranslate (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:504:31)
    at #getOrCreateModuleJobAfterResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:555:36)
    at afterResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:603:52)
    at ModuleLoader.getOrCreateModuleJob (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:609:12)
    at ModuleJob.syncLink (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:162:33)
```

issues.title: `_nuxt/*` chunk `[hash]` not unique across builds — cached copy collides with newer content
issues.body:
### Environment

```
●  Nuxt root directory: /home/surgiie/projects/nuxt-hash-issue
│
│ ╭── Nuxt project info (copied to clipboard) ─────────────────────────────╮
│ │                                                                        │
│ │  Operating system      Linux 6.18.44                                   │
│ │  CPU                   Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 5 125H (18 cores)       │
│ │  Node.js version       v24.19.0                                        │
│ │  nuxt/cli version      3.37.0                                          │
│ │  Package manager       npm 11.17.0                                     │
│ │  Nuxt version          4.5.2                                           │
│ │  Nitro version         2.13.4                                          │
│ │  Builder               vite 8.2.2                                      │
│ │  Config                compatibilityDate, devtools, hooks, nitro, ssr  │
│ │  Modules               -                                               │
│ │                                                                        │
│ ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
```

### Reproduction

https://github.com/surgiie/nuxt-hash-issue

Refer to the readme for full instructions.

### Describe the bug

Two builds of the same Nuxt app can emit a shared JS chunk under the **same `_nuxt/<hash>.js` filename** with **genuinely different content**. This is problematic for applications that do **all** of the following:

  - Add [subresource integrity attributes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Subresource_Integrity) to script tags that load `_nuxt/<hash>.js` files.
  - Cache these `_nuxt/*` files with long cache ages via the `Cache-Control` header.

  When serving an app in this fashion, a browser can end up with a cached file whose content no longer matches the integrity hash the current page expects — producing a hard browser failure like:

  ```
  Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource
  '.../_nuxt/<name>.js' with computed SHA-256 integrity '...'.
  The resource has been blocked.
  ```

  Visually, Nuxt's error page renders something like:

  ```
  500
  Internal Server Error
  Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:4173/_nuxt/<hash>.js
  ```


### Additional context

## Workarounds & Findings

  It's unclear to me whether this is fully deterministic (same inputs always collide) — confirming that would take a lot more testing than I'd like to put in right now. Some assistance/guidance figuring out a cleaner fix or workaround would be appreciated. What I've tried or considered so far:

  - **Widening the chunk hash** (`build.rolldownOptions.output.chunkFileNames` / `entryFileNames`, e.g. `_nuxt/[name]-[hash:21].js`) — with some help from an LLM, I noticed this produces more consistent results in my testing, but I'm not entirely sure it fully eliminates the possibility of this happening. I'd guess a collision is still possible.
  - Setting entryImportMap: false seems to mitigate the issue as hinted by others in #33247 
  - **Dropping SRI/`integrity` attributes entirely and not caching assets** — would remove the hard failure mode I'm seeing, but I'd rather not go this route: it's a real security control to give up, and it doesn't fix the actual bug — the wrong bytes would still silently end up served at a filename other code/caches trust, just without anything catching it.
  - **Cache Invalidations**  - Possible but not ideal for us when paired with large amount of builds and defeats the purpose of hash file names.

  ## Expectations

  Changing the codebase should produce consistent hash names, so that a site can rely on the filename itself to know when it needs to request a new asset file. If there's a known-good mitigation, or this is already understood/fixed upstream in a way I'm missing, I'd appreciate a pointer.


### Logs


The reproduction repository provides util script commands for producing visual output showcasing the problem that include which file has differing content between builds but the same `[hash]` filename. There are no relevant logs produced by nuxt when reproducing this or worth sharing.



### Related

I believe the following issue maybe related or very similar 
- https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/33247

comments.author: EmanueleDB
comments.body:
We hit this in production on Nuxt 4.5.2 today and I have data that suggests #36198 only closes half of it.

**How it surfaced.** A dependency update moved Vite 8.2.0 → 8.3.0, which bumps rolldown 1.2.1 → 1.2.8. Rolldown's newer code splitting folds shared runtime code into the entry chunk: in our app 82 lazy chunks now statically import the entry, where under rolldown 1.2.1 none did (165 chunks → 137, entry 388 KB → 548 KB). With `entryImportMap` those imports become `#entry`, so the entry's hash no longer feeds their filenames, while their `__vite__mapDeps` still carry the entry's real filenames. Nothing changed in Vite's dependency collection between 8.2.0 and 8.3.0 (diffed `importAnalysisBuild.ts`); the bundle shape changed and exposed this.

**Measurement.** Two consecutive commits differing only by a Tailwind utility class (so the entry JS and `entry.<hash>.css` both get new names), built with the same lockfile, 137 client chunks each:

- 11 chunks keep their filename with different bytes.
- In every one of them the only difference is the `__vite__mapDeps` array, and inside it exactly two entries: the entry chunk's filename and the entry CSS filename.

With `Cache-Control: immutable` on `/_nuxt/**` and nuxt-security's SRI, returning browsers served the stale copy, the digest failed, and the dynamic import ended in a 500 page.

**Why #36198 is not enough.** It removes the entry chunk through `build.modulePreload.resolveDependencies`. But Vite partitions the list before calling that hook and re-appends the CSS untouched (`importAnalysisBuild.ts`, `generateBundle`):

```ts
for (const dep of depsArray) (dep.endsWith('.css') ? cssDeps : otherDeps).push(dep)
depsArray = [...resolveDependencies(normalizedFile, otherDeps, { hostId, hostType }), ...cssDeps]
```

So `entry.<hash>.css` stays in `__vite__mapDeps`. Replaying the #36198 filter on our 11 colliding chunks (strip the entry JS name from both builds' arrays) still leaves all 11 differing, on the CSS name alone. Any change to the global stylesheet, which with Tailwind is most deploys, reproduces the collision.

**Runtime side is safe to change.** Both entries are always already in the SSR markup (`<link rel="modulepreload">` for the entry, `<link rel="stylesheet">` for its CSS), and Vite's preload helper returns early when a matching `<link>` exists, so removing the entry's CSS from the preload list has no observable effect.

**Suggestion.** Extend the fix so that the entry chunk's CSS (`viteMetadata.importedCss` of the entry) is dropped too. Since `resolveDependencies` never sees CSS, that likely means either rewriting the `__vite__mapDeps` array and its index lists in a `generateBundle` hook ordered after Vite's, or a Vite-side change to pass CSS through `resolveDependencies`.

Our workaround in the meantime is a per-build `app.buildAssetsDir` (`/_nuxt/<build-id>/`), which sidesteps hashing entirely at the cost of cross-deploy caching.

Environment: Nuxt 4.5.2, Vite 8.3.0, rolldown 1.2.8, nuxt-security 2.6.0 (SRI on), SSR, node-server preset.

issues.title: Layer reached twice by package name has its config merged twice; `seenLayerDirs` never sees it
issues.body:
### Environment

Resolved versions, printed by the reproduction run rather than read from `package.json`. They are at the top of `repro.log` in the repo below.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `nuxt` | 4.5.2 |
| `nitropack` | 2.13.4 |
| `c12` | 3.3.4 |
| `defu` | 6.1.7 |
| `node` | v24.20.0 |
| OS | Darwin 24.6.0 |
| Package manager | npm (workspaces) |

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jd-solanki/reproductions/tree/nitro-cloudflare-crons-duplicated-by-diamond-layers--2026-09-10

```bash
npm install
npm run repro
```

It builds the same app twice, once with each spelling of `extends`, prints the merged config and the layer list, then exits non-zero if the behaviour below is not observed.

### Describe the bug

A layer reached by two paths in the `extends` graph has its config merged once per path. Every array it declares comes out doubled.

Nuxt already guards against this. `seenLayerDirs` in `@nuxt/kit`'s layer loader was added in #35712 to fix #34667, which reported this same symptom as "scheduled tasks executed twice if scheduled in a layer". The guard works, but only when the layer is spelled as a path.

Same graph, same versions, only the spelling of `extends` differs:

```ts
extends: ['@repro/layer-a', '@repro/layer-b']   // package names
// nitro.cloudflare.wrangler.triggers.crons -> ['0 0 * * *', '0 0 * * *']
// nitro.scheduledTasks['0 0 * * *']         -> ['someTask', 'someTask']

extends: ['./packages/a', './packages/b']       // relative paths, same graph
// nitro.cloudflare.wrangler.triggers.crons -> ['0 0 * * *']
// nitro.scheduledTasks['0 0 * * *']         -> ['someTask']
```

The cause looks like the existence check that the guard sits behind:

```js
const path = aliased ?? resolve(base, source)
if (!existsSync(path)) return
const layerDir = canonicalLayerDir(path)
if (seenLayerDirs.has(layerDir)) return { config: {}, cwd: layerDir, source }
```

A package specifier resolves to a path that does not exist on disk, so the hook returns before it reaches `seenLayerDirs`, and c12 goes on to resolve and merge that layer again. Paths and aliases pass the check and are deduplicated. That part is a guess; the contrast above is what we measured.

Nothing looks wrong from the outside. `nuxt.options._layers` lists the layer exactly once, with a unique `cwd`, while the merged config carries both copies. A reader checking the layer list concludes the diamond is already handled.

### Additional context

Two ways this surfaced in a real app.

The Cloudflare deploy fails. The doubled cron reaches `.output/server/wrangler.json` and the API rejects it. It rejects on the `PUT .../schedules` call *after* the script has uploaded, so the Worker goes live with a red deploy and its schedules untouched:

```
duplicate cron found: 0 0 * * * [code: 10100]
```

The scheduled task runs twice. `nitro.scheduledTasks` is an object, so its keys collapse on merge, but the task list under each key is an array, and it does not. The built bundle carries `tasks: ["someTask","someTask"]`, and nitro's in-flight guard does not collapse the pair, because `runTask` yields before it records the promise. The task body executes twice, concurrently, on every fire. This half is preset-independent and raises no error anywhere. No nitro release addresses it, and it has nothing to do with Cloudflare cron generation.

Arrays elsewhere in the config are unaffected because Nuxt deduplicates them downstream itself: `modules` by identity, `css` by an explicit filter, `imports.dirs` by unimport. Nothing deduplicates `nitro.*`, so that is where it shows.

Related: nitrojs/nitro#4155 reports the double task execution against Nitro. unjs/defu#136 and unjs/c12#309 both rule the array concatenation itself as intended, which is why this is filed here rather than there.

### Initial steps
- `pnpm i && pnpm build &&  node .output/server/index.mjs` 

Compare page styles before and after hydration, note the missing stylesheets (they are preloaded though).

### Expected
Every component that is server-rendered on a page has its stylesheet linked in the `<head>` of that page, regardless of how the bundler chunked it

### Actual
Components that land in a chunk without a facade module render unstyled on first paint

### Describe the bug

With `features.inlineStyles: false`, a page can server-render a component while its scoped CSS is not linked in the `<head>`. The element is in the HTML, but the stylesheet that styles it only appears as prefetch `<link rel="prefetch" as="style">`. The browser applies it once the client bundle loads the chunk, so the component is unstyled on first paint.

The two repositories with a reproduction contain two small cases that trigger this:

- Nuxt 4.4.2, Rollup: the default layout calls a composable that is also used by a lazily loaded, client-only component inside the layout. The layout ends up in a chunk without a facade. The manifest has no `layouts/default.vue` key and the layout CSS is missing on every page.

- Case B (Nuxt 4.5.2, rolldown): a component is rendered through `<LazySuggestedProducts />` on one page and imported statically by a component on another page. It ends up in a shared chunk without a facade. The manifest has no `components/suggested-products.vue` key. On the page that renders it lazily the CSS is missing; on the page that imports it statically the CSS is linked.

### Additional context

- The issue happens when the bundler puts a component into a chunk that has no facade module. In the client manifest such a chunk is keyed by its file name (`_<hash>.js`) and has no `src`, so there is no manifest entry for the component's own id (for example `layouts/default.vue` or `components/suggested-products.vue`). The server renderer looks the component up by that id when it collects the stylesheets for the page, finds nothing, and skips the CSS

- Whether a component gets its own manifest key depends on the whole import graph. Adding or removing a single shared import elsewhere in the app changes the chunking and makes the CSS appear or disappear, which made this look random

comments.author: hamedniroomand
comments.body:
@mrleblanc101 Nuxt's default `scrollBehavior` does *not* ignore the saved position on first load. In [`router.options.ts`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/main/packages/nuxt/src/pages/runtime/router.options.ts), the `from === START_LOCATION` branch goes straight to `_calculatePosition`, which returns `savedPosition` first and only falls back to `{ left: 0, top: 0 }` when there is none.

And vue-router does provide a `savedPosition` on reload: it writes the current scroll into `history.state.scroll` on `beforeunload`, and `history.state` survives a refresh, so the first navigation receives it. In a plain Nuxt 4 app, scroll *is* restored after refresh — the "Nuxt only knows positions tracked in the current session" explanation isn't accurate.

So if `savedPosition` is empty in your project, something is discarding it before `scrollBehavior` runs. Two likely candidates from your config:

1. **`@nuxtjs/i18n` redirect on initial load.** If the first navigation is redirected (e.g. `/` → `/fr`, or a browser-language redirect), the navigation resolves to a different `fullPath` than the one the scroll was saved against, so there is no saved position for it and Nuxt falls back to top. Easy check: does the problem still happen with `@nuxtjs/i18n` removed from `modules`, or with `detectBrowserLanguage` / redirects disabled?
2. **Document height at restore time.** If the target position is below the current document height when `scrollBehavior` resolves (client-only content, images without dimensions, fonts shifting layout), the scroll is clamped.

### Describe the feature

We have [checkOutdatedBuildInterval](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/going-further/experimental-features#checkoutdatedbuildinterval) which uses a timer to periodically check for an updated app manifest. However, there are several cases where timers can get throttled or suspended. For example, if a tab has been inactive for a long time, or when when a PWA gets moved to a background state [[1]](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/setTimeout#reasons_for_longer_delays_than_specified) [[2]](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/setInterval#delay_restrictions).  

It would therefore be beneficial to have a function to call to manually trigger the check for the app manifest. The user could then use this in  their own app hooks, trigger it from a worker or even use the [Periodic Sync API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Periodic_Background_Synchronization_API) in the future. 

I'd be happy to have a go implementing this, but would appreciate some guidance on naming and where it should live in the codebase.

issues.title: Allow modules to register directories for the keyed-function factory scan (createUseFetch / createUseAsyncData)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

`createUseFetch` and `createUseAsyncData` factories are only detected when they live in `<layer>/composables`. The compiler scan (`runScanPlugins` in `packages/nuxt/src/compiler/module.ts`) iterates over `nuxt.options._layers` and resolves `resolve(layer.config.srcDir, 'composables')`. Composables exposed by a module through `addImportsDir()` are auto-imported, but never scanned. A factory defined in a module is therefore not transformed, and gets no automatic key.

Our setup: a shared Nuxt module used by several sites exposes a `useAPI` composable that wraps `useFetch` with a custom `$fetch`. Following the "Custom useFetch" recipe, we would like to write it with `createUseFetch`, but this only works if the module is turned into a layer.

### Proposal

A way for modules to add scan directories. For example, a `compiler.scanDirs` option that modules can push to, or a kit helper such as `addCompilerScanDir(path)`.

### Current workaround

A manual wrapper around `useFetch`, or registering the name in `optimization.keyedComposables`. Both work, but lose the benefit of the factory.

### Additional information

Checked against v4.5.2.

comments.body: cc @cernymatej

comments.author: cernymatej
comments.body:
I'd probably lean towards a kit utility to register the factory instead (something along the lines of `addImports()`). I don't think it's good practice for modules to register their own internal directories for scanning, as they can provide the paths to the utils they expose, saving some perf overhead.

We decided with Daniel to keep the `compiler` module internal for the time being.

issues.title: Prerendered page with `layout: false` + `setPageLayout()` is fully re-rendered on hydration when the URL has a query string
issues.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: macOS 26.7
- Node Version: v22.22.2
- Nuxt Version: 4.5.2
- Vue Version: 3.5.43
- Vue Router Version: 5.3.1
- Nitro Version: 2.13.4
- Builder: vite 8.3.1
- Deployment: static (`nuxt generate`)
- Last working version: 4.4.8


### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-zkzjxhxn?file=app%2Fplugins%2Fssr-dom-check.client.ts

```sh
npm install
npm run generate
npm run preview
```

- `http://localhost:3000/` shows `Server-rendered DOM reused on hydration: true`
- `http://localhost:3000/?foo=bar` shows `Server-rendered DOM reused on hydration: false`

The whole reproduction is a plain layout and this page:

```vue
<!-- app/pages/index.vue -->
<template>
  <main>Page content</main>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({
  layout: false,
  middleware: [() => setPageLayout("default")],
});
</script>
```

A client plugin (`app/plugins/ssr-dom-check.client.ts`) keeps a reference to the server-rendered `<main>` and compares it with the one on screen in `onNuxtReady`.

### Describe the bug

When a prerendered page is opened with a query string (for example the UTM parameters of an ad campaign), the server-rendered DOM of the layout and of the page is discarded and rendered again on the client instead of being hydrated. Without a query string, the same page hydrates normally.

It only happens when the page opts out of the default layout with `layout: false` and picks its layout with `setPageLayout()` in a route middleware. With `layout: "default"` in `definePageMeta`, or with Nuxt 4.4.8, the DOM is reused.

It looks related to the deferred route restore introduced in 4.5 (`hasDeferredRoute` in `pages/runtime/plugins/router.js`, restore moved to the `<NuxtPage>` suspense `onResolve` in #35442): the app hydrates against the query-less `payload.path`, then restores the real route with `router.replace({ force: true })` while hydration is still in progress. The middleware runs again during that navigation and the layout `<Suspense>` goes pending again (its `pendingId` ends at 5 instead of 1 on a static build of our site), which replaces the layout branch.

On a larger app the consequences are worse than a re-render. On our production site (static marketing pages opened from ads with UTM parameters), async components inside the layout (`defineAsyncComponent`, including ones using `hydrateOnVisible`) end up in one of two states:

- never mounted: `asyncDep` stays unresolved, presumably because `registerDep` drops them once the suspense `pendingId` has changed. The navigation stays dead and its `onMounted` hooks never run.
- stuck in an infinite microtask loop: Vue keeps re-scheduling the update of a parent through `asyncDep.then(() => queuePostRenderEffect(...))` for a child that never finishes hydrating. The main thread never goes idle, so later client plugins (analytics, cookie banner) never run.

In our case, both states are only reached with a query string, and only since 4.5.

### Additional context

#### Workaround

A client plugin running between `nuxt:revive-payload:client` (order -30) and `nuxt:router` (order -20) appends the query and hash to `payload.path` when the pathname matches. `hasDeferredRoute` is then false and hydration happens against the real route, as in 4.4:

```ts
import { isSamePath } from "ufo";

export default defineNuxtPlugin({
  name: "prerendered-route",
  order: -25,
  setup(nuxtApp) {
    const { path } = nuxtApp.payload;
    if (!nuxtApp.isHydrating || !nuxtApp.payload.prerenderedAt || !path) return;

    const { pathname, search, hash } = window.location;
    if (!isSamePath(pathname, path)) return;

    nuxtApp.payload.path = `${path}${search}${hash}`;
  },
});
```

It fixes both the reproduction and our production issue, but it relies on `payload.path` internals, so we would rather drop it once this is fixed upstream.

Possibly related: #34845 (setPageLayout props lost on query-only navigations), #35197, #35355.

issues.title: Recommended API for third-party state to participate in payload extraction?
issues.body:
[TanStack Query’s Nuxt hydration guide](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/vue/guides/ssr#nuxt-3) stores dehydrated query state using `useState()`.

With `experimental.payloadExtraction: true` on an SWR route, I observed that `useState` is serialized under `payload.state` and remains inline in the HTML, while `_payload.json` contains `payload.data`.

Storing the dehydrated cache in `nuxtApp.payload.data` instead makes it participate in payload extraction:

```ts
nuxtApp.payload.data['vue-query-state'] = dehydrate(queryClient)
```

Is `nuxtApp.payload.data` the intended API for third-party modules integrating with Nuxt payload extraction, or should this use `useNuxtData`, `useAsyncData`, or another public API?

Depending on the answer I would submit a PR to the Tanstack Query repo to make it work with the standard payload extraction.
issues.author: peterbud

comments.author: peterbud
comments.body:
Or a potential inconsistency in the [docs](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/getting-started/prerendering#payload-extraction):

> When Nuxt renders a page on the server, it serializes the results of your data fetching ([useAsyncData](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-async-data) and [useFetch](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-fetch)) and app state ([useState](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-state)) into a payload so the client can hydrate without re-fetching. With payload extraction enabled, Nuxt also writes this payload to a _payload.json file alongside the route's HTML

However it seems to me that `useState()` results are NOT extracted to `_payload.json`.

comments.author: danielroe
comments.body:
you're right on the inconsistency. state is part of the payload, but is exempted from being _extracted_, which should be clarified.

`data` is the correct home for anything that wants to be in the payload, and I would recommend `useNuxtData` for an integration with tanstack query...

issues.title: Hash navigation ignores scroll-margin-top when the target id starts with a digit
issues.body:
### Environment

- Nuxt: 4.5.2
- vue-router: 5.2.0
- Vue: 3.5.41
- Node: 24.16.0
- Browser: Chromium

### Reproduction

No hosted reproduction - the steps are minimal:

1. A page with two headings below the fold, both with `scroll-margin-top: 32px`: `<h2 id="tips">` and `<h2 id="5-tips">` (Nuxt Content renders `## 5 tips` exactly like this).
2. Click `<NuxtLink to="#tips">` - the heading stops 32 px below the top of the window.
3. Click `<NuxtLink to="#5-tips">` - the heading stops at 0 px: its `scroll-margin-top` is ignored.

### Describe the bug

`_getHashElementScrollMarginTop` in `packages/nuxt/src/pages/runtime/router.options.ts` resolves the target with `document.querySelector(selector)`, where `selector` is `to.hash`. An id that starts with a digit is not a valid CSS selector, so `document.querySelector("#5-tips")` throws, the `catch` swallows the error and the function returns `0`. vue-router still scrolls to the element (it looks ids up with `getElementById`), but without the offset, so the target ignores its `scroll-margin-top` and the root `scroll-padding-top`.

Headings such as `## 5 tips` or `## 2026 prices` are common in Nuxt Content articles, and their slugs start with a digit.

### Additional context

vue-router resolves id selectors with `document.getElementById(el.slice(1))` for exactly this reason (see the comment in its `scrollToPosition`). Suggested fix: do the same in `_getHashElementScrollMarginTop` - `document.getElementById(selector.slice(1))` for `#` selectors, or `CSS.escape` the id before `querySelector`

issues.title: add `defineValidatedHandler` to `nuxt/server`
issues.body:
### Environment


- nuxt 4.6.0, @nuxt/nitro-server 4.6.0, nitropack 2.13.4, h3 1.15.11
- zod 4.6.5
- typescript 6.0.3, vue-tsc 3.3.11


### Reproduction


`nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  experimental: { routeTypedFetch: true },
})
```

`server/api/probe/portable.post.ts` (taken from the 4.6 release post):

```ts
import { defineEventHandler, readValidatedBody } from 'nuxt/server'
import { z } from 'zod'

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const body = await readValidatedBody(event, z.object({ title: z.string(), count: z.number() }))
  return { created: body.title }
})
```

`app/utils/probe.ts`:

```ts
import { $fetch } from '#build/fetch'

export async function probe() {
  const ok = await $fetch('/api/probe/portable', { method: 'POST', body: { title: 'a', count: 1 } })
  const r: number = ok                                                                       // error, as expected
  await $fetch('/api/probe/portable', { method: 'POST', body: { title: 'a', count: 'no' } }) // no error
  await $fetch('/api/probe/portable', { method: 'POST' })                                     // no error
  return r
}
```


### Describe the bug


The response type is inferred (`{ created: string }`), but the body isn't. The wrong `count` type and the missing body both type-check, while the release post shows both as errors:

> ```ts
> await $fetch('/api/users', { method: 'post', body: { title: 'a', count: 'no' } })
> //                                                                ^ not assignable to number
> await $fetch('/api/users', { method: 'post' })
> //           ^ body is required
> ```

The generated `.nuxt/server-routes.d.ts` types the body as `RequestBodyOf<typeof import("../server/api/probe/portable.post").default>`. Under `@nuxt/nitro-server`, `RequestBodyOf` (`@nuxt/nitro-server/request-types`) only reads the request shape from h3 v1's `H3Event<Request>` handler parameter. A `nuxt/server` handler is typed `(event: RequestEvent) => Result`, so it always resolves to `never`, and the call site stays permissive.

Today the only way to get the body or query checked on Nuxt 4 is an h3 handler with an annotated event (`async (event: H3Event<{ body: Body }>) => ...`). That works against the advice to move handlers to `nuxt/server`.


### Additional context


On Nuxt 4.6 with `@nuxt/nitro-server`, a `nuxt/server` handler that validates its body or query with `readValidatedBody` / `getValidatedQuery` contributes those shapes to the generated route types, as the release post shows. If that's only planned for Nuxt 5 / Nitro 3, the post and the `routeTypedFetch` docs should say so.

```shell-script

```

issues.title: docs: aria-current="page" is also set on links that differ only by query
issues.body:
The accessibility guide's Links section says "the link matching the current route already exposes `aria-current="page"`" ([docs](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/best-practices/accessibility#links)).

That holds only when links differ by path. Vue Router decides exact-active on the route record and params, and "Other route properties, such as the `query`, are not taken into account" ([Vue Router docs](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/active-links.html)). So every `<NuxtLink>` whose target differs from the current page only by query is marked `aria-current="page"`. Examples are a list of `?edit=<id>` rows, filter links, or `?tab=` links. A screen reader then announces "current page" on all of them. That breaks the rule the Vue Router maintainer states in vuejs/router#1746: "only one element should have `aria-current=page`".

Suggested addition to the Links section: a note that query-only links share the current page's exact-active state. For those, set `aria-current` yourself, e.g. `:aria-current="$route.query.tab === 'x' ? 'true' : undefined"` for a current item in a set, or `aria-current="false"` for an action link. Alternatively, use the `custom` slot.

Happy to open a PR with the wording.

issues.title: compatibilityVersion: 5 rejects nitro preset options such as `nitro.cloudflare`
issues.body:
### Environment

Nuxt nightly `4.6.0-2610091445-242e197` (4.x at 242e1971e) · nitropack 2.13.4 · TypeScript 6.0.3 · vue-tsc 3.3.12 · Node 24.20.0

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jd-solanki/reproductions/tree/nuxt-compat5-nitro-preset-options-untyped--2026-10-10

`pnpm install && pnpm test` runs `nuxt typecheck`.

### Describe the bug

A follow-up to #36516. With `future.compatibilityVersion: 5`, `nuxt typecheck` rejects valid preset options under `nitro`:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  future: { compatibilityVersion: 5 },
  nitro: {
    preset: 'cloudflare_module',
    cloudflare: { deployConfig: true },
  },
})
```

```text
nuxt.config.ts(7,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'cloudflare' does not exist in type 'ResolveNuxtNitroConfig<NitroConfig>'.
```

242e1971e maps `nitropack`, `nitropack/types` and `nitropack/runtime` to declaration files in the generated node tsconfig, so `preset` type-checks now. `nitropack/presets` isn't mapped, and its declarations re-export without file extensions, which `nodenext` can't follow:

```ts
// nitropack/presets.d.ts
export * from "./dist/presets/index";

// nitropack/dist/presets/index.d.mts
export { resolvePreset } from "./_resolve";
```

So every preset's options (`cloudflare`, `vercel`, `netlify`, …) drop out of `NitroConfig`. The same config type-checks without the flag, and on 4.6.0 the earlier `preset` error from #36516 hides this one.

Expected: preset options type-check under `compatibilityVersion: 5`, as they do without it.

### Additional context

Found while moving a Cloudflare Workers app, which sets `nitro.cloudflare.deployConfig` and wrangler options, towards `compatibilityVersion: 5`.

### Logs

```shell-script
[nuxt] ℹ Running with compatibility version 5
nuxt.config.ts(7,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'cloudflare' does not exist in type 'ResolveNuxtNitroConfig<NitroConfig>'.
```

issues.title: Aborted navigation to an unmatched route renders a 404
issues.body: ### Environment macOS 27.0.0; Node 24.21.0; npm 11.17.0; Chrome 155.0.8059.40. Nuxt 4.6.1 (latest), Vue 3.5.43, Vue Router 5.4.0, Nitro 2.13.4, Vite 8.3.4. No third-party Nuxt modules. Also reproduced on Nuxt 3.20.2 and 3.21.11. ### Reproduction Self-contained reproduction (all files below). Run npm install, then npm run dev, wait for hydration, and click "Abort navigation". package.json ```json {"private":true,"type":"module","scripts":{"dev":"nuxt dev","generate":"nuxt generate","postinstall":"nuxt prepare"},"dependencies":{"nuxt":"4.6.1","vue":"3.5.43"}} ``` nuxt.config.ts ```ts export default defineNuxtConfig({ srcDir: 'app', compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15', devtools: { enabled: false }, nitro: { prerender: { crawlLinks: false, routes: ['/'] } }, }) ``` app/app.vue ```vue ``` app/pages/index.vue ```vue ``` app/middleware/abort.global.ts ```ts export default defineNuxtRouteMiddleware((to) => { if (to.query.abort === '1') return false }) ``` app/error.vue ```vue ``` There is intentionally no /missing page. For static production reproduction, stop the dev server, run npm run generate, then serve .output/public with python3 -m http.server 3000 --directory .output/public and repeat the click. ### Describe the bug Expected: the guard returns false, so navigation is aborted and the home page remains visible. Actual: the URL and router.currentRoute remain at /, but Nuxt fires app:error and renders 404 for /missing?abort=1. afterEach receives failure.type = 4 (aborted) and to.matched.length = 0. This happens after hydration, not during initial page load. NuxtLink, router.push, router.replace and navigateTo all reproduce it. No second application, external redirect or CDN is required. ### Additional context Verified in real Chrome, using isolated Nuxt projects: - 3.20.2: reproduced in development and generated static output. - 3.21.11: reproduced in development. - 4.6.1: reproduced in development and generated static output. ### Possible solution A possible solution is to check the navigation failure argument in the unmatched-route afterEach handler and skip the 404 handling when navigation fails: ```ts router.afterEach((to, _from, failure) => { if (failure) return // Existing unmatched-route 404 handling }) ``` This appears to prevent the erroneous 404 during aborted navigation. It was verified in generated static builds of Nuxt 3.20.2 and 4.6.1, while successful navigation to a missing route still produces a 404. Aborted navigation to a matched route already behaves correctly. Cancelled and duplicated navigation have not been individually verified in the browser. This may be related to #18875, but the reproduction here is an aborted internal navigation after hydration. ### Logs ```shell-script Observed after the cancelled click: route: / browser pathname: / Nuxt isHydrating: false afterEach: { to: '/missing?abort=1', from: '/', matched: 0, type: 4 } app:error: { statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Page not found: /missing?abort=1' } rendered heading: 404 ```

issues.title: NodeMismatch with iOS and phone numbers
issues.body:
<!-- 💚 Thanks for your time to make Nuxt better with your feedbacks 💚 -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Yes. My Nuxt app worked fine on all platforms and browsers except iOS Safari. The page would break. I spent 2 days trying to track down this bug (almost abandoned the project) until I came across the workaround that was (yes, very clearly) stated in the documentation under Concepts -> Server Side Rendering. The issue is that I had a phone number on the page, and iOS Safari converts the phone number into a link, causing a NodeMismatch and breaking the page.

The bug was very difficult to describe, so I spent hours and hours searching the web, GitHub, stack overflow, etc. trying to find the source of the bug until I happened to stumble across a similar issue that identified the source as the phone number.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I think this workaround (using a meta tag to stop the phone number link transformation) should be the default configuration for a Nuxt project. I really spent a lot of time trying to track down this bug. The potential for an app to completely break on a browser used by a non-trivial number of people is far worse than disabling the phone number link transformation by default.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Alternatives include 1) the workaround described above, 2) transforming all NuxtLinks into standard "a" tags, or 3) relying on people reading every page of the documentation and happening to take note of the page describing this unique bug at an early stage in a project when you might not even have a phone number listed on the page.

### Additional context

That about covers it.

issues.title: Proposal: optional EvalPort (openeval) export for evals/ and agent-results.json
issues.body:
## Summary

Proposing an optional `openeval` export for this repo's eval tasks and `agent-results.json`, using [EvalPort](https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/evalport) — a small, framework-agnostic JSON Schema (not a runner, not a service) for describing eval suites and results portably. I read through `evals/*/PROMPT.md` + `EVAL.ts`, `scripts/export-results.ts`, and `agent-results.json`'s shape before writing this, so the mapping below is grounded in this repo's actual data model, not a generic pitch.

I'm not affiliated with Nuxt or Vercel — just an outside contributor who thinks this repo's 31 tasks and 20-model result set are exactly the kind of real, well-authored eval data EvalPort is meant to make portable. Happy to open a draft PR for either half if there's interest; posting here first since this changes the export surface and I'd rather get a maintainer read before writing code.

## Why this repo specifically

This isn't a generic "please adopt my format" ask. Two things stood out reading the source:

1. Each `evals/nuxt-XXX-*/` is a real, self-contained fixture — `PROMPT.md` (symptom-based task), a working-but-flawed Nuxt app, and `EVAL.ts` with vitest assertions that check both the fix *and* reject the anti-pattern (e.g. `nuxt-018-nuxt5-migration/EVAL.ts` asserts `compatibilityVersion: 5` is set **and** that the deprecated `dedupe: true` boolean and the pre-v4 `=== null` data guard are both gone). That's exactly the shape EvalPort's `code` grader type was designed for — it carries `params.language` + `params.source`, so the actual vitest file can travel with the suite rather than being replaced by a lossy pass/fail flag.
2. `scripts/export-results.ts` already produces a clean, structured `agent-results.json` across 20 models/harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) with `passRate`, `firstRunSuccess`, `costUsd`, and `passAt1`/`avgPassRate` per experiment — this is already 90% of the way to an EvalPort `ResultSet`. It's currently a bespoke shape consumed only by `nuxt.com/evals`; an EvalPort export would let the same data be read by any EvalPort-aware tool without knowing this repo's internal `AgentResult`/`ExportedData` types.

Since `AGENTS.md` already points at Vercel's own `next-evals` as the sibling repo this one's structure was modeled on, a shared portable export is also the thing that would let a cross-framework (Next vs Nuxt vs whatever else adopts this pattern) comparison exist without someone hand-parsing multiple bespoke JSON shapes.

## Concrete mapping

**Suite side** — `evals/*/` → one `EvalSuite` with one `TestCase` per directory:

```ts
// sketch: fixtureToTestCase(dir: string): TestCase
{
  id: 'nuxt-018-nuxt5-migration',
  input: readFileSync(join(dir, 'PROMPT.md'), 'utf-8').trim(),
  graders: ['gr_vitest'],
  metadata: {
    // source files an EvalPort-aware runner would need to actually execute this
    'openeval.starter_files': listAppAndServerFiles(dir),
    'openeval.eval_type': dir.includes('-fix-') ? 'fix' : 'build', // README's own Type column
  },
}
```

```ts
// one shared grader per suite — the vitest source travels with it
{
  id: 'gr_vitest',
  type: 'code',
  params: { language: 'typescript', source: readFileSync(join(dir, 'EVAL.ts'), 'utf-8') },
}
```

**Results side** — one `ResultSet` per experiment (`results/<experiment>/`), `suite_id` matching the suite above:

```ts
// sketch: agentResultToResult(r: AgentResult): Result
{
  test_case_id: r.evalPath,
  passed: r.result.success,          // summary.passedRuns > 0
  duration_ms: r.result.duration,
  metadata: {
    cost_usd: r.costUsd,             // spec explicitly scopes Result.metadata for cost/tokens
    'openeval.pass_rate': r.result.passRate,       // censored under earlyExit — same caveat your own comment already flags
    'openeval.first_run_success': r.result.firstRunSuccess,
    'openeval.passed_runs': r.result.totalRuns,
  },
  grader_results: [{ grader_id: 'gr_vitest', type: 'code', score: r.result.passRate, passed: r.result.success }],
}
```

`ResultSet.runner` maps straight from your own `HARNESS_NAMES`/`MODEL_NAMES` tables (`runner.name` = harness, `provider.model` = the AI-Gateway model string).

## Where this is genuinely lossy (not glossing over it)

- **Per-run repetition doesn't have a first-class slot.** Each (model, eval) pair here runs 4x (`runs: 4`, `earlyExit: true`) and `export-results.ts` collapses that into `passRate`/`firstRunSuccess`/`passedRuns`/`totalRuns` on one `AgentResult`. EvalPort's `Result` is one-per-test-case-per-`ResultSet`, with no built-in "N repetitions" concept — the sketch above pushes the raw counts into `metadata.openeval.*` rather than inventing four synthetic `run_id`s, but that's a judgment call, not settled by the spec. Worth deciding explicitly rather than shipping either choice silently.
- **`earlyExit: true` censoring.** Your own code comment on `passRate` already notes it "understates per-run reliability for retried evals" — that caveat has to travel into any EvalPort metadata field that carries `pass_rate`, or a downstream reader will treat it as an unbiased rate.
- **This only covers `agent-results.json`**, not live `results/<experiment>/<timestamp>/` run directories (raw transcripts, `summary.json` fingerprints) — those stay yours; the export is a projection, not a full mirror.
- I haven't run `@vercel/agent-eval` end-to-end against this idea — this is a source-level read, not a working PR yet. If the mapping above looks reasonable I'd rather build it against your actual fixtures than guess further in prose.

## What I'm asking

Not "please merge an adapter" — more: does an `openeval` export (as an opt-in `pnpm run export-openeval` alongside the existing `export-results`, non-invasive to `agent-results.json`/`nuxt.com/evals`) seem useful to you, and if so, does the `metadata.openeval.*` placement for the repetition/censoring caveats above seem right, or would you rather see that decided differently before any code lands? Full spec: https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/evalport/blob/main/spec/SPEC.md

— Sahi, independent contributor (not affiliated with this project)

issues.title: Improve setup steps on deploying Nuxt app to AWS Amplify on docs
issues.body:
# Affected page
https://nuxt.com/deploy/aws-amplify

# Description
The documentation states that the integration of a Nuxt 3 app with AWS Amplify requires zero configuration. But that is not the case and I'll explain why.

The default build config that AWS Amplify generates is this:
```yaml
version: 1
frontend:
  phases:
    preBuild:
      commands:
        - nvm use 18
        - corepack enable
        - npx --yes nypm i
    build:
      commands:
        - yarn run build
  artifacts:
    baseDirectory: .amplify-hosting
    files:
      - '**/*'
```

However, Nuxt's build (and generate) command generates an `.output` directory that contains the app's contents ready to be served.

Hence, the `baseDirectory` property in Amplify's build config will need to be updated to `.output/public`. Hence, Nuxt's integration with AWS Amplify isn't zero config.

Happy to open a PR.

P.S: [Nitro's docs](https://nitro.unjs.io/deploy/providers/aws-amplify) might be misleading as well.
issues.author: idorenyinudoh

In regards of zero configs, the `yml` is fairly a static configuration we advise to add to allow furthor customizatiom however amplify UI should be already able to autodetect Nuxt/Nitro and configure it hence _zero_ config is required.

issues.title: PNPM Deployment to GitHub Pages
issues.body:
The current example [deployment](https://nuxt.com/deploy/github-pages) script generates warnings due to the actions using deprecated versions.

I also use `pnpm` locally, so an example of how to get started with `pnpm` as well as `npm` would be nice.

I'm not sure what the preset does in `npx nuxt build --preset github_pages` and if that's the same as the [Nitro preset](https://nitro.unjs.io/deploy/providers/github-pages)?

My own static page could be deployed using `pnpm generate` with this `deploy.yaml` script:

```yaml
# https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages#usage
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

  workflow_dispatch:

# Grant GITHUB_TOKEN the permissions required to make a Pages deployment
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write      # to deploy to Pages
  id-token: write   # to verify the deployment originates from an appropriate source

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: 9.0.x
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
      # Pick your own package manager and build script
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install
      - name: Build nuxt
        run: pnpm generate
      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./.output/public

  # Deployment job
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github_pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

I'm hesitant to update the docs with this example myself when I don't fully understand it all yet, but maybe this could be useful as a starter to someone with more knowledge then me (or future me).

I took some inspiration from the [Vitepress](https://vitepress.dev/guide/deploy#github-pages) example, which is why a couple of things have been moved or reformatted slightly.

---

Edit: remove `- run: corepack enable` as I don't think its necessary.

issues.title: Short analysis on visual clarity: Attention, Emphasis, Separation, Grouping and Unambiguity
issues.body:
Dear Nuxters,

When I look at the documentation, I often feel overwhelmed by the many options, hints, links to different sections, and the overall interconnectivity. As a trained designer, my first thought was: How can I visually enhance the readability?

I would like to share a brief analysis with you. It may open up a discussion or at least provide some stimuli for thought. I am well aware that the following is highly opinionated. I'm also aware that the Nuxt docs are derived from the Nuxt UI Pro docs template. However, since I primarily use Nuxt directly, I believe this is the appropriate place to address the following.

The focus of this analysis is on achieving clarity in design to make the layout, elements, and behaviors more understandable for users. While individual layout parts, elements, and behaviors may be clear on their own, there is room for improvement when they work together. Enhancing these interactions may improve the overall clarity of the documentation.

## (1) Attention

The docs use a 10-column grid.
However, the main section is slightly off to the right because the child element also uses a 10-column grid instead of 8.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 07 54 26](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/cd664604-8a34-4ae4-83d4-cfe6e9bab38a)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 07 54 37](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/5283172b-f2a7-4f89-a7bc-2657e778743b)

Paired with the narrow max-width, this layout leads to the blurring of boundaries between navigation, main text, and side content. While reading, your eyes often jump to the navigation, making it harder to read and maintain focus.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 08 00 45](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/c33d9bd5-601d-439d-a491-9bb4c603dca0)

One solution would be to consistently use a 10-column grid and adjust the spacing accordingly. I also added a max-w-8xl (96rem) to the wrapper and a max-w-5xl to the navigation and aside sections.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 08 10 08](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/c346c834-bacb-40e9-8636-f330f742e88c)

## (2) Emphasis

### (2.1)

Within the documentation, we have various elements that demand attention: current main navigation, current navigation, current breadcrumb, title, description, current table of contents, text links, inline code, and info boxes.

Emphasis can be very useful as it helps readers scan the text quickly or find specific information. However, every emphasis also interrupts the reader's flow. As a side note, Jan Tschichold, one of the most influential typographers for print, once said: "The addiction to highlight almost half of the words [...] makes the reader feel like they're being considered as idiots."

It's generally agreed that when highlighting elements in a text, it's best to use a single type of emphasis—whether it be bold, italic, color, background-color, underline, or border—so that no one element stands out too much or overwhelms the others.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 09 20 30](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/5d786414-99fd-448f-8380-e18c4acbfc9e)

We can easily balance the emphasis by making the following adjustments:

1. Breadcrumbs should not be green.
2. Remove letter-spacing from the introduction.
3. Use a distinguishable font size (font-xl) for the description text, keep it white, and avoid turning down the color.
4. Avoid using bold for inline code.
5. Avoid using bold for links.
6. Soften the background color of the info boxes.
7. Always place the imperative/verb at the beginning (e.g., "try out…", "read more…", "find other…") and make the entire info box a clickable link.
8. Consider giving all linked boxes a dashed border for consistency.
9. Use white and gray colors for the table of contents instead of adding color

So, we come from here
(Original)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 07 28](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/316200f5-a7de-4a59-80bd-8b40ce7aaa96)

To here
(Modified Emphasis)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 07 10](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/188dc217-1518-43c8-9330-b31082ca60c7)

To here
(With Grid adjustments)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 10 41](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/adf29167-edc3-49e4-8a6a-74131c71ce7f)

1. Start by reading the navigation.
2. Jump to the introduction block.
3. Then proceed to the main content.
4. Optionally, explore the aside section afterward.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 07 10 Kopie](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/97bddd4e-e8ec-4799-b3e0-510092f44d20)

### (2.2)

Another issue with the current emphasis strategy is that the colored boxes vie for attention and compete with the most critical part: code examples.
For instance, on the Configuration page, there's a excessive amount of information presented one after the other, with each piece of information emphasized differently.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 19 43 03](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/26132a8f-cbc8-4218-96e6-5bdaf51e3c1c)
![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 19 43 17](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/a83d5182-e1aa-4b73-b46a-1b5a7648ccea)

I believe it would be beneficial to tone down these boxes. While adjusting the background of the boxes, we could also align the color of the inline code with the color of the code examples to enhance consistency. It's reasonable to maintain the strong border color, as it serves as the primary emphasis style.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 19 48 01](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/f8ef5f54-faf8-4a67-8a72-841d18a2b464)
![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 19 48 28](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/10ff6659-b4fe-4d74-843e-c12f76910629)

## (3) Separation

Connected to the previously mentioned point about the difficulty of differentiating content due to numerous emphasis levels, it's also challenging to follow the content because there are no clear breaks for the reader to understand where one section ends and another begins.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 20 10 46](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/a102330d-767f-4dd4-ac2d-c8a69053e9cb)

Headlines could be enhanced by adding an underline and increasing the spacing, especially at the top.
This results in more completed sections.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 20 10 34](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/e8416f4f-675f-452c-af8c-056eff20d26d)

## (4) Grouping

There's often a lot to cover regarding various aspects of a particular feature, which is why info boxes are frequently used. However, similar to emphasis, the sheer volume of info boxes can be overwhelming, and it's not always clear how to follow up as a reader.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 20 01 03](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/0d243c02-08e2-409a-9391-67b3ea87d85f)

Group similar elements together: In this example, the reader can better understand that a series of "read more" blocks will follow. (Additionally, each "read more" should be a link itself; in this example, there are two inline links, and the middle info box is a link.)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 20 04 48](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/8d177633-bf20-483e-a573-a18bb805ee2c)

## (5) Unambiguity

Inline code and info boxes are sometimes links, and sometimes they're not. The visual difference lies in a dashed versus a solid border, which can be easily overlooked.

Given 3 seconds to scan the site, it's not immediately clear if "nuxt.config.ts" is clickable or if "defineNuxtConfig" is clickable, and if they are not clickable, why not?

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 23 00](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/5e979fd3-aa30-4c1d-989c-287ac139e529)

One solution would be to make links appear more like buttons rather than tags. Another option would be to use an arrow, similar to what's done with external links.

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 29 13](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/476d0eeb-bbc6-4313-b4d6-7be0d715b419)

![Bildschirmfoto 2024-06-10 um 10 32 17](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/assets/15716389/1475bdfc-7f16-4109-94ec-a28f378b8b67)

## The end

I've only picked a few examples, but I'm aware that there are likely many more cases that need careful consideration before implementing any changes. However, I'm confident that the principles of attention, emphasis, separation, grouping, and unambiguity can be applied to those other cases as well. If any of the points resonate with you, I'm happy to help

issues.title: internationalisation for nuxt.com
issues.body:
we'd love to have the nuxt.com docs available in translations for users across the world

although this has been a plan for some time, and was indeed the case in nuxt v2, we're still not there with v3 docs

Related issues: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/19926, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/21926, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions/16054, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/issues/1448 and https://github.com/nuxt/translations/discussions/4 (private repo - relevant content copied into this issue).

## Key requirements

- needs to be performant and not regress performance of the documentation
- translations need to remain always in sync, falling back to english text if required
- needs to allow community contribution

## Translation and sync automation

Documentation sources currently come from https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com, https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt and https://github.com/nuxt/examples. upstream changes need to be localisable, and trigger call for updates for translators, without blocking the documentation.

It would be nice to consider exploring LLM triggers for translation (see for example the way https://github.com/formkit uses ai in the process of building their documentation website) - at least for 'fallback' content.

👉 See https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions/29949 for a proposal

## Building a team

We've had many offers of help for translating the docs, and we'll need to build a team - but first we need to add the infrastructure to make updating translations possible.

So initially I would love for someone or a small group to take on the task of building up the automation + integration into the [nuxt/nuxt.com](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com) repository, before we move ahead to create a bigger team of translators.

The question is, what the "data flow" should look like. 

### Example:

english docs:

```md
## Hydration Strategies

Nuxt provides a range of built-in hydration strategies. Only one strategy can be used per lazy component.
```

```md
Nuxt bietet eine Reihe von Hydration Strategien. Nur eine kann kann pro Lazy-Komponente verwendet werden.

```

issues.title: Laggy search and navigation feedback
issues.body:
I've been using the new Nuxt website for a few months right now and wanted to provide some UX feedback based on my developer usage. For context I find myself using the docs multiple times a day.

1. When searching the docs the text input field gets blocked from rendering which means there is a disconnect with what you're typing and what is displayed. I don't think the search results need to be instant but what you're typing in the text input should not be blocked. For example in the recording below I am constantly typing but it's really choppy and I finished typing a full 10 seconds before my typed text is actually completely displayed.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca0dfca-5ca2-4292-9979-84cf318dba3b)

2. The animations for the menus are cool but the artificial delay trips me up multiple times a day if I'm moving "too fast". I know where I want to go but frequently find myself needing to slow down or try again to get to the menu that I want because of the delay.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7930a643-c37a-4498-922d-bc371be1f167)

_All if this feedback is in contrast to the previous website which I didn't have nearly as much friction using when navigation around and didn't feel like I was be throttled when navigating through the docs. If this was only a marketing page that would be fine but since it's also developer documentation I think it should be a bit more responsive._
issues.author: mcfarljw

comments.author: sh-at-cs
comments.body: To save time for anyone else wanting to look into this: The search [is implemented](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/blob/4767740d6b4e4886dc8601b893915d9183ec9753/app/app.vue#L91-L97) using Nuxt UI Pro's **[ContentSearch](https://ui.nuxt.com/components/content-search)** component (you can even observe the same input field lag in the examples on the linked doc page), which [isn't open source](https://github.com/nuxt/ui-pro/tree/v3/src/runtime/components/content/ContentSearch.vue), so I guess it's not even possible for the community to try and help with this... Unless the issue is actually in [CommandPalette](https://ui.nuxt.com/components/command-palette) which ContentSearch is based on, but to me it doesn't seem like that one suffers from the same issue.

comments.author: mcfarljw
comments.body:
I don't think the laggy search is an issue with the Nuxt UI component specifically but rather how it's being used on both the website in the examples. The first issue is it doesn't seem to be doing any kind of debouncing which causes it to lock up the main thread and the second issue is it's searching a very large JSON file in memory (https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/issues/1538), add those two things together and it's going to be slow.

It would be better to send a network request which searches the JSON file and returns the results async making using of the loading indicator https://ui.nuxt.com/components/command-palette#loading and also adding in like 300ms debounce.

comments.author: loilo
comments.body:
I did some profiling on the search feature, and what I found is that two things drag down performance significantly:

1. **Performing search** itself on a large amount of items.
2. The way how **entries are passed** to the command palette.

Debouncing/throttling can help with both of these problems (as @HugoRCD has already prepared in #1952), but it will only get you so far. It still improves the situation drastically (profiled INP goes down from 11.9s to 3.5s), but as you can see, a 3'500ms INP is not the experience you might want to shoot for.

I've dabbled around with solutions to both of these problems, and I locally brought the INP down to 500ms (still not great, but at least another leap in the right direction). Unfortunately though, I cannot make a PR with my changes since not all of this is directly in the hands of the nuxt.com repo.

**1. Performing Search**

Using a web worker for search instead of running it on the UI thread does a lot of good, but the search business logic is part of the [`CommandPalette`](https://ui.nuxt.com/components/command-palette) component, so that component would have to be adjusted.

I can see a world where (the option to) using a worker would benefit many Nuxt UI users, but I'm not sure whether the disproportionate scale of nuxt.com search would justify adding the additional complexity in Nuxt UI for everyone.

(Ideally, the worker approach would be provided as an improvement in VueUse's [`useFuse`](https://vueuse.org/integrations/usefuse/) composable directly. But to be honest, I don't see this happen — workers, in particular worker URLs, are a pain to get right and almost impossible to offer in libraries.)

**2. Passing Entries**

[The "Ask AI" entry](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.com/blob/6e65a048c2ff8170aa423d4a4175b13eb02835ba/app/composables/useNavigation.ts#L276-L284) currently really drags down performance, because it echoes the current search term. This establishes a dependency of the searchable entries on the search term, meaning that a new list of entries is passed to Nuxt UI Pro's `ContentSearch` component (and thus to the `CommandPalette`) _on every keystroke_.
While only the "Ask AI" entry actually changes in that list, the `ContentSearch` component still has to perform the ceremony of processing _all_ the entries to prepare them for search (the `mapNavigationItems()` function being run a lot was particularly prominent in the profiler).

So, unless there would be a significant redesign of how the Ask AI feature is presented in search (or how semi-permanent items are embedded in the `CommandPalette` in general), I don't see a quick way to fix this without really downgrading the Ask AI feature.

Just my 2 cents & hints for future improvements.

comments.author: HugoRCD
comments.body: @loilo Thank you very much for doing this, it's hyper relevant and will help me a little more to move forward in the optimization I think there is clearly work that could be done on the "Ask AI" function by doing something more "native" with Nuxt UI's [ChatPalette](https://ui.nuxt.com/components/chat-palette) and Vercel's aiSDK 🤔

issues.title: [Proposal] Unified Nuxt Documentation Experience
issues.body: ## Motivation Nuxt leverage the unjs ecosystem for core parts of the framework, mainly Nitro, H3 and oftech. While the UnJS ecosystem can be used stand-alone, the majority of its users comes from Nuxt. Yet, the experience while looking for information about Nuxt in general is often disjointed, due to Nuxt.com and Nitro being separated website, and h3/ofetch currently not having dedicated websites https://github.com/unjs/h3/issues/418 This makes it hard to reason about Nuxt for newcomers, when they will look for how to do something in the docs, won't find it, then have to navigate to the Nitro website, or the github READMEs for H3 or oftech, or googling / finding information in articles. With separated websites, the information is not searchable and accessible easily. We could have a single algolia index that search throughout Nuxt/Nitro/H3. It's something that cloudflare does well, the search bar can jump from one product to the other seamlessly. ## Proposal ### For Nuxt Integrate H3, Nitro and ofetch in the nuxt.com website, such so that we have - https://nuxt.com/docs/nitro/ - https://nuxt.com/docs/h3/ - https://nuxt.com/docs/$fetch/ and one search bar that can be used to reference the content of all 3. This would remove the duplicated content accross Nuxt and these website, are they would use the *same* source. ### For Nitro, H3 and ofetch Since these tools are meant to be used either standalone or with Nuxt, we could have a nuxt version for them. This can be implemented with a NuxtOnly and a StandAlone component that we can use to wrap docs paragraph or code examples. Using Nitro as an example, this would serve multiple purposes : - Documentation for Nitro and Nuxt would share the same source of truth - Nitro would still have a standalone website that would be identical to what it is today - Nitro would feel more integrated under the Nuxt umbrella as its docs would be accessible without navigating to an external page. Wether they're the same Nuxt app, or there's is one website for each subdocs is an implementation detail. Additionally, the Nitro website could use a toggle like the vue composition/options api switcher : This toggle would enable nuxt or standalone instructions. It would be hidden inhttps://nuxt.com/docs/nitro/ which would default to Nuxt, and would be either hidden or visible in https://nitro.unjs.io/ which would default to standalone. ## Extra toughts There are also additional libraries that are used by Nuxt such as vue, vite, vue-router, but this doesn't affect the experience as bad as Nitro/h3. However a similar system can be adopted for unjs libraries that are end-user facing and auto-imported. Where this makes sense. Perhaps Unstorage/db0 as they come with Nitro/Nuxt. ### Additional information - [X] Would you be willing to help implement this feature? - [ ] Could this feature be implemented as a module? ### Final checks - [X] Read the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution). - [X] Check existing [discussions](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/discussions) and [issues](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues).

issues.title: Add a Docker deployment guide to /deploy
issues.body:
### Describe the feature

[`/deploy`](https://nuxt.com/deploy) documents 23 hosting providers, but there is no page on running Nuxt in a container, and [`/docs/getting-started/deployment`](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/deployment) never mentions Docker either — it covers the Node.js server preset, static hosting, serverless/edge, PM2 and cluster mode, but the words "Docker" and "container" do not appear in it.

That is a noticeable gap, because a container image is the default deployment unit for anyone self-hosting on a VPS, Kubernetes, Fly.io, Railway, Coolify, Dokploy, ECS or Cloud Run — and several providers already listed under `/deploy` are consumed through an image anyway.

This repository already assumes people ask the question. `test/mcp.eval.ts` contains:

```ts
{ input: 'What deployment providers support Docker containerization?', expected: [{ toolName: 'list_deploy_providers' }] }
```

`list_deploy_providers` currently has nothing Docker-related to return.

### Why it matters

Without a canonical page, people copy Dockerfiles from blog posts and the same mistakes keep recurring:

- copying the host `node_modules` into the image because there is no `.dockerignore`
- shipping the whole source tree to production instead of the standalone `.output` directory
- not knowing `.output` needs nothing but a Node.js runtime, so no multi-stage build
- confusing build-time values (baked into the image) with `runtimeConfig` values (`NUXT_*`, read at container start), which leads to secrets in image layers
- missing `NITRO_PORT` / `NITRO_HOST` when the platform assigns a port

None of that is hard, but it is currently undocumented and each of the 23 provider pages assumes a managed build instead.

### Proposal

Add `content/deploy/docker.md` covering:

- a multi-stage Dockerfile per package manager, copying only `.output` into a clean runtime stage
- a `.dockerignore`
- build and run commands
- the runtime environment variables, and the build-time vs runtime distinction
- a Docker Compose example
- a static variant (`nuxt generate` served by nginx), including the `200.html` / `404.html` fallback caveat

One small code change comes with it: `dockerfile` is not part of `content.build.markdown.highlight.langs` in `nuxt.config.ts`, so Dockerfile code fences currently render as plain text. `@nuxt/content` maps each entry of that array to `import('@shikijs/langs/<entry>')` and keys the result by the entry string verbatim, without expanding aliases, then looks the fence language up in that map — so the entry has to match the fence label exactly. Listing `docker` is not enough for a ` ```dockerfile ` fence; `dockerfile` is itself a valid `@shikijs/langs` subpath that re-exports the `docker` grammar, and that is the entry to add.

### Additional information

- [x] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?

issues.title: fix(modules): debounce search input to avoid a payload request per keystroke
issues.body:
## Description

Typing in the modules search on https://nuxt.com/modules updates the route on every keystroke. `/modules` is an ISR route, so each character fetches a new page payload (`/modules/_payload.json?q=...`) even though the module list is already in memory and filtered on the client.

This was fixed in nuxt/modules#477 (closes nuxt/modules#467) in 2022. The modules UI now lives in this repo and the search input no longer debounces.

## Reproduction

1. Open https://nuxt.com/modules
2. Open the network panel and filter by `_payload.json`
3. Type `eslint` one character at a time
4. One `GET /modules/_payload.json?q=<prefix>` fires per keystroke (6 requests for 6 characters), all 200

## Where

`app/pages/modules/index.vue` binds the input to `route.query.q` and calls `replaceRoute` on every `update:model-value` (`app/composables/useFilters.ts`). `q` is a computed from the route in `app/composables/useModules.ts`.

comments.author: TheAlexLichter
comments.body:
Great points :+1: 

Having a dedicated utility repo/package for modules is definitely a must-have and will make module development even easier.

My thoughts:

## Class vs. Function

I'd stick to the create function (personal preference). Would vote against having both approaches/ways built-in because it'll "split" the module developers and doesn't add any real value. But concerning this, it'd make sense to talk to the module maintainers as well so we all can decide on one way to do it.

## Package name

`@nuxt/module-utilities` sounds pretty good to me. `@nuxt/modules` is too brief IMO and `@nuxt/sdk` sounds more like a developer tool for the core to me.

## Place of the module

Probably an own dedicated repo (maybe even under the `nuxt` namespace?).

## Old ModuleContainer code

We can't remove it for now as it'd be a breaking change, but for 3.X I'd do that.
People should start transitioning as soon as it's out so we can remove the code. A "bridge" for older modules might be an idea worth to pursue as well.

## Question of Scope

The utilities are 'only' for modules (not for replacing, say @nuxt/webpack with an own implementation of @nuxt/parcel), or should they cover that as well?

## Misc

> Actually, module authors can use this.nuxt.hook guard to lazy require and only configure webpack options when we are building project but in reality, no-one did this (Maybe because it was hard?) 

Likely because it wasn't written down anywhere / suggested to do so :man_shrugging: 
We need a more detailed modules guide as well.

comments.body:
Nice idea about config overriding/preset @wagerfield. But config handling is out of module scope. The order of a nuxt project bootstrap is:

1.CLI > 2.Read Config > 3.Normalize Options > 4.Run Modules > 5.Ready (Including Listen, ...)

All current modules _assume_ that shape of `this.options` is already normalized with applied defaults. As module entry point function is exactly **one**, the only possible way would be swapping 3 with 4 which is not only a breaking change but makes modules unstable depending on user input.

I suggest moving this enhancement to #16 (Improve Config) by allowing **presets** in `nuxt.config`:

```js
{
  presets: [
     'nework',
     '@company/defaults'
  ]
}
```

Presets can have an interface just like `modules` a function like you described above.

PS: As described in original RFC I suggest keeping `ModuleContainer` frozen and instead introduce module utils package.
